\subsection{The refinement}

\begin{theorem}[Countable-input nonconservativity]\label{swo:gcz:thm:main}
Let \(\mathsf T\) be either \(\ZC\) or \(\ZC_{\mathrm F}\). Add a
total unary operation \(c\), allow Separation to mention it, and require only
\[
 \forall X\,[X\ne\varnothing\ \wedge\ X\injto\omega
                       \ \longrightarrow\ c(X)\in X].
\]
This extension is not conservative over \(\mathsf T\) for sentences of the
original language \(\{\in\}\). In particular, it proves the negation of the
appropriate Glazer obstruction sentence \(\Theta\), while
\(\mathsf T\) does not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Assume \(\Theta\) in the expanded theory. Apply \cref{swo:gcz:thm:uniform} with
\(D=\omega\) to obtain, uniformly in \(n\), injections
\(u_n:X_n\injto\omega\). The countable rows and incidence data supplied by
\(\Theta\) satisfy \cref{swo:gcz:thm:compression}. Thus
\[
 T\injto\Pow(\omega\times\omega).
\]
The standard pairing bijection \(\omega\times\omega\longleftrightarrow\omega\)
induces a bijection of their power sets. We obtain
\(T\injto\Pow(\omega)\), contradicting \(\Theta\).

The base theory has a model satisfying \(\Theta\) by the cited countermodel
theorem, so it cannot prove \(\neg\Theta\). No step of the additional
uniformization or compression argument used Foundation; applying the relevant
version of the input proves both cases.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Metatheory]\label{swo:gcz:n5.2}
The positive implication \(\Theta\to\bot\) is a derivation in the
specified expanded weak theory. The nonderivability statement uses the
published countermodel result. Glazer states that his model-construction
theorems are established in \(\ZF\); our refinement inherits that input.
This is not an assertion that \(\ZC\) proves its own consistency.
Readers preferring conditional consistency language may assume
\(\operatorname{Con}(\ZF)\); no claim of an optimal metatheoretic bound is
needed here.
\end{remark}

\merge\ (4 October 2026, batch~90.) Glazer's Oberwolfach abstract \emph{A
hypertalk} (Oberwolfach Reports 22 (2025), Report No.~2/2025, pp.~106--107)
reports a parallel phenomenon without Foundation: the classification of
connected one-dimensional manifolds, not necessarily second countable or
set-sized, is not a theorem of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ without Foundation but becomes
provable when Global Choice is added. He asks whether
$\mathsf{ZFC}-\mathsf{Fnd}+\mathsf{GC}$ proves that every topological manifold
is a set. Part~XII of \path{polish-models-of-omnific-arithmetic} (its
source~18, batch-90 manuscript~03; AI-assisted, unrefereed, not formalized)
prints that question for connected Hausdorff real class manifolds of
dimension at least two (its Question~165.6, \code{pma:gcm:q:glazer}), and
proves, without Global Choice, that a connected real class manifold is a set
when its carrier has an ordinal exhaustion, a compatible real class metric, or
a class injection into or surjection from some $\No^m$; the question itself
stays open. Neither that part nor source~31 uses the other's theorems.

\begin{corollary}[A single infinite input cardinality suffices]\label{swo:gcz:cor:exactomega}
The nonconservativity conclusion remains true if the selector is required to
choose only from sets in bijection with \(\omega\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(c_\infty\) select from countably infinite sets. If
\(\varnothing\ne X\injto\omega\), then \(X\times\omega\) is countably
infinite. Indeed, it injects into \(\omega\times\omega\), and after fixing
one element of \(X\), it contains a copy of \(\omega\). The ordinary
set Cantor--Bernstein theorem, provable by the bounded finite-path construction,
gives the bijection. Define
\[
 c(X)=\pi_1\bigl(c_\infty(X\times\omega)\bigr)
\]
for these inputs, and \(c(X)=\varnothing\) otherwise. This is a countable-set
selector. Separation for it translates into Separation for \(c_\infty\), so
\cref{swo:gcz:thm:main} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Any fixed infinite bound]\label{swo:gcz:n5.4}
Suppose a fixed well-ordered \(D\) contains a set copy of \(\omega\). A
selector on all nonempty sets embeddable into \(D\), with expanded Separation,
already implies the countable-input conclusion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Every countable set embeds into \(D\). Restrict the selector's specified
behavior to those inputs and apply \cref{swo:gcz:thm:main}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The exact role of expanded Separation}

\begin{proposition}[An uninteracting selector is conservative]\label{swo:gcz:prop:nosep}
If the Separation schema is \emph{not} extended to the new symbol, adjoining
the selector requirement alone is conservative over \(\ZC\), and likewise
over \(\ZC_{\mathrm F}\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Use the ordinary external \(\ZFC\) metatheory for this model-theoretic
argument. Every set-sized model \(M\) of the base theory can be expanded by
selecting an \(\in^M\)-member of each internally nonempty set. External
Choice makes these selections on the external set \(M\). The resulting
operation satisfies even unrestricted global selection in the expanded
structure. All original axioms still hold because their schemas do not mention
the new operation. Thus every base model has an expansion, and completeness
gives conservativity for original-language sentences.
\end{proof}

Expanded Separation is therefore part of the mathematical content of
\cref{swo:gcz:thm:main}. Merely writing a choice operation into a formal language is
not the same assertion.

\section{Full-class rank models and the sign carrier}\label{swo:gcz:sec:ranksetup}

From this section onward, work in an external universe satisfying \(\ZFC\).
Fix a limit ordinal \(\lambda>\omega\). The set sort of \(\RM_\lambda\)
is \(V_\lambda\), and its class sort consists of every external subset of
\(V_\lambda\). Ordered pairs and finite tuples are encoded in the usual way.
Since \(\lambda\) is a limit, any finite rank increase remains below
\(\lambda\); hence every relation or function on this domain can be
represented by a class of coded tuples.

\begin{proposition}[Available axioms]\label{swo:gcz:prop:rankbase}
\(\RM_\lambda\) satisfies \(\ZC_{\mathrm F}\) on its set sort, elementary
class comprehension, Separation with arbitrary class parameters, and global
choice. Its internal ordinals are precisely the ordinals below \(\lambda\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Transitivity and limit height give Extensionality, Pairing, Union, Power Set,
Infinity, and Foundation. Every external subset of a set \(a\in V_\lambda\)
again belongs to \(V_\lambda\), proving Separation even with arbitrary class
parameters. External Choice gives a choice function on a set-sized family
\(a\); its graph has rank bounded by the ranks of \(a\) and its union,
plus a finite amount, so belongs to \(V_\lambda\). Thus internal set Choice
holds.

Every extension of a formula on the domain is an admitted class, giving class
comprehension. External Choice also selects one member of every nonempty
element of the external set \(V_\lambda\); its graph is an admitted class
and witnesses global choice. Transitivity and the actual well-foundedness of
membership identify the internal ordinals with \(\lambda\).
\end{proof}

\subsection{Sign sequences and bounded birthdays}

Each binary function on an ordinal \(\alpha<\lambda\) has rank between
\(\alpha\) and \(\max(\omega,\alpha)+m\) for an absolute finite coding
constant \(m\), after harmless adjustment for finite \(\alpha\). It therefore
belongs to \(V_\lambda\). Conversely, the domain of any internally represented
ordinal-length binary function is an ordinal below \(\lambda\). The internal
sign-sequence class is exactly \(S_\lambda\).

The following boundedness criterion will be used repeatedly:
\[\tag{S31.6}\label{swo:gcz:eq:boundedbirthday}
 B\subseteq S_\lambda\text{ is an internal set}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sup\{\bd(s):s\in B\}<\lambda.
\]
For the reverse implication, uniformly bounded lengths give a fixed rank bound
on all the coded functions and on their collection. For the forward implication,
the rank of the internal set bounds the ranks, and therefore the lengths, of its
members. In particular, \(S_\lambda\) is an internal proper class.

This identification is about the sign presentation and its birthday filtration.
For example, at a noncardinal cutoff, operations on two sign sequences may
produce a sequence whose length reaches the cutoff. Accordingly, no theorem
below treats every \(S_\lambda\) as a real-closed field or as a model of all
surreal arithmetic.

\subsection{Set-like well-orders at every height}

\begin{proposition}[Choice orders without ordinal enumeration]\label{swo:gcz:prop:allwo}
For every limit \(\lambda>\omega\), \(V_\lambda\) has a rank-monotone
set-like class well-order, and \(S_\lambda\) has a birthday-monotone set-like
class well-order. These orders give a least element to every nonempty admitted
class, not only to every internal nonempty set.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Externally choose a well-order of each rank layer of \(V_\lambda\), and
order first by rank, then by the selected layer order. Every nonempty subclass
has a least occurring rank and then a least element on that layer. The
predecessors of a given point are contained in a fixed rank segment, so form
an internal set. The construction for \(S_\lambda\) is identical, with
birthday layers \({}^\alpha2\). Its predecessors have bounded birthday,
and equation~\eqref{swo:gcz:eq:boundedbirthday} applies.
\end{proof}

One must not infer that either of these orders has type \(\Ord^{\RM_\lambda}\).
Such an inference requires both the availability of ordinal representatives for
predecessor orders and a justification that the resulting enumeration has the
appropriate range. We determine exactly when the corresponding statements hold.

\merge\ At a strongly inaccessible $\kappa$, $\RM_\kappa$ is source~12's model
$\mathcal M$ of \cref{swo:st:sec:model}, and the identification of the internal
sign-sequence class with $S_\kappa=\No_{<\kappa}$ is clause~(i) of
\cref{swo:st:thm:model}; source~09's universe enlargement
(\cref{swo:ec:sec:universe}) and the universe sections of Part~IX
(\cref{swo:ix:sec:universes}) also work at an inaccessible height. This section
and the next five drop inaccessibility. \Cref{swo:gcz:prop:allwo} gives a
set-like class well-order of $S_\lambda$ at every height, which by
\cref{swo:gcz:thm:bare} need not have type $\Ord$; over $\GB$, which has class
Replacement, the two are equivalent (\cref{swo:cf:choice} and the dated note
after it).

\section{Ordinal enumeration and birthday order}\label{swo:gcz:sec:signspectra}

For an infinite cardinal \(\kappa\), write
\[
 2^{<\kappa}=\sup_{\mu<\kappa,\,\mu\text{ a cardinal}}2^\mu.
\]
Our use of cardinal equalities in this and the following sections is entirely
external.

\begin{lemma}[Size of the sign carrier]\label{swo:gcz:lem:signcard}
Let \(\lambda>\omega\) be a limit ordinal and \(\kappa=|\lambda|\).
Then
\[\tag{S31.7}\label{swo:gcz:eq:signcard}
 |S_\lambda|=
 \begin{cases}
  2^{<\kappa},&\lambda=\kappa,\\
  2^\kappa,&\kappa<\lambda.
 \end{cases}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The layers have size \(2^{|\alpha|}\), and distinct layers are disjoint.
For \(\lambda=\kappa\), their cardinal sum is
\(\kappa\cdot 2^{<\kappa}=2^{<\kappa}\). Here
\(2^{<\kappa}\ge\kappa\): at a successor cardinal this follows from
Cantor's theorem at the predecessor cardinal; at a limit cardinal it follows
by taking the supremum of the successor cardinals below it.

If \(\kappa<\lambda\), the birthday \(\kappa\) layer is present and has
size \(2^\kappa\). Every layer has at most this size, and there are
\(\kappa\) layers, giving the matching upper bound.
\end{proof}

\merge\ The case $\lambda=\kappa$ is the count
$\card{\No_{<\kappa}}=2^{<\kappa}$ of \cref{swo:sw:cutoffs} (before
\cref{swo:sw:cutoffspectrum}), proved there by the same sum.

\begin{theorem}[Bare ordinal enumeration]\label{swo:gcz:thm:bare}
There is an admitted class bijection
\(\Ord^{\RM_\lambda}\longleftrightarrow S_\lambda\) if and only if
\(\lambda\) is a cardinal \(\kappa\) satisfying \(2^{<\kappa}=\kappa\).
The same condition characterizes a class injection
\(S_\lambda\injto\Ord^{\RM_\lambda}\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All external functions on the relevant carriers are admitted class functions.
The assertion is therefore cardinal equality with \(|\lambda|\), or the
corresponding cardinal inequality. At a noninitial \(\lambda\),
\cref{swo:gcz:lem:signcard} and Cantor's theorem rule it out. At an initial
\(\kappa\), the same lemma gives exactly the displayed condition. An
injection of \(\lambda\) into \(S_\lambda\) is always available by taking
the all-zero sequence at each birthday, so injection and bijection have the
same threshold.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}\label{swo:gcz:n7.3}
An \emph{ordinal birthday enumeration} is a class bijection
\(e:\lambda\to S_\lambda\) satisfying
\(\xi<\eta\Rightarrow\bd(e(\xi))\le\bd(e(\eta))\).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Birthday enumeration threshold]\label{swo:gcz:thm:birthday}
An ordinal birthday enumeration exists if and only if \(\lambda\) is a
strong-limit cardinal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Such an enumeration is in particular a bare enumeration, so
\cref{swo:gcz:thm:bare} implies \(\lambda=\kappa\) is a cardinal. Fix
\(\alpha<\kappa\) and choose a sign sequence of birthday \(\alpha+1\).
It occurs at some position \(\xi<\kappa\). Monotonicity places every
sequence of birthday \(\alpha\) before that position. Hence
\[
 2^{|\alpha|}\le |\xi|<\kappa.
\]
Thus \(\kappa\) is strong limit.

Conversely, suppose \(\kappa\) is strong limit. For each
\(\alpha<\kappa\), externally well-order \({}^\alpha2\) in its initial
cardinal order type \(\theta_\alpha=2^{|\alpha|}<\kappa\). Concatenate
these orders in increasing birthday. For every \(\beta<\kappa\), the
ordinal sum of the layers up through \(\beta\) has cardinal at most
\[
 \max\bigl(\aleph_0,|\beta|,2^{|\beta|}\bigr)<\kappa.
\]
As \(\kappa\) is an initial ordinal, each such partial sum is below
\(\kappa\). Their supremum is therefore at most \(\kappa\). It is at
least \(\kappa\), since there is a nonempty layer for every birthday.
The concatenated order has type exactly \(\kappa\), giving the required
enumeration. No regularity of \(\kappa\) was used.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{swo:gcz:n7.5}
A birthday-monotone \emph{set-like well-order} exists at every limit height by
\cref{swo:gcz:prop:allwo}; the extra demand in \cref{swo:gcz:thm:birthday} is that its order
type be the internal \(\Ord\). The difference is visible even at
\(\omega_1\) under CH, as shown in \cref{swo:gcz:sec:examples}.
\end{remark}

\section{Universal set coding and ordinal abstraction}\label{swo:gcz:sec:beth}

Recall the external beth hierarchy:
\[
 \beth_0=\aleph_0,\qquad
 \beth_{\alpha+1}=2^{\beth_\alpha},\qquad
 \beth_\delta=\sup_{\alpha<\delta}\beth_\alpha\quad(\delta\text{ limit}).
\]
For an uncountable initial cardinal \(\kappa\),
\[\tag{S31.8}\label{swo:gcz:eq:Vbeth}
 |V_\kappa|=\beth_\kappa.
\]
Indeed, \(|V_{\omega+\alpha}|=\beth_\alpha\) by induction, and
\(\omega+\kappa=\kappa\). In particular, one must not substitute this
formula without adjustment at \(\lambda=\omega+\omega\), where the
cardinality is \(\beth_\omega\).

\begin{lemma}[Growth facts]\label{swo:gcz:lem:growth}
For an uncountable cardinal \(\kappa\), \(\beth_\kappa\ge\kappa\),
and \(\beth_\kappa\) is a strong-limit cardinal. If
\(\beth_\kappa=\kappa\), then
\(|V_\alpha|<\kappa\) for every \(\alpha<\kappa\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The beth sequence is strictly increasing and continuous. At the limit index
\(\kappa\) its supremum has cardinal at least \(\kappa\). If
\(\mu<\beth_\kappa\), some \(\beth_\beta\) exceeds \(\mu\), with
\(\beta+1<\kappa\); hence
\(2^\mu\le\beth_{\beta+1}<\beth_\kappa\). This proves the strong-limit
assertion. In the fixed-point case, the rank-cardinality formula, or its
monotone upper bounds for small ranks, puts every \(|V_\alpha|\) below
\(\beth_\kappa=\kappa\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Universal coding threshold]\label{swo:gcz:thm:universal}
For a limit ordinal \(\lambda>\omega\), the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item there is a class injection \(V_\lambda\injto S_\lambda\);
\item there is a class bijection \(V_\lambda\longleftrightarrow S_\lambda\);
\item there is a class bijection \(V_\lambda\longleftrightarrow\lambda\);
\item \(\lambda=\kappa=\beth_\kappa\).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
All the functions in question are external functions between sets, represented
internally as classes. Because \(S_\lambda\subseteq V_\lambda\), (i)
and (ii) are equivalent by external Cantor--Bernstein.

First suppose \(\lambda\) is not an initial ordinal, and put
\(\kappa=|\lambda|<\lambda\). If \(\kappa=\omega\), then
\(\lambda\ge\omega+\omega\), so
\[
 |V_\lambda|\ge\beth_\omega>2^\omega=|S_\lambda|.
\]
If \(\kappa>\omega\), then \(\kappa+2<\lambda\), because
\(\lambda\) is a limit. By equation~\eqref{swo:gcz:eq:Vbeth},
\[
 |V_\lambda|\ge|V_{\kappa+2}|
       =2^{\,2^{\beth_\kappa}}>2^\kappa=|S_\lambda|.
\]
Thus neither (i) nor (iii) can hold at a noninitial height.

Now let \(\lambda=\kappa\). If \(\beth_\kappa>\kappa\), the
strong-limit property in \cref{swo:gcz:lem:growth} gives
\[
 |S_\kappa|=2^{<\kappa}\le2^\kappa<\beth_\kappa=|V_\kappa|.
\]
Both (i) and (iii) fail. If \(\beth_\kappa=\kappa\), then \(\kappa\)
is strong limit, so \(|S_\kappa|=\kappa=|V_\kappa|\). All three
coding statements hold.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Ordinal abstraction]\label{swo:gcz:n8.3}
\(\OA\) asserts that every internal set well-order is isomorphic, by an
internal set graph, to an internal von Neumann ordinal.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Ordinal abstraction threshold]\label{swo:gcz:thm:OA}
\(\RM_\lambda\models\OA\) if and only if
\(\lambda=\kappa=\beth_\kappa\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Assume first that \(\lambda=\kappa=\beth_\kappa\). Every internal set
\(a\) has size below \(\kappa\), by \cref{swo:gcz:lem:growth}. An internal
well-order on \(a\) is externally a genuine well-order: every external
subset of \(a\) is internal. Let its external order type be \(\alpha\).
Since \(|\alpha|=|a|<\kappa\) and \(\kappa\) is initial,
\(\alpha<\kappa\). Its isomorphism graph has bounded rank and belongs
to \(V_\kappa\). Thus the collapse is internal.

Conversely, suppose first that \(\lambda\) is not initial. The ordinal
\(\kappa=|\lambda|\) belongs to \(V_\lambda\). Transport the order
\(\lambda\) to the carrier \(\kappa\) by an external bijection. The
resulting relation is a subset of \(\kappa\times\kappa\), so has rank
below \(\lambda\). It is an internal well-order of external type
\(\lambda\), which has no internal ordinal representative. This refutes
\(\OA\).

Finally, let \(\lambda=\kappa\) and suppose
\(\beth_\kappa>\kappa\). Continuity of the beth hierarchy gives some
\(\beta<\kappa\) with \(\beth_\beta>\kappa\); otherwise its supremum
would be at most \(\kappa\). A rank segment below \(\kappa\) therefore
contains an internal set of size at least \(\kappa\). Choose an external
subset \(a\) of that set of size \(\kappa\), and transport the order
\(\kappa\) to \(a\). Both \(a\) and the relation are internal by rank
boundedness. This well-order has type \(\kappa\), again with no internal
ordinal representative.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Why this does not prove Replacement}

At a singular beth fixed point, every internal set well-order has an ordinal
type and the entire set universe has a class bijection with \(\Ord\).
Nevertheless, a class function on a small ordinal can have unbounded-rank
values. An external class bijection does not imply that the images of all of
its set-sized domain restrictions are internal sets. The next section makes
this obstruction exact.

\section{The exact domain size for Class Replacement}\label{swo:gcz:sec:replacement}

\begin{definition}\label{swo:gcz:n9.1}
For an internal set \(a\), let \(\CR(a)\) assert that the range of every
admitted class function \(F:a\to V_\lambda\) is an internal set. Let
\(\CR(\Ord)\) assert \(\CR(\alpha)\) for every internal ordinal
\(\alpha\). Full \(\CR\) asserts \(\CR(a)\) for every internal set.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The domain-size criterion]\label{swo:gcz:lem:domain}
For every \(a\in V_\lambda\),
\[\tag{S31.9}\label{swo:gcz:eq:domain}
 \RM_\lambda\models\CR(a)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |a|<\cf(\lambda).
\]
The same condition characterizes full-class Collection on the domain \(a\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If \(|a|<\cf(\lambda)\), the ranks of the values of any function
\(F:a\to V_\lambda\) form an externally bounded subset of \(\lambda\).
Its range therefore has rank below \(\lambda\), so is internal.

If \(|a|\ge\cf(\lambda)\), choose externally a surjection
\(p:a\to\cf(\lambda)\) and a cofinal map
\(g:\cf(\lambda)\to\lambda\). The admitted class function
\(g\circ p\) has an unbounded set of ordinal values. That range is not
an internal set, refuting \(\CR(a)\).

For Collection, a total class relation on \(a\) has an external witness
selection by ambient Choice. When \(|a|<\cf(\lambda)\), these selected
witnesses have bounded rank and give a collecting set. In the other direction,
the functional relation just constructed has unique witnesses and no internal
collecting set.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Replacement thresholds]\label{swo:gcz:thm:replacement}
For every limit ordinal \(\lambda>\omega\),
\begin{align*}
 \RM_\lambda\models\CR(\omega)
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\cf(\lambda)>\omega,\\
 \RM_\lambda\models\CR(\Ord)
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
        \lambda\text{ is an uncountable regular cardinal},\\
 \RM_\lambda\models\CR
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
        \lambda\text{ is strongly inaccessible}.
\end{align*}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is \cref{swo:gcz:lem:domain} with \(a=\omega\).

For the second, if \(\lambda\) is regular initial, every
\(\alpha<\lambda\) has size below \(\cf(\lambda)=\lambda\).
Conversely, if \(\cf(\lambda)<\lambda\), then
\(\cf(\lambda)\) is itself an internal ordinal and its domain violates
\cref{swo:gcz:lem:domain}. The only remaining possibility is
\(\cf(\lambda)=\lambda\), which says that \(\lambda\) is an initial
regular cardinal.

For full Replacement, the second assertion first forces regular cardinal
height. If that regular cardinal \(\kappa\) is not strong limit, choose
an infinite cardinal \(\mu<\kappa\) with \(2^\mu\ge\kappa\).
The internal set \(\Pow(\mu)\) has size at least
\(\cf(\kappa)=\kappa\), so violates \cref{swo:gcz:lem:domain}. Conversely,
at a strongly inaccessible \(\kappa\), induction on
\(\alpha<\kappa\) gives \(|V_\alpha|<\kappa\): the successor step
uses strong limit and the limit step uses regularity. Every internal set has
size below \(\cf(\kappa)\), and \cref{swo:gcz:lem:domain} proves full Class
Replacement.
\end{proof}

\merge\ The inaccessible case of the third equivalence is the classical fact
that source~12's model uses (``regularity and the strong-limit property ensure
the required closure of set operations and class Replacement'',
\cref{swo:st:sec:model}). The first equivalence makes exact that section's
warning that $V_{\beth_\omega}$ ``lacks the regularity used in Replacement'':
there $\cf\lambda=\omega$, so Class Replacement fails already on the domain
$\omega$ (\cref{swo:gcz:sec:examples}).

\begin{corollary}[Separating the two requirements]\label{swo:gcz:cor:decompose}
Within the structures \(\RM_\lambda\), the conjunction of ordinal-domain
Class Replacement and ordinal birthday enumeration is equivalent to full
Class Replacement. The same is true with ordinal birthday enumeration replaced
by ordinal abstraction or universal set coding.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first conjunction says exactly that the height is regular and strong limit.
For the second, a beth fixed point is strong limit, and regularity again gives
strong inaccessibility. Every inaccessible cardinal is a beth fixed point:
induction gives \(\beth_\alpha<\kappa\) for \(\alpha<\kappa\), and
continuity gives \(\beth_\kappa=\kappa\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Ordinal domains are not all well-orderable domains]\label{swo:gcz:n9.5}
The distinction in \cref{swo:gcz:thm:replacement} concerns \emph{ordinal domains}.
It must not be confused with Replacement on every well-orderable set.
Freire and Hamkins prove that the latter implies full Replacement over
Zermelo set theory with Foundation, without assuming Choice
\cite{gczFreireHamkins}. An internal well-ordered carrier may have no internal
ordinal representative, precisely as \cref{swo:gcz:thm:OA} shows.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Full classes versus definable classes]\label{swo:gcz:n9.6}
The inaccessible threshold characterizes Replacement for \emph{all external
class functions} admitted in \(\RM_\lambda\). It is not a classification
of heights satisfying the first-order Replacement schema for formulas of the
pure membership language. Such heights are usually discussed through worldly
rank segments; the class parameter restriction changes the problem. No result
about first-order Replacement at all singular heights is asserted here.
\end{remark}

\section{The sizes of internal proper classes}\label{swo:gcz:sec:classsizes}

The available classes form an external set, but many are proper classes relative
to the internal set sort. This distinction is useful rather than paradoxical.

\begin{theorem}[Proper-class cardinal spectrum]\label{swo:gcz:thm:classsizes}
A class \(C\subseteq V_\lambda\) is an internal proper class exactly when
it is unbounded in rank. Its possible external cardinalities are precisely
\[\tag{S31.10}\label{swo:gcz:eq:classsizes}
\{\theta:\theta\text{ is a cardinal and }
              \cf(\lambda)\le\theta\le|V_\lambda|\}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A rank-bounded subclass is an external subset of some \(V_\alpha\) and
therefore belongs to \(V_\lambda\). Conversely, an element of
\(V_\lambda\) bounds the ranks of all of its members. An unbounded subclass
must have at least \(\cf(\lambda)\) elements. A cofinal sequence of
ordinals below \(\lambda\) realizes that lower bound.

For any cardinal \(\theta\) in the displayed interval, choose an external
subset \(B\subseteq V_\lambda\) of size \(\theta\), and adjoin a fixed
cofinal set of ordinals of size \(\cf(\lambda)\). The union is
rank-unbounded and still has size \(\theta\). It is an admitted proper
class of the required cardinality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two different limitation-of-size conditions]\label{swo:gcz:cor:limitation}
In \(\RM_\lambda\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item every proper class admits an injection from \(\Ord\) if and only if
      \(\cf(\lambda)=|\lambda|\);
\item every proper class is class-bijective with \(\Ord\) if and only if
      \(\lambda\) is strongly inaccessible.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For (i), compare the least possible size \(\cf(\lambda)\) with
\(|\Ord^{\RM_\lambda}|=|\lambda|\). For (ii), the universal class
itself first forces \(|V_\lambda|=|\lambda|\), which by
\cref{swo:gcz:thm:universal} forces a beth-fixed-point cardinal height
\(\kappa\). The minimum proper-class size then forces
\(\cf(\kappa)=\kappa\), hence strong inaccessibility. At an inaccessible
height both the minimum and maximum sizes equal \(\kappa\), so all
proper classes have the required bijections.
\end{proof}

At a noninitial height, condition (i) is not the same as regular cardinal
height. For example \(\lambda=\omega_1\cdot2\) has
\(\cf(\lambda)=|\lambda|=\omega_1\), but fails ordinal-domain Class
Replacement since \(\omega_1\) is an internal ordinal domain. This example
separates cardinal comparability from internal image bounding.

\section{Explicit separating models}\label{swo:gcz:sec:examples}

\subsection{Global choice without any ordinal sign enumeration}

Take \(\lambda=\omega+\omega\). Then
\[
 |\Ord^{\RM_\lambda}|=\aleph_0,
 \qquad |S_\lambda|=2^{\aleph_0},
 \qquad |V_\lambda|=\beth_\omega.
\]
Global choice and birthday-monotone set-like well-orders exist, but even a
class injection \(S_\lambda\injto\Ord\) is impossible. Class Replacement
on \(\omega\) fails, witnessed by the class function
\(n\mapsto\omega+n\), whose range is unbounded in \(\lambda\).
Thus a global selector, including its countable restriction, need not supply
any countable image-bounding principle.

\subsection{Ordinal sign enumeration without birthday enumeration}

Assume CH and take \(\lambda=\omega_1\). Then
\(2^{<\omega_1}=2^{\aleph_0}=\omega_1\), so a class bijection
\(\omega_1\longleftrightarrow S_{\omega_1}\) exists. But there are
\(\omega_1\) sequences of birthday \(\omega\). A birthday-monotone
enumeration would have to place all of them before any sequence of birthday
\(\omega+1\). No position below \(\omega_1\) has that many predecessors.

Ordinal-domain Class Replacement holds by regularity, but full Class Replacement
and ordinal abstraction fail. This refines the role of the established
\(V_{\omega_1}\) example by separating arbitrary sign enumeration from
enumeration that respects the birthday filtration.

\subsection{Birthday enumeration without universal set coding}

Take \(\kappa=\beth_\omega\). This is a singular strong-limit cardinal
of cofinality \(\omega\). Hence ordinal birthday enumeration of
\(S_\kappa\) exists. But
\[
 |V_\kappa|=\beth_\kappa>\beth_\omega=\kappa=|S_\kappa|.
\]
Universal set coding and ordinal abstraction fail. This example requires no
continuum hypothesis and no inaccessible cardinal.

\subsection{Universal coding and ordinal abstraction without Replacement}

Define externally
\[
 \kappa_0=\omega,\qquad
 \kappa_{n+1}=\beth_{\kappa_n},\qquad
 \kappa=\sup_{n<\omega}\kappa_n.
\]
The sequence is strictly increasing, so \(\cf(\kappa)=\omega\).
Continuity gives
\(\beth_\kappa=\sup_n\beth_{\kappa_n}
 =\sup_n\kappa_{n+1}=\kappa\).
This is the first beth fixed point reached above the starting value.
Consequently
\[
 V_\kappa\longleftrightarrow S_\kappa\longleftrightarrow\kappa
\]
by class bijections, and every internal set well-order has an internal ordinal
type. Nevertheless the admitted class function \(n\mapsto\kappa_n\)
has unbounded range. Even \(\CR(\omega)\) fails.

No first-order definability assertion about this particular sequence is needed
for the example: every external class function is admitted in the structure.
This makes its failure of \emph{Class} Replacement immediate and avoids
confusing the two replacement schemas.

\subsection{The inaccessible case}

If a strongly inaccessible \(\kappa\) exists, all properties in the main
classification table hold in \(\RM_\kappa\). In particular, every internal
proper class has external cardinality \(\kappa\), and its class functions
on internal sets have internally bounded images. This is the setting in which
the rank-model examples in the inspected ProveIt report are placed.
(\merge\ This report: \cref{swo:st:sec:model,swo:ec:sec:universe,swo:ix:sec:universes}.)

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccccc@{}}
\toprule
Height & \(\GC\) & bare sign & birthday & universal & full \(\CR\)\\
 & & enumeration & enumeration & set coding & \\
\midrule
\(\omega+\omega\) & yes & no & no & no & no\\
\(\omega_1\), assuming CH & yes & yes & no & no & no\\
\(\beth_\omega\) & yes & yes & yes & no & no\\
First beth fixed point & yes & yes & yes & yes & no\\
Strongly inaccessible \(\kappa\) & yes & yes & yes & yes & yes\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\section{Consequences for surreal foundations and formalization}\label{swo:gcz:sec:formal}

\subsection{A precise extension of the ProveIt questions}

The classification explains why a proof formulated over \(\GB\) cannot simply
be read over \(\ZC\) with class comprehension. Three jobs must be separated:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Selection:} choose a local presentation or local order.
\item \emph{Collapse and coding:} represent that presentation by an available
      ordinal or sign sequence.
\item \emph{Image bounding:} ensure that the values obtained over a set domain
      still form an internal set.
\end{enumerate}
The first part of this article shows that selection restricted to countable
inputs already has nonconservative consequences when combined with expanded
Separation. The second shows that even unrestricted selection leaves collapse
and image bounding at distinct thresholds in full-class rank models.

These are concrete answers about the mechanisms named in the repository's weak
foundations agenda (\merge\ \cref{swo:ge:n10}; the questions
\cref{swo:pc:n13.9,swo:nb:n14.10} of sources~24 and~26 ask about the same
resources). They do not prove that its supported-prefix extension,
small-net rigidity, or inverse-reconstruction schemes are each equivalent to a
particular row of our table. Establishing those equivalences would require
encoding the exact input and output types of each scheme in a common weak base.

\subsection{A formalization architecture with an explicit trust boundary}

A proof assistant development can formalize the first part without implementing
all the symmetric-extension machinery. The natural target is a theorem about
models of a specified first-order theory, with Glazer's obstruction isolated as
an input interface. Its parameters would be formulas defining the class family,
incidence relation, label domain, and target map, together with their required
properties. The formal theorem would show that no expanded model can satisfy
both that interface and countable selection with the relevant Separation
instances.

The thread construction should be represented by a bounded object:
\(\Thr_X\subseteq\Pow(X)\times\Pow(X^2)\).
The main lemmas are initial-segment comparability, well-foundedness of its union,
maximality, rigidity of well-orders, and correctness of least-code normalization.
The compression theorem then needs only injectivity of each row presentation
and target separation by traces. This organization makes accidental appeals to
Replacement visible.

For the second part, use a universe separation: the metatheory has an actual set
\(V_\lambda\), and its class sort is another set \(\Pow(V_\lambda)\)
in the larger universe. Internal ``set'' and external ``set'' are distinct
predicates. No term denoting a set of all sets or a set of all actual surreal
numbers is required. The sign carrier is explicitly the set
\(\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}{}^\alpha2\) in the metatheory.

A first machine-checked milestone should be the domain-size criterion
\cref{swo:gcz:lem:domain}, followed by the sign-cardinality formula and the two
enumeration thresholds. These use ordinary external cardinal arithmetic and
rank bounds. The ordinal-abstraction theorem adds the distinction between an
internal well-order relation and its external order type.

\subsection{Why no experimental computation is offered as proof}\label{swo:gcz:sub:noexperiment}

Finite experiments with selectors can illustrate the thread construction, but
cannot verify nonconservativity, lack of ordinal collapse, or Class Replacement.
The mathematical verification here consists of displayed set bounds and
independent checks of the proofs. The supplied source is an ordinary LaTeX
article, not a proof-assistant certificate. A later formal development should
report separately the checked uniformization theorem and any assumed
countermodel construction.

localized nonconservativity statement would be the next scholarly step.

\section{The question and the contribution}
\label{swo:bo:sec:scope}

There are two quite different senses in which an ordering can be longer
than all ordinals. An ordinary set cannot carry a well-order longer than
every ordinal: its order type is itself an ordinal. A proper class can
carry such an ordering, and can carry many different ones. For example,
tagging each ordinal with $0$ and putting a new tagged endpoint above
all of them gives $\Omega+1$. Putting one entire tagged copy of the
ordinals after another gives $\Omega+\Omega$. The endpoint or the first
point of the second copy has a proper class of predecessors. That is
the precise structural change.

The purpose of this paper is not to postulate an absolute ordinal above
all ordinals. It is to organize the well-orders already expressible as
class relations, determine which operations are legitimate, and identify
what limits their notation. A formula defining a relation, a proof that
it is well-ordered, an isomorphism to another presentation, and a uniform
procedure ranging over all definitions are different mathematical objects.
Much of the difficulty lies in keeping these objects separate.

\subsection{Relation to the inspected ProveIt material}

We inspected the ProveIt repository at commit
\texttt{e1d2f3048b947801873a6e9ddc4e03736234b328}.
The principal source is the consolidated report
\emph{Lexicographic Orders of Well-Orderings of the Surreal Numbers},
especially its treatment of canonical blocks, polynomial presentations,
and Source 29's canonical-history equivalence \cite{xviAtPinBO}.
Its status ledger explicitly leaves the theory over $\GB$ open after
establishing the corresponding equivalence over $\GBC$. The present
paper supplies the missing choice-free polynomial argument and checks the
remaining dependencies. The theorem applies to arbitrary supplied class
well-orders, not only to a surreal carrier.

The repository also contains work on omnific notation and definable
surreal numbers. Those directions concern additional algebraic structures
or definability of individual numbers. Here the objects are order
presentations. In particular, a formal symbol $\Omega$ in this paper
does not designate a surreal larger than every ordinal surreal.
There is no such surreal in the usual class of surreal numbers, since
each surreal is set-coded and has an ordinal birthday.

The most direct answer to a repository open question is the change of base
theory in the third row. The other developments provide a systematic
framework for constructing, interpreting, and bounding long notations.
The much broader problem of whether strong class-well-order comparability
implies $\ETR$ is not solved here. Hamkins and Woodin formulate that
question explicitly; the sources checked during preparation did not provide
a verified later resolution \cite[Theorem 6 and Question 7]{HamkinsWoodin}.
This is a dated literature-status statement, not a proof that no resolution
exists.

\subsection{What ``farther'' will mean}

For class well-orders $A,B$, write $A\emb B$ if there is a class
order embedding and $A\iemb B$ if an embedding has an initial range,
allowing the whole range. We use $A\cong B$ for a class isomorphism.
The claim that $B$ is strictly longer than $A$ is strongest when
$A$ embeds as a proper initial segment of $B$. A construction that
contains $A+1$ as a suborder also proves $B\not\emb A$, even when
initial-segment comparability is unavailable. We specify which conclusion
is proved rather than silently identifying the two relations.

In a sufficiently large external universe, a class model can itself be
set-sized. Its internally proper class orders then have ordinary external
ordinal lengths. This supplies precise numerical calibrations, but those
external ordinals are not new ordinals of the original model.

% ---- source 35, its Section 1
\subsection{Source 35: scope, results, and their provenance}

% ---- source 35 (batch-96 manuscript 11), lines 123-224
\label{swo:fc:sec:introduction}

There is a coherent arithmetic of well-ordered classes that continue
past the order $\Ord$.  Its objects should be understood as ordered
presentations, and its equality should be understood as the existence
of an appropriate class isomorphism.  This immediately permits
$\Ord+1$ without asserting the existence of a set ordinal larger than
every ordinal.  The new final point is a tagged set in a class carrier;
its predecessor class is proper.  This distinction is the starting
point for everything that follows.

The question ``how far beyond $\Ord$?'' has several answers.  Explicit
finite syntax reaches sums, products, class powers, and an exponential
fixed point containing every finite tower of $\Ord$-powers.  Given a
fixed point, one can construct another strictly above it.  A uniformly
coded family with a supplied well-ordered index class always has a strict
upper bound for ordinary suborder embeddability, so no such family is
cofinal among all class well-orders.  In ambient ZFC, for strongly
inaccessible $\kappa$, the full two-sorted model based on $V_\kappa$ has
external upper boundary $\kappa^+$, while a family restricted to first-order
definitions occupies a bounded part of that spectrum.  None of these
statements identifies a last class ordinal.

The main results fall into three groups.  First, we give an explicit
arithmetic with proofs requiring only predicative class comprehension
and class Replacement.  Second, we connect the repository's canonical
condensation machinery with fixed-point completion.  Third, we quantify
the obstruction to one all-purpose definable notation system.  The
axioms used in the second and third groups are specified separately:
an explicit constructor being elementary is a much weaker assertion
than every class well-order having a comparable canonical presentation.

\subsubsection{What is inherited, and what is developed here}

The relevant ProveIt source is the maintained
\emph{surreal-well-orders} article, inspected at commit
\texttt{f158f27b46bd1efb5a771ffc3c07e64eea970501}, dated
4 October 2026 \cite{xviAtPinFC}.  Its polynomial orders and canonical
histories are directly relevant even though the surrounding report
also studies lexicographic orders of labelled well-orders.  This paper
studies the individual well-order presentations themselves.

The repository identifies its relevant additions as unrefereed and
not machine formalized.  We therefore supply proofs of the machinery
needed for the extensions, rather than treating a manuscript label as
a proof certificate.  The results called extensions are new relative
to the inspected development; this statement is deliberately narrower
than a claim of first discovery in the literature.  In particular,
the article does not claim a solution to the general reverse-mathematical
problem asking whether $\CWO$ implies $\ETR$.

\subsubsection{A precise reading of the choice-free improvement}

The repository explicitly retains the question of the strength of
canonical histories over $\GB$ without Global Choice.  The improvement
proved below addresses this boundary: the same four-way characterization
already holds over $\GB$.  This identifies the history principle with
strong comparability in that weaker base.  It does \emph{not} prove
either principle outright in $\GB$, give a complete independence
classification, or remove Choice from every theorem about orders of
the entire surreal carrier.  Transporting arbitrary proper carriers to
one fixed carrier is a separate use of Global Choice.

Over $\GBC$, the key local result concerning fixed points can be read
independently of any universal comparison principle.  For a supplied well-order $W$,
one specific initial embedding $W\iemb P(W)$ is enough to construct
a fixed-point extension of $W$.  Conversely, a fixed-point extension
provides this embedding.  Thus a question about completing one order
has a concrete structural certificate.

% ---- source 32, its Section 1
\subsection{Source 32: the question and the scope of the answer}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 101-117
\label{swo:dc:sec:scope}

The expression ``longer than $\Ord$'' becomes meaningful as soon as one stops requiring every predecessor segment of a well-order to be a set. For example, take two disjoint copies of $\Ord$, place the first entirely before the second, and compare ordinals normally within each copy. Every nonempty admitted subclass has a least point, but the first point of the second copy has a proper class of predecessors. This is a legitimate class well-order, not a new von Neumann ordinal.

We write
\[
\Omega=(\Ord,{<})
\]
for this \emph{order presentation}. An expression such as $\Omega^{[\Omega]}$ will denote a specifically defined class of sets with a specifically defined ordering. It will never mean that $\Ord$ has become an element of the set universe. Likewise, a variable $W$ denotes a supplied class relation and its domain, not an element of a class of all proper-class order types.

There are three different questions behind the user's problem. Which long orders have explicit definitions in a weak class theory? Which recursive operations can that theory perform along those orders? And, relative to a specified model and a specified meaning of ``definable'', which external ordinal lengths can its class presentations realize? These questions have different answers. A large presentation need not support strong recursion, and an externally available isomorphism need not be an admitted class.

\subsubsection{Main results and their provenance}

The constructions of sums, products, and finite-support powers in \cref{swo:dc:sec:arithmetic} are presentation-level extensions of ordinary ordinal arithmetic. The set-like boundary and the distinction between arbitrary and initial embeddings are foundational facts, not proposed discoveries. The repository already develops least-representative set-interval blocks and explicit polynomial condensation examples \cite{xviStatusTwentyThree,xviReadme}. We reprove the ingredients needed here and use them to sharpen the structural picture.

The principal additional results proved in this manuscript are the uniform diagonal theorem (\cref{swo:dc:thm:diagonal}), the conditional termination bound for general condensation (\cref{swo:dc:thm:termination}), and the definability-ceiling and exact truth-presentation theorems (\cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling,swo:dc:thm:truth}). These are mathematical contributions of this treatment in the sense that complete arguments are supplied here. Their historical novelty has not been established. The condensation theorem answers the repository's termination question under an explicit recursion hypothesis, while leaving the exact strength of hierarchy existence open.

The repository inspection was targeted rather than exhaustive. The relevant research-status file explicitly distinguishes its GBC polynomial examples from a general termination theorem. The merged report identifies the source as manuscript 23, with its condensation material incorporated into the larger surreal well-order study \cite{xviStatusTwentyThree,xviReadme}. We do not certify the other manuscripts in that collection.

\subsubsection{Conventions about foundations}

Our default theory is $\GBC$: G\"odel--Bernays class theory with Global Choice and a ZFC set part. Every member of a class is a set. A class relation can therefore be coded by a class of ordered pairs or tuples of sets. Class parameters in elementary comprehension are allowed, but quantification over classes inside that comprehension is not.

When a statement is made in a model $(M,\mathcal X)$, ``class'' means an element of the admitted class collection $\mathcal X$. This is especially important for well-foundedness and isomorphisms. Sections \cref{swo:dc:sec:spectrum} and \cref{swo:dc:sec:truth} explicitly change viewpoint to an external ZFC metatheory with a strongly inaccessible cardinal. Their ordinal spectra are external sets of ordinals; they are not same-level class quotients in GBC.

% ---- source 33, its Section 1
\subsection{Source 33: the problem and the principal results}\label{swo:dh:sec:intro}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 143-239
\subsubsection{What does ``longer than Ord'' mean?}
Write
\[
   \Omega=(\Ord,\in)
\]
for the class well-order of all set ordinals. The symbol $\Omega$ is an abbreviation
for an order presentation, \emph{not} a new set and not an ordinal of the same
universe. The tagged disjoint union $\Omega+1$ is a perfectly legitimate class
well-order. Its last point has a proper class of predecessors. This is precisely
why the usual theorem assigning an ordinal to every \emph{set} well-order does
not collapse $\Omega+1$ to a set ordinal or to $\Omega$.

There are several different questions hidden in the request to go beyond
$\Ord$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),itemsep=2pt]
\item Which longer orders can be constructed by explicit formulas?
\item Which arithmetic operations preserve class well-foundedness?
\item When can two arbitrary class well-orders be compared by an initial
      embedding?
\item How does the answer depend on allowed parameters, truth predicates,
      and the surrounding class model?
\item Can all relevant orders be organized into one uniform notation system?
\end{enumerate}
The answers are not interchangeable. In particular, constructing
$\Omega^{[\Omega]}$ is much easier than producing a uniform comparison procedure for
arbitrary class well-orders. The literature on class recursion makes this
separation explicit \cite{HamkinsWoodin,GitmanHamkins,xviBartonWilliams}.

\subsubsection{A map of the results proved here}
The article's main statements are the following.

\begin{resultbox}\textbf{Structural and definability results.}\par
\textbf{Canonical division.} Every class well-order $W$ has a canonical
presentation
\[
                   W\cong \Omega\cdot Q+\alpha,
\]
where $Q$ is a class well-order and $\alpha$ is a set ordinal
(\cref{swo:dh:thm:division}).

\textbf{Finite digits.} An exhausting, uniformly supplied set-interval
condensation tower indexed by $\Gamma+1$ yields an order embedding
\[
                   W\longrightarrow\Omega^{[\Gamma]}
\]
whose values have finite support (\cref{swo:dh:thm:digits}).

\textbf{Definability diagonal.} At every fixed finite syntactic level $n$,
a parameter-free-in-$(\in,G)$ order $D_n$ dominates every set-parameter
$\Sigma_n(G)$ presentation, and $D_n$ embeds into none of those orders
(\cref{swo:dh:thm:bounded}).

\textbf{External height.} Over $V_\kappa$ with $\kappa$ inaccessible, the
supremum $\delta_G$ of the $G$-definable well-order types satisfies
\[
 \kappa<\delta_G<\kappa^+,
 \qquad \cf(\delta_G)=\omega,
 \qquad \delta_{G,T}>\delta_G
\]
when $T$ is truth for $(V_\kappa,\in,G)$
(\cref{swo:dh:thm:height,swo:dh:thm:truthjump}).
\end{resultbox}

The most important common mechanism is \emph{uniformity}. A class-indexed
family of class relations is usable when one class of tuples gives all its
sections. A metatheoretic collection of individually definable relations does
not automatically have such a code. The difference accounts both for positive
constructions and for diagonal obstructions.

\subsubsection{Relationship with ProveIt and the literature}\label{swo:dh:subsec:repo}
The targeted repository review used the main README, the surreal research
catalogue, and the guide to
\texttt{Algebra/SurrealNumbers/docs/foundations-and-computation/}
\texttt{surreal-well-orders/} \cite{xviProveItReadme,xviCatalogue,xviReadme}.
The latter guide describes twenty-three merged manuscripts and an 860-page
report. It explicitly separates unrefereed research text from formalized Lean
results. Its later parts already contain class-order and transfinite
condensation material. Therefore neither the existence of orders beyond
$\Ord$ nor the general idea of an arbitrarily long condensation hierarchy is
claimed here as a new contribution to the repository.

This manuscript takes a different organizing route: intrinsic class-order
arithmetic, canonical division, finite digits, and the relationship between
syntactic complexity and attainable order lengths. Its proofs are
self-contained except for clearly cited foundational background. The
repository review was targeted, not a line-by-line audit of the full merged
report, and it does not establish absence of overlapping arguments elsewhere
in the repository.

Three literature interfaces matter particularly. First, class comparison is
part of the reverse mathematics of elementary transfinite recursion
\cite{HamkinsWoodin}. Second, truth predicates and their iterations are genuine
class-existence principles rather than harmless uniform notation
\cite{GitmanHamkins,GHHSW}. Third, unrolling and class-theoretic potentialism
supply ways to study external order heights while retaining the distinction
between sets and classes \cite{Williams,xviBartonWilliams,AntosFriedman}. The results below
are not presented as solutions of the published comparison/recursion problems.
