\subsubsection{Fix the language before asking what is definable}
Fix a named set-like global well-order $G$ and the first-order language
\[
                             \mathcal L_G=\{\in,G\}.
\]
A presentation is \emph{$G$-definable with set parameters} if its domain and
relation are defined by two formulas of this language with a finite tuple
of set parameters. It is \emph{set-parameter-free} if no such tuple is
needed. The named class $G$ is still allowed.

Allowing an arbitrary new class parameter for each presentation would make
this distinction meaningless: every relation is definable from itself.
Likewise, allowing a truth predicate changes the language and must be
recorded explicitly.

Choose an ordinary effective coding of formulas and finite parameter tuples.
For each fixed standard natural number $n$, let $\Sigma_n(G)$ denote a
standard bounded level of the first-order hierarchy. It is harmless to pad
formulas with unused quantifiers, so every particular first-order formula
belongs to $\Sigma_n(G)$ for some sufficiently large finite $n$.
We require both the domain formula and the relation formula of a
$\Sigma_n(G)$ presentation to lie at that level.

\begin{lemma}[Partial evaluation at a fixed level]\label{swo:dh:lem:partialsat}
For each fixed standard finite $n$, there is an elementary formula
$\Sat_n(e,\vec a;G)$ that correctly evaluates $\Sigma_n(G)$ formulas coded
by $e$ at assignments $\vec a$. Its construction is a metatheoretic schema
in $n$, not an assertion that all the predicates $\Sat_n$ form one
$G$-definable class uniformly in $n$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Bounded formulas can be evaluated inside a set containing the transitive
closures of the parameter values. Restrict the named class predicate $G$
to the relevant set of pairs; elementary class separation supplies this
restriction as a set. Ordinary satisfaction for that set structure evaluates
the bounded formula.

For a fixed number of unbounded quantifier blocks, place those blocks in
front of the bounded evaluation formula and handle their finite tuples of
variables by set coding. This gives a finite first-order formula for the
chosen level. The passage from level $n$ to the next is a construction of
formulas outside the object theory; it does not supply truth for all
formulas in one predicate.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The bounded-complexity diagonal}
\begin{theorem}[Bounded definability cannot bound class-order length]\label{swo:dh:thm:bounded}
For each fixed standard finite $n$, there is a class well-order $D_n$ with
a set-parameter-free definition in $\mathcal L_G$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),itemsep=2pt]
\item every class well-order having a $\Sigma_n(G)$ presentation with
      arbitrary set parameters embeds into $D_n$;
\item $D_n$ embeds into no class well-order having such a presentation;
\item in particular, $D_n$ has no isomorphic $\Sigma_n(G)$ presentation,
      even one using set parameters.
\end{enumerate}
The quantification over $n$ is a schema. Each instance is provable in $\GBC$.
Nonembedding in (b) holds for all embeddings available in the ambient class
model, not merely for definable embeddings of bounded complexity.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\emph{Coding all candidate parameters.}
Let the index class be all sets in the order $G$. A valid index is a code
\[
                          i=(e_D,e_R,\vec p)
\]
for a pair of $\Sigma_n(G)$ formulas and a finite set-parameter tuple.
Invalid codes will designate the empty order.
Using the fixed evaluator from \cref{swo:dh:lem:partialsat}, define the candidate
domain and relation jointly in $i,x,y$.

\emph{Selecting only well-orders.}
For a valid index, test whether the candidate relation, restricted to its
domain, is a linear order and has no descending set function of domain
$\omega$. This is a first-order property of $i$ in the language with $G$:
replace each occurrence of the candidate domain and relation by its
$\Sat_n$ definition. By \cref{swo:dh:lem:wftest}, the test is equivalent to being
a class well-order in the ambient model. If the test fails, replace the
candidate by the empty order.

Thus we have one $G$-definable uniform family $(W_i)_{i\in V}$ of genuine
class well-orders, containing every $\Sigma_n(G)$ presentation with any
set parameters. No truth predicate beyond the chosen partial level was
used. The well-orderhood test can increase formula complexity; it is not
claimed to remain $\Sigma_n(G)$.

\emph{Diagonalization.}
Put
\[
                         D_n=\sum_{i\in(V,G)}(W_i+1).
\]
The index $n$ has been fixed externally and is represented by a numeral in
the resulting formula. All set parameters of all candidates are now
variables ranging through the index class. Consequently this presentation
of $D_n$ has no set parameters.

Apply \cref{swo:dh:thm:diagonal}. It gives (a) and (b). If (c) failed, choose an
index $i$ coding an isomorphic $\Sigma_n(G)$ presentation. That isomorphism
would itself be an embedding of $D_n$ into $W_i$, contradicting (b).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Parameter-free presentations are externally cofinal]\label{swo:dh:cor:paramfree}
Every $G$-definable class well-order with set parameters embeds into a
set-parameter-free $G$-definable class well-order. Externally, the countable
family of presentations
\[
                           D_0,D_1,D_2,\ldots
\]
is cofinal under embeddability among all $G$-definable class well-orders
with set parameters.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The two formulas defining a given presentation have some fixed finite
complexity bound $n$. Apply \cref{swo:dh:thm:bounded}(a).
\end{proof}

This is a cofinality statement, not pointwise elimination of parameters.
It does not say that every parameter-definable order has an isomorphic
parameter-free presentation. The replacement order can be substantially
longer, as the diagonal construction intentionally ensures.

\begin{corollary}[No definable uniform cofinal family]\label{swo:dh:cor:nodefcofinal}
There is no $G$-definable uniform family of class well-orders, indexed by a
$G$-definable class of sets and allowing a fixed finite tuple of set
parameters in its definition, which is cofinal among all $G$-definable
class well-orders with set parameters.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Order the indices by the restriction of $G$. The diagonal of that family
is again $G$-definable with the same fixed parameters. Cofinality would
place its order type below a member under embeddability, contradicting
\cref{swo:dh:thm:diagonal}.
\end{proof}

In particular, the external list of formulas defining the $D_n$ is not a
uniform $G$-definable evaluation of all their order relations. The schema
and the missing uniform evaluator coexist without contradiction. This is
one place where the analogy with truth hierarchies is exact in its logical
shape: every fixed level is available, while their complete uniform
assembly requires a change of resources.

\subsubsection{Removing the named global order in special universes}
\begin{corollary}\label{swo:dh:cor:pure}
Suppose the universe has a parameter-free first-order definable set-like
global well-order. Then every set-parameter-definable class well-order
embeds into a parameter-free first-order definable class well-order.
There is an external countable cofinal family of the latter presentations.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Use the definable global order as $G$ in \cref{swo:dh:cor:paramfree}, then replace
occurrences of $G$ in each resulting formula by its fixed parameter-free
definition. The substitution may increase finite complexity but introduces
no parameters.
\end{proof}

The constructible universe provides the standard intended example through
its canonical global ordering. Without a definable global well-order, this
proof does not remove the named class parameter. It is important not to
replace ``relative to $G$'' by an unconditional parameter-free claim about
every model of $\ZFC$.

\subsubsection{A precise account of what has been resolved}
The preceding theorems answer three concrete structural questions:
\emph{Can one fixed definability level be cofinal?} No.
\emph{Do arbitrary set parameters increase the external supremum beyond
parameter-free presentations, once $G$ is fixed?} No.
\emph{Can the resulting countable cofinal construction itself be uniformly
evaluated in the same language?} No.

These are proved statements with explicit hypotheses. They are not claimed
to settle a historically recognized open problem. Establishing whether the
same arguments or consequences occur in the existing literature requires
a broader bibliographic and expert review than the targeted search recorded
here.

% ---- source 34 (batch-96 manuscript 10), lines 1603-1865
\section{External spectra and the effect of definability}
\label{swo:bo:spec:section}

The question ``how far beyond $\Ord$?'' acquires a precise numerical answer
after a model and its available classes have been fixed. The answer belongs
to the external metatheory: a proper class of a set model is itself an
ordinary set externally. Its genuinely well-founded orderings therefore
have ordinary external ordinal ordertypes. This viewpoint does not turn an
internal proper class into an internal set. It compares two different
levels of discourse.

Throughout this section the metatheory is ZFC. A \emph{transitive
$\beta$-model} $(M,\mathcal X)$ is a transitive model of class theory which
is correct about the well-foundedness of its class relations. Transitivity
alone does not imply this correctness: an external descending sequence
through a class relation need not be a set of $M$. The distinction is
standard in the model theory of second-order set theories
\cite{Williams}. Our spectra below count genuinely externally
well-founded orders. The $\beta$-hypothesis will allow an internal
definability test to select exactly those orders.

\subsection{The full spectrum over an inaccessible universe}

\begin{theorem}[Full spectrum]
\label{swo:bo:spec:full}
Let $\kappa$ be an inaccessible cardinal in the external universe. In the
full class model
\[
   \mathfrak V_\kappa=(V_\kappa,\mathcal P(V_\kappa)),
\]
the external ordertypes of class well-orders are exactly the ordinals
$\alpha<\kappa^+$. Those whose domains are internally proper classes have
exactly the ordertypes
\[
   \kappa\leq\alpha<\kappa^+.
\]
Here $\Ord^{\mathfrak V_\kappa}$ has external ordertype $\kappa$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Inaccessibility gives $|V_\kappa|=\kappa$. Every class domain is an external
subset of $V_\kappa$, so any well-order on it has cardinality at most
$\kappa$ and hence ordertype below $\kappa^+$. Conversely, every
$\alpha<\kappa^+$ has cardinality at most $\kappa$, so an injection into
$V_\kappa$ transports its ordering to a subclass of $V_\kappa$. Every such
relation is available in the full class collection. Finite tuple coding
stays inside $V_\kappa$, so binary relations can be represented by unary
class predicates.

Every element of $V_\kappa$ has cardinality below $\kappa$. Conversely, an
external subset $D\subseteq V_\kappa$ of cardinality below $\kappa$ has
bounded element ranks by regularity; consequently $D\in V_\kappa$.
Thus a subclass is internally proper precisely when its external
cardinality is $\kappa$. The second assertion follows.
\end{proof}

The use of inaccessibility also makes the full class model a legitimate
model of the usual strong class axioms: arbitrary class comprehension is
available, and regularity ensures that the image of an internal set under
a class function remains an internal set. It is a $\beta$-model. Indeed,
an external countable sequence of elements of $V_\kappa$ has bounded ranks
and belongs to $V_\kappa$. The same argument shows $\beta$-correctness for
any GBC realization over this $V_\kappa$.

\Cref{swo:bo:spec:full} supplies an exact ceiling, but only relative to
this particular model and the full external class collection. The ceiling
$\kappa^+$ is not itself represented by one of its class well-orders. It
is neither an internal successor cardinal of a set $\Ord$ nor a largest
class ordertype. Restricting the available definitions gives a much
smaller external ceiling.

\subsection{Parameter spectra are intervals; parameter-free spectra need not be}

Fix a transitive set model $M$ with a finite language $L$ expanding
membership by named class predicates. Assume these predicates occur in a
GBC realization, so first-order definitions and their set restrictions
are legitimate available classes. Put $\lambda=|M|$, externally. Let
$\mathcal S_{\mathrm{par}}^L$ be the external ordertypes of well-orders on
subclasses of $M$ whose domains and relations are first-order
$L$-definable using finite tuples of set parameters from $M$. Write
$\mathcal S_0^L$ for the parameter-free version. A named predicate is part
of the language; ``parameter-free'' here excludes additional set
parameters, not the named predicates themselves.

\begin{proposition}[The parameter spectrum]
\label{swo:bo:spec:interval}
There is a limit ordinal $\Theta_L<\lambda^+$ such that
\[
   \mathcal S_{\mathrm{par}}^L=[0,\Theta_L).
\]
The set $\mathcal S_0^L$ is countable, is closed under successors, and has
no greatest member. Its supremum has cofinality $\omega$. In general
$\mathcal S_0^L$ need not be an ordinal interval.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
There are countably many formulas and only $\lambda$ finite parameter
tuples, so $|\mathcal S_{\mathrm{par}}^L|\leq\lambda$. If an order has
external ordertype $\alpha$ and $\beta<\alpha$, let $x\in M$ be its element
at position $\beta$. The initial segment below $x$ is definable with $x$
as one more set parameter and has ordertype $\beta$. Therefore the
parameter spectrum is downward closed.

Tagged addition of one last element turns any definable presentation of
$\alpha$ into a definable presentation of $\alpha+1$, using the same
parameters. Thus this downward closed set has no largest member. It is
an ordinal interval $[0,\Theta_L)$ for a limit $\Theta_L$, and its
cardinality bound implies $\Theta_L<\lambda^+$.

There are only countably many parameter-free definitions. Successor
addition is still parameter-free, so their ordertypes have no largest
member. Their supremum consequently has cofinality exactly $\omega$.
The initial-segment argument does not establish downward closure here,
because the cutoff point need not be parameter-free definable.
\end{proof}

In fact, for a parameter-free definable \emph{set} well-order, its unique
ordinal collapse is parameter-free definable. Thus, over $V_\kappa$ for
uncountable inaccessible $\kappa$, the countable parameter-free spectrum
omits many ordinals below $\kappa$, whereas the definable class $\Ord$
itself supplies the external type $\kappa$. This gives a concrete reason
the parameter-free spectrum is not downward closed in that setting.

For $M=V_\kappa$, the parameter spectrum contains $\kappa$ and its
successor, and \Cref{swo:bo:spec:interval} gives the strict bounds
\[
   \kappa<\Theta_L<\kappa^+.
\]
These are external statements about definitions over the fixed
structure. They do not require the isomorphism between two presentations
of the same external type to be definable over that structure. The
external initial-segment theorem therefore does not settle the internal
class well-order comparability problem.

\subsection{Parameter elimination by a definable sum}

We now prove a more informative relation between the two spectra. It
uses explicit class sums to remove set parameters from an upper bound
on a given definable ordertype. We present it as a synthesis theorem with
a full proof, without a claim of historical priority. Naming the
predicates is essential. The broader
study of expansions by truth predicates and additional classes provides
the appropriate surrounding context \cite{xviBartonWilliams}.

\begin{theorem}[Parameter-free cofinality, relative to a global order]
\label{swo:bo:spec:cofinal}
Let $(M,\mathcal X)$ be a transitive $\beta$-model of GBC. Fix finitely
many class predicates $\vec A\in\mathcal X$ and a global well-order
$G\in\mathcal X$. In the finite language
$L=\{\in,\vec A,G\}$, the parameter-free spectrum is cofinal in the
set-parameter spectrum. Consequently,
\[
   \sup\mathcal S_0^L=\Theta_L,
   \qquad \operatorname{cf}(\Theta_L)=\omega.
\]
If $G$ is parameter-free definable from the other named predicates, it
need not be added as a separate symbol.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix one pair of ordinary finite $L$-formulas
$\delta(x,\vec p)$ and $\rho(x,y,\vec p)$, with a fixed finite number
of parameter positions. For every tuple $\vec q$ of the corresponding
length from $M$, let $D_{\vec q}$ and $R_{\vec q}$ be the domain and
relation obtained by substituting $\vec q$. Let $I_{\delta,\rho}$ be
the class of those tuples for which $M$ judges $R_{\vec q}$ to be a
class well-order on $D_{\vec q}$.

This filtering condition is first-order and uses no set parameters.
Substitute the two fixed formulas into the requirements for a linear
order and into the assertion that no descending \emph{set} sequence
of length $\omega$ exists. There is no variable formula code to
evaluate, so no satisfaction predicate is needed. Elementary
comprehension supplies $I_{\delta,\rho}$, and the restriction of $G$
well-orders its tuple codes.

Form the lexicographic sum
\[
   U_{\delta,\rho}
      =\sum_{\vec q\in(I_{\delta,\rho},G)}
                    (D_{\vec q},R_{\vec q}).
\]
Its elements are set pairs $(\vec q,x)$ with
$\vec q\in I_{\delta,\rho}$ and $x\in D_{\vec q}$. Distinct blocks
are compared by $G$, and elements of one block by $R_{\vec q}$. The
domain and ordering are $L$-definable without set parameters, with the
fixed formulas substituted into their definitions. Internally this is
a class well-order: a nonempty subclass has a least occupied index and
then a least element in that block. It is therefore externally
well-founded by $\beta$-correctness. The same correctness ensures that
the filter admitted no externally ill-founded candidates.

Every genuinely well-founded instance of this formula pair, with any
particular parameter tuple $\vec p$, passes the internal test and
occurs as a block of $U_{\delta,\rho}$. Its external ordertype is
therefore at most $\otp(U_{\delta,\rho})$. This proves that every
member of $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{par}}^L$ is bounded by a member of
$\mathcal S_0^L$.

Externally there are countably many ordinary finite formula pairs.
Enumerating them gives a countable cofinal family of the separately
defined orders $U_{\delta,\rho}$. The two spectra have the same
supremum, and successor closure excludes a largest member. Hence
$\operatorname{cf}(\Theta_L)=\omega$.
\end{proof}

The hypotheses are deliberately explicit. The realization
$\operatorname{Def}(M;\vec A,G)$, allowing set parameters, inherits class
replacement and satisfies GBC. It is also a $\beta$-model: both
realizations have the same sets, and in each the well-foundedness of a
common class relation is equivalent to the absence of a descending
$M$-set $\omega$-sequence. They therefore agree about well-foundedness,
and the larger realization is $\beta$-correct. No assumption that every
possible external class is available is needed. Conversely, mere
transitivity would not justify
the filter: a candidate with an external descending sequence missing
from $M$ could be admitted. Naming $G$ does not assert a parameter-free
definable global well-order in the original pure membership language.

\begin{corollary}
\label{swo:bo:spec:inaccessible-relative}
For an inaccessible $\kappa$ and fixed named predicates $\vec A,G$ in
the full class model over $V_\kappa$, with $G$ a global well-order,
\[
   \kappa<\Theta_L<\kappa^+,
   \qquad \operatorname{cf}(\Theta_L)=\omega.
\]
Parameter-free $L$-definitions are cofinal in this interval of
parameter-definable types, although they realize only countably many
of its members.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Why the cofinal family does not create a largest notation}

Choose an external enumeration of the finite formula pairs, and denote
the resulting orders by $U_n$. For each standard $n$ its definition is
a finite formula, but the proof supplies no single $L$-formula that
evaluates all these definitions uniformly. Such a
uniform, $L$-definable cofinal family is impossible: its
$\omega$-indexed lexicographic sum followed by one new last point would
again be $L$-definable and would have ordertype larger than every member
of the supposedly cofinal family.

A stronger class collection may contain a uniform code for the family.
For example, the full collection $\mathcal P(V_\kappa)$ does. There is
no contradiction: using that additional class as a predicate enlarges
the language of permitted definitions. The obstruction concerns a
uniform code definable in the \emph{same fixed language}. One could
instead organize the construction using separate bounded-complexity
satisfaction predicates. They likewise do not assemble into a
definable full truth predicate for that language; the fixed-formula
proof shows that this additional machinery is unnecessary here.

Thus external countable cofinality is compatible with the impossibility
of internally listing a cofinal family by one definition. A research
question suggested by these results is to classify the ordinals
$\Theta_L$ obtainable from a fixed $V_\kappa$ as the named class
predicates vary, subject to amenability and the desired recursion
axioms. Another is to determine which restricted notation calculi are
cofinal in particular definability spectra. The present theorems give
necessary bounds and an explicit external construction; they do not
identify one absolute endpoint beyond $\Ord$.

\merge\ \Cref{swo:bo:spec:full} is source~12's full-class model
\cref{swo:st:thm:model}~(iv) (Part~V; extended to every limit height by
source~31, \cref{swo:gcz:thm:replacement}), proved again by sources~35, 32
and~33 (\cref{swo:fc:thm:full-spectrum,swo:dc:thm:fullspectrum,swo:dh:thm:fullspectrum}).
The definable ceilings of the four sources are one invariant. Over $V_\kappa$
with $\kappa$ inaccessible, source~32's $\delta_A$ is $\Theta_L$ for
$L=\{\in,G,A\}$ (\cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling}: its spectrum is the interval
$[0,\delta_A)$), source~33's $\delta_G$ and $\delta_G^0$ are $\Theta_L$ and
$\sup\mathcal S_0^L$ for $L=\{\in,G\}$ (\cref{swo:dh:thm:height}), and
source~35's $\delta_{\mathrm{set}}$ is $\Theta_L$ for the pure language
$L=\{\in\}$, by \cref{swo:bo:spec:interval} applied in the full model
(\cref{swo:fc:thm:definability-spectrum}). \Cref{swo:bo:spec:cofinal} is the
most general form, for any transitive $\beta$-model of $\GBC$ with a named
global well-order; sources~32 and~33 prove the case $V_\kappa$, and source~32
adds $\kappa^{\delta_A}=\delta_A$, source~33 the closure under ordinal
arithmetic. Together they answer in part source~31's \cref{swo:gcz:n7}
(\cref{swo:xvi:sec:qstatus}).

% ---- source 35, its Sections 9.1--9.3 (Sections 9.4--9.5 are printed in Section XVI.10)
\subsection{Source 35: external lengths: the full-model spectrum and definability-sensitive cutoffs}

% ---- source 35 (batch-96 manuscript 11), lines 2419-2449
\label{swo:fc:sec:formalization}

The constructions above are meaningful internally, without assigning a set
ordinal to a proper class order.  An ambient set universe can nevertheless
measure their lengths when the entire class model is a set there.  Keeping
these two viewpoints separate gives a precise answer to ``how far beyond
$\Ord$?'' and prevents an external cardinal bound from becoming an internal
largest notation.

\subsubsection{The exact full-model spectrum}

Work in an ambient universe satisfying $\mathsf{ZFC}$, and let $\kappa$ be
strongly inaccessible.  Consider the two-sorted structure
\[
 \mathcal M_\kappa=(V_\kappa,\mathcal P(V_\kappa)).
\]
Its sets are the elements of $V_\kappa$; its classes are \emph{all ambient
subsets} of $V_\kappa$, with the appropriate tagged copies if the two sorts
are formally disjoint.  This notation does not assert that
$\mathcal P(V_\kappa)$ is a set or a class \emph{inside} $\mathcal M_\kappa$.
Relations and functions use the usual set codes for ordered pairs.

This structure satisfies $\KM$ with Global Choice.  Full comprehension
holds because every subset of the first-order universe is available.
For Class Replacement, if $a\in V_\kappa$ and a class function has domain
$a$, its image has cardinality less than $\kappa$.  Regularity bounds the
ranks of its elements below $\kappa$, so the image belongs to $V_\kappa$.
A bijection between $\kappa$ and $V_\kappa$ in the ambient universe provides
Global Choice.  Here the identity $|V_\kappa|=\kappa$ uses strong
inaccessibility.

\begin{note}[Source~35, Theorem~9.1, ``Full external spectrum'']\label{swo:fc:thm:full-spectrum}
\emph{The external order types of class well-orders in $\mathcal M_\kappa$
are exactly the ordinals $\theta<\kappa^+$: those of sets are the
$\theta<\kappa$, those of proper classes the $\theta$ with
$\kappa\le\theta<\kappa^+$. The same proper-class spectrum is obtained if the
carrier is required to be exactly $\Ord^{\mathcal M_\kappa}=\kappa$.} This is
source~34's \cref{swo:bo:spec:full} and source~12's \cref{swo:st:thm:model}~(iv),
by the same cardinality and regularity count; source~35 adds the last sentence
(transport to the carrier $\kappa$ by an ambient bijection) and that internal
and external well-foundedness agree because every external witness of
ill-foundedness is an available class.
\end{note}

% ---- source 35 (batch-96 manuscript 11), lines 2485-2512

In this example $\Omega$ has external length $\kappa$, while
$\Omega+1$, $\Omega\cdot 2$, and $\Omega^{[\Omega]}$ have the corresponding ordinary
ordinal lengths $\kappa+1$, $\kappa\cdot 2$, and $\kappa^\kappa$.
There is no conflict with the absence of a largest internal class
well-order.  The external ordinal $\kappa^+$ is not represented by a
class well-order in $\mathcal M_\kappa$, and the model does not possess
the collection of all its classes as a same-level object.  This full
spectrum is background already present in the repository; the next
refinement records the effect of restricting definitions.

\subsubsection{Definability changes the external ceiling}

Use the fixed countable language $\{\in\}$.  A presentation consists of
formulas for its carrier and relation, evaluated over $V_\kappa$.
Let $S_0$, $S_{\mathrm{ord}}$, and $S_{\mathrm{set}}$ be the external
sets of order types of genuine well-orders with presentations using,
respectively, no parameters, finitely many ordinal parameters, and
finitely many arbitrary set parameters from $V_\kappa$.  Put
\[
 \delta_0=\sup S_0,\qquad
 \delta_{\mathrm{ord}}=\sup S_{\mathrm{ord}},\qquad
 \delta_{\mathrm{set}}=\sup S_{\mathrm{set}}.
\]
These are definitions in the ambient universe, which has the satisfaction
relation of the set structure $V_\kappa$.  They are not proposed as
uniform truth definitions inside $V_\kappa$.

\merge\ In \cref{swo:fc:thm:definability-spectrum}, $\delta_{\mathrm{set}}$ is
$\Theta_L$ for $L=\{\in\}$ and the set-parameter spectrum is the interval
$[0,\delta_{\mathrm{set}})$, by source~34's \cref{swo:bo:spec:interval} applied
to the full model, which is a $\GBC$ realization containing the predicate;
$\cf(\delta_0)=\omega$ is also there. Whether the inequalities
$\delta_0\le\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\le\delta_{\mathrm{set}}$ are strict in the
pure language, and $\cf(\delta_{\mathrm{set}})$, stay open; with a named global
well-order the analogue of $\delta_0=\delta_{\mathrm{set}}$ holds
(\cref{swo:bo:spec:cofinal}; \cref{swo:dh:thm:height}). The reflection-tree
example below is the standard mechanism of Hamkins's answer to Glazer's
MathOverflow question, as source~35 says; it is not new.

% ---- source 35 (batch-96 manuscript 11), lines 2513-2618
\begin{theorem}[Definability-sensitive spectrum bounds]
\label{swo:fc:thm:definability-spectrum}
With these conventions,
\[
 \kappa<\delta_0\leq\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}
       \leq\delta_{\mathrm{set}}<\kappa^+,
 \qquad \operatorname{cf}(\delta_0)=\omega.
\]
None of the three spectra has a maximum.  Each of the other two suprema
has cofinality at most $\kappa$.  Allowing arbitrary class parameters
instead recovers the full spectrum of \Cref{swo:fc:thm:full-spectrum}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
There are countably many parameter-free formula pairs, and at most
$\kappa$ formula pairs with finite parameters from $V_\kappa$.  The same
bound holds for ordinal parameters.  Thus
\[
 |S_0|\leq\aleph_0,\qquad
 |S_{\mathrm{ord}}|\leq\kappa,\qquad
 |S_{\mathrm{set}}|\leq\kappa.
\]
Every member lies below $\kappa^+$ by
\Cref{swo:fc:thm:full-spectrum}.  The ambient successor cardinal
$\kappa^+$ is regular, so the supremum of at most $\kappa$ of its
members is still below $\kappa^+$.

Given any presentation of $A$, form the tagged carrier
$(\{0\}\times A)\cup\{(1,0)\}$, retaining the old order in the first
part and putting the new point last.  This defines $A+1$ with exactly
the same permitted parameters.  Its external type is strictly larger.
Hence no spectrum has a maximum.  A countable nonempty set of ordinals
without a largest member has a supremum of cofinality $\omega$.
The parameter-free presentation of $\Omega$ and its successors gives
$\delta_0>\kappa$.  Inclusion of the permitted parameter families gives
the remaining inequalities and cardinal bounds on cofinality.

If class parameters are unrestricted, use a carrier and its ordering
relation themselves as parameters.  Every class presentation is then
definable, so there is no remaining restriction.
\end{proof}

The same suprema result if one restricts to proper-class carriers:
given any definable set order, append a copy of $\Omega$ to obtain a
definable proper-class order of greater external type.  We make no
claim that the inequalities between the three definability suprema
are strict.  Their exact values require additional information about
$V_\kappa$.  In particular, the counting argument does not assign an
exact cofinality to $\delta_{\mathrm{set}}$.

It is also important not to identify these spectra with an automatic
$\GBC$ model $(V_\kappa,\operatorname{Def}(V_\kappa))$.  The definable
classes always give the expected elementary comprehension and
replacement, but a global well-order definable from a set parameter
need not exist.  The spectrum theorem takes place inside the full model
and merely restricts which presentations are counted.

\subsubsection{Internal well-foundedness and external well-foundedness}

For a class model $(M,\mathcal X)$, internal well-foundedness quantifies
over the subclasses in $\mathcal X$.  A transitive first-order universe
$M$ does not by itself make this equivalent to external well-foundedness.
The relevant additional correctness condition is the usual
$\beta$-model condition: relations declared well-founded internally must
be genuinely well-founded externally.

In $\GBC$, a class relation is well-founded if and only if it has no
descending $\omega$-sequence coded by a set.  For the nontrivial direction,
Global Choice recursively chooses a smaller member of any nonempty class
with no minimal member; Class Replacement collects the resulting
$\omega$-sequence.  Thus two $\GBC$ realizations with the same first-order
universe agree about well-foundedness of every relation they share.
This invariance concerns their \emph{internal} judgment, and does not
imply that judgment is externally correct.

Here is the standard reflection-tree mechanism giving a transitive
counterexample; compare Hamkins's answer in~\cite{xviGlazerMO}.
Assume a countable transitive model of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ exists, and choose
$M=L_\alpha$ of least possible height.  Fix a primitive recursive
increasing sequence $k_i$ large enough to cover the first $i$ axioms in a recursive
enumeration of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.  Let $T$ consist of finite increasing
ordinal sequences $(\beta_i)$ such that $L_{\beta_i}$ satisfies those
axioms and
\[
 L_{\beta_i}\prec_{\Sigma_{k_i}}L_{\beta_{i+1}}
 \quad\text{whenever both entries occur.}
\]
This is definable using satisfaction for set structures.  Reflection
produces an external infinite branch.  An $M$-set branch would have
$\lambda=\sup_i\beta_i<\alpha$; eventual elementarity for every formula
would give $L_\lambda\models\mathsf{ZFC}$, contradicting minimality.
The Kleene--Brouwer order of $T$, with extensions preceding their prefixes,
is therefore internally well-founded but externally ill-founded in
$(M,\operatorname{Def}(M))$.  Internally, a descending sequence would
yield a branch by successive coordinate stabilization.  Externally, the
branch itself yields descending finite prefixes.

The inaccessible-height situation is much better.  Every ambient
$\omega$-sequence of elements of $V_\kappa$ belongs to $V_\kappa$:
regularity bounds its coordinate ranks, and the graph then has rank
below $\kappa$.  Consequently \emph{any} $\GBC$ realization with
first-order universe $V_\kappa$ is correct about well-foundedness of its
admitted relations.  This gives a second proof of the correctness used
in \Cref{swo:fc:thm:full-spectrum}, and explains exactly why that
external calculation is safe.

% ---- source 32, its Section 8
\subsection{Source 32: external spectra and the ceiling of definability}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 520-546
\label{swo:dc:sec:spectrum}

We now give a precise model-relative answer to ``how much farther than $\Ord$?'' This section takes place in an external ZFC metatheory and assumes a strongly inaccessible cardinal $\kappa$. This is a sufficient setting for the results, not a claim that such a cardinal follows from ZFC or is necessary for every related phenomenon.

Put $M=V_\kappa$. Fix a class predicate $G$ coding a bijection $\kappa\to V_\kappa$, and let $A\subseteq V_\kappa$ be an arbitrary additional predicate. Tuples and relations may be coded as unary predicates using ordinary set pairing. Define
\[\tag{S32.11}
\label{swo:dc:eq:defclasses}
\mathcal X_A=\Def(V_\kappa;\in,G,A),
\]
where \emph{all set parameters from $V_\kappa$ are allowed}. The parameters $G,A$ are fixed; they are not varied separately for each definition within this one class realization.

The distinction between different admitted class collections over one set universe is central in work on class-theoretic potentialism \cite{xviBartonWilliams}. Here it lets us isolate a numerical invariant of definability rather than assigning an absolute length to ``the definable classes'' without specifying a language or a model.

\subsubsection{Why this setting has honest external well-orders}

\begin{lemma}[The inaccessible-rank model]
\label{swo:dc:lem:rankmodel}
Both $(V_\kappa,\mathcal X_A)$ and $(V_\kappa,\mathcal P(V_\kappa))$ satisfy GBC. For every class relation on $V_\kappa$, its internal class well-foundedness in either model is equivalent to external well-foundedness.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The set structure $V_\kappa$ satisfies ZFC. A subset of any $x\in V_\kappa$ belongs to $V_\kappa$, so separation with arbitrary class predicates holds. If a class function is evaluated on a set $x\in V_\kappa$, then $|x|<\kappa$. Its values form fewer than $\kappa$ many sets of rank below $\kappa$. Regularity of $\kappa$ bounds all their ranks below $\kappa$, so the image belongs to $V_\kappa$. This verifies Class Replacement even for arbitrary external class predicates. The predicate $G$ gives Global Choice. For $\mathcal X_A$, elementary comprehension holds by substituting the definitions of its finitely many class parameters; for the full power set it is automatic.

Every external sequence $f:\omega\to V_\kappa$ belongs to $V_\kappa$: the ranks of its countably many values have supremum below $\kappa$, and its graph then has rank below $\kappa$. Consequently an external descending $\omega$-sequence is an internal set witness to failure of well-foundedness. Conversely an internal descending sequence is certainly external. External dependent choice and \cref{swo:dc:lem:descending} give the equivalence.
\end{proof}

The last assertion is not valid for arbitrary countable or nonstandard models. Such models may admit internally well-founded presentations that are externally ill-founded. We use the inaccessible setting precisely to rule out that ambiguity, rather than silently identifying internal and external order types everywhere.

\begin{note}[Source~32, Theorem~8.2, ``The full-class spectrum'']\label{swo:dc:thm:fullspectrum}
\emph{In $(V_\kappa,\mathcal P(V_\kappa))$, the external order types of class
well-orders are exactly the ordinals below $\kappa^+$, and those of
proper-class well-orders exactly
\[\tag{S32.12}\label{swo:dc:eq:fullspectrum}
 [\kappa,\kappa^+).
\]
The set-like proper-class type is $\kappa$, the
external type of the internal $\Omega$.} This is source~34's
\cref{swo:bo:spec:full} and source~12's \cref{swo:st:thm:model}~(iv), with the
same proof.
\end{note}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 561-615

Thus full second-order semantics produces every length below the next external cardinal, not merely finite expressions in $\kappa$. It does not produce a greatest type: $\kappa^+$ is a supremum outside the range, not an extra class ordinal in that model. Restricting to definable classes produces a much smaller, structured ceiling.

\subsubsection{The definability ceiling theorem}

Let $S_A$ be the external set of ordinal types of the $\mathcal X_A$-admitted class well-orders. There are only a set of these presentations externally, so the following definition is ordinary metatheoretic set formation:
\[\tag{S32.13}
\label{swo:dc:eq:ceilingdef}
\delta_A=\sup\{\beta+1:\beta\in S_A\}.
\]

\begin{theorem}[Definability ceiling]
\label{swo:dc:thm:ceiling}
The realized spectrum is exactly the initial segment
\[\tag{S32.14}
\label{swo:dc:eq:spectrumdelta}
S_A=\{\beta:\beta<\delta_A\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[\tag{S32.15}
\label{swo:dc:eq:deltafacts}
\kappa<\delta_A<\kappa^+,
\qquad \cf(\delta_A)=\omega,
\qquad \kappa^{\delta_A}=\delta_A,
\]
where the exponentiation and cofinality in \eqref{swo:dc:eq:deltafacts} are external ordinal operations. In particular, $\delta_A$ is not itself represented by any class well-order in $\mathcal X_A$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\emph{Initiality and no last type.} Suppose $\beta\in S_A$, represented by $W$, and $\gamma<\beta$. The point of $W$ at external position $\gamma$ is an element $x\in V_\kappa$. Restricting $W$ below $x$ is definable with the additional allowed set parameter $x$ and has type $\gamma$. Thus $S_A$ is downward closed. It is closed under successor because $W+1$ is a definable class presentation. Therefore it has no largest member, and it is exactly the initial segment in \eqref{swo:dc:eq:spectrumdelta}. Its supremum is not represented. The internal ordinal class has external type $\kappa$, so $\kappa\in S_A$ and $\kappa<\delta_A$.

\emph{A countable cofinal sequence of bounds.} Externally enumerate all first-order formula pairs for domains and binary relations in the fixed finite language with $G,A$:
\[
(\varphi_0,\psi_0),(\varphi_1,\psi_1),\ldots.
\]
Each formula pair is arranged to use one code for its finite tuple of set parameters. For each ordinary natural number $n$, apply \cref{swo:dc:cor:finitesyntax} to the first $n+1$ pairs, with all such set parameters. Let $D_n$ be the resulting definable diagonal well-order and put
\[
\theta_n=\otp(D_n).
\]
Each $\theta_n$ belongs to $S_A$, so $\theta_n<\delta_A$. Every definable well-order $W$ uses some formula pair, say the $j$th. For all $n\geq j$, the diagonal theorem says that $W$ embeds into $D_n$ and that $D_n$ does not embed into $W$. These are actual external well-orders by \cref{swo:dc:lem:rankmodel}. Ordinary ordinal comparison therefore gives
\[
\otp(W)<\theta_n.
\]
Hence $(\theta_n)_{n<\omega}$ is externally cofinal in $\delta_A$.

Each $\theta_n<\kappa^+$ by \cref{swo:dc:thm:fullspectrum}. Since $\kappa^+$ is regular and uncountable, the supremum of this countable sequence is strictly below $\kappa^+$. The ordinal $\delta_A$ is a nonzero limit with no largest represented type, so a finite subset cannot be cofinal. Its cofinality is therefore exactly $\omega$.

\emph{Closure and the fixed-point equation.} If $\alpha,\beta\in S_A$ and $\alpha\geq2$, choose definable class presentations of those types. Their finite-support power is definable in the same structure and is a well-order by \cref{swo:dc:thm:power}. Externally its type is the ordinary ordinal $\alpha^\beta$, by \cref{swo:dc:lem:digits} applied in the external universe. Thus $S_A$ is closed under this exponentiation, as well as under sums and products.

In particular, since $\kappa\in S_A$, for every $\beta<\delta_A$ we have $\kappa^\beta<\delta_A$. Continuity of ordinary exponentiation at the limit $\delta_A$ gives
\[
\kappa^{\delta_A}=\sup_{\beta<\delta_A}\kappa^\beta\leq\delta_A.
\]
For every ordinal $\beta$ and base at least $2$, ordinary induction gives $\beta\leq\kappa^\beta$. Taking suprema yields the reverse inequality. This proves all of \eqref{swo:dc:eq:deltafacts}.
\end{proof}

\merge\ \Cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling} is source~34's \cref{swo:bo:spec:interval}
and \cref{swo:bo:spec:inaccessible-relative} at $V_\kappa$ for the language
$\{\in,G,A\}$, by a different route: source~34 bounds each formula pair by its
own parameter-free sum, source~32 by the diagonals of finite lists of formula
pairs (\cref{swo:dc:cor:finitesyntax}). The equation $\kappa^{\delta_A}=\delta_A$
is proved here only by source~32; source~33's \cref{swo:dh:cor:heightclosure}
adds $\omega^{\delta}=\delta$ and closure under ordinal arithmetic.
\Cref{swo:dc:cor:ceilingsvary} is proved only by source~32.

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 616-647
\begin{remark}[What the ceiling does and does not mean]\label{swo:dc:n8.4}
The spectrum statement uses set parameters essentially: they permit restriction below an arbitrary point of a presentation. It is not a theorem about parameter-free definability. Likewise, ``definable with arbitrary class parameters'' would mean something different if the class parameter were allowed to change separately for each presentation. Here $A$ and $G$ are fixed before $\delta_A$ is formed.

The countable sequence $(D_n)$ above is at this point an \emph{external sequence of individually admitted classes}. It is not asserted to be a single $\mathcal X_A$-admitted family. If it were such a family, its sum could already reach the forbidden ceiling. The distinction is not bookkeeping: it is exactly where truth enters.
\end{remark}

\subsubsection{Further structural consequences}

\begin{corollary}
\label{swo:dc:cor:ceilingsvary}
For fixed $\kappa$ and $G$, the ordinals $\delta_A$, as $A\subseteq V_\kappa$ varies, are unbounded in $\kappa^+$. More precisely,
\[
\sup_{A\subseteq V_\kappa}\delta_A=\kappa^+.
\]
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Given $\theta<\kappa^+$, transfer a well-order of type $\theta$ to a subset of $V_\kappa$ and code its domain and relation in one unary predicate $A$. That order is then definable from $A$, so $\theta\in S_A$ and $\theta<\delta_A$. The reverse bound follows from \cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling} for each $A$.
\end{proof}

The necessary conditions $\cf(\delta_A)=\omega$ and $\kappa^{\delta_A}=\delta_A$ are not a classification of possible ceilings. In fact the spectrum is closed under more than ordinary exponentiation: it is closed under every fixed finite presentation constructor developed here, including $A\mapsto\Eps(A)$. Determining which such closure properties are sufficient, or how these ordinals are related to other definability invariants, remains a substantive question.

A useful schematic comparison is therefore
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{admitted presentations over }V_\kappa&\text{external spectrum}\\\hline
\text{set-like class well-orders}&\{\beta:\beta\leq\kappa\}\\
\Def(V_\kappa;G,A)\text{ well-orders}&\{\beta:\beta<\delta_A\}\\
\text{all class well-orders}&\{\beta:\beta<\kappa^+\}.
\end{array}
\]
In the first row the set-order types are below $\kappa$, and the single proper set-like type is $\kappa$. In the other rows many different non-set-like types appear. None of these external spectra is being asserted to be an admitted universal family in the model it describes.

% ---- source 32, its Section 9
\subsection{Source 32: a truth predicate reaches the old ceiling exactly}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 649-685
\label{swo:dc:sec:truth}

Let $T_A$ be the full satisfaction predicate for the \emph{set-sized external structure} $(V_\kappa,\in,G,A)$, with finite assignments coded in $V_\kappa$. Such a predicate exists externally and is an element of $\mathcal P(V_\kappa)$. It is not definable in that same structure with set parameters, by the usual diagonal argument for truth. Form the enlarged definable class realization
\[
\mathcal X_{T_A}=\Def(V_\kappa;\in,G,T_A).
\]
The predicate $A$ is recoverable from the truth values of its atomic formulas, so $\mathcal X_A\subseteq\mathcal X_{T_A}$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact truth presentation and strict jump]
\label{swo:dc:thm:truth}
There is an $\mathcal X_{T_A}$-definable class well-order whose external type is exactly $\delta_A$. Consequently,
\[\tag{S32.16}
\label{swo:dc:eq:truthjump}
\delta_A<\delta_{T_A}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Use the fixed external effective enumeration of formula pairs from the proof of \cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling}. In the language with $T_A$, evaluation of these pairs is uniform in their natural-number codes and set parameters. Validity of each evaluated fiber is still an elementary condition, by \cref{swo:dc:lem:descending}; its external correctness follows from \cref{swo:dc:lem:rankmodel}. Fix once and for all the global ordering of the formula-tag and parameter-code index class obtained from $G$.

The diagonal construction for the first $n+1$ formula pairs can now be carried out uniformly in $n$. It gives one admitted family $(D_n)_{n<\omega}$ in $\mathcal X_{T_A}$. Its $n$th fiber is exactly the individually definable order used in the ceiling proof: for a fixed standard $n$, the finitely many evaluations can be replaced by their actual formulas, eliminating the truth predicate from that one fiber.

Define the class order
\[\tag{S32.17}
\label{swo:dc:eq:truthsum}
L=\sum_{n<\omega}(D_n+1).
\]
It is definable from $G,T_A$ and is a class well-order by \cref{swo:dc:prop:sums}. Every finite partial sum of \eqref{swo:dc:eq:truthsum} belongs to $\mathcal X_A$, because it involves only finitely many of the individually definable $D_n$. Thus each finite partial sum has external type strictly below $\delta_A$. Since these are nested initial segments whose union is $L$, continuity of the external ordinal sum gives
\[
\otp(L)\leq\delta_A.
\]
On the other hand, every $D_n$ embeds into $L$. The ordinals $\theta_n=\otp(D_n)$ are cofinal in $\delta_A$, so $\otp(L)\geq\delta_A$. Hence $\otp(L)=\delta_A$ exactly.

The new spectrum therefore contains $\delta_A$. It is successor closed and is the initial segment below its own ceiling, by \cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling} applied with $T_A$ as the extra predicate. This implies \eqref{swo:dc:eq:truthjump}.
\end{proof}

This theorem gives a precise interpretation of one step beyond a definability boundary. Truth does not merely yield some unrelated longer order. It assembles the formerly nonuniform finite-syntax bounds into a presentation of the old supremum itself. The construction is parallel in spirit to class-theoretic truth hierarchies, but its conclusion here follows from the explicit diagonal argument rather than from an assumed global iterated-truth principle.

\merge\ \Cref{swo:dc:thm:truth} is the strongest of the four truth results:
source~34's \cref{swo:bo:diag:truth} produces, internally and from an assumed
full satisfaction class, an order dominating every definable one; source~33's
\cref{swo:dh:thm:truthjump} shows at $V_\kappa$ that truth raises the height,
with the bounds of the new height; source~32 shows that truth represents the
old height exactly. Its \cref{swo:dc:n9.2} gives one family with no uniform
code, as source~33's \cref{swo:dh:cor:nodefcofinal} and source~34's
\cref{swo:bo:diag:bounded} do for theirs.

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 686-698
\begin{corollary}[The old bounds cannot have been uniformly admitted]\label{swo:dc:n9.2}
The particular family $(D_n)_{n<\omega}$ used above has no uniform code in $\mathcal X_A$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Such a code would make \eqref{swo:dc:eq:truthsum} an $\mathcal X_A$-admitted class well-order of type $\delta_A$, contradicting \cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling}.
\end{proof}

One can externally repeat the construction: set $A_0=A$ and let $A_{n+1}$ code the full truth predicate for the structure with $A_n$. Then
\[
\delta_{A_0}<\delta_{A_1}<\delta_{A_2}<\cdots<\kappa^+.
\]
Each individual step is covered by \cref{swo:dc:thm:truth}. This assertion does not automatically supply one admitted internal hierarchy of all these truth predicates; combining them is again a uniformity question. The same caution applies at limit stages.

% ---- source 33, its Section 9
\subsection{Source 33: external spectra, definability heights, and truth}\label{swo:dh:sec:spectra}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1153-1167

\subsubsection{A full-class model at an inaccessible cutoff}
In this section the surrounding metatheory is ordinary external $\ZFC$.
Assume $\kappa$ is strongly inaccessible and let
\[
                    M=V_\kappa,\qquad \mathcal X=\Pow(M).
\]
Relations and tuples are coded as elements of $M$, so writing all subclasses
as $\Pow(M)$ covers binary relations as well. The set structure $M$ satisfies
$\ZFC$. Every subset of $M$ is an available class in $(M,\mathcal X)$.
Full class comprehension holds externally. Class replacement holds because
a set of $M$ has external cardinality below $\kappa$, and regularity bounds
the ranks of fewer than $\kappa$ many output values. A global ordering can
be chosen externally and belongs to $\mathcal X$.

\begin{note}[Source~33, Lemma~9.1, ``Correct well-foundedness at the cutoff'']\label{swo:dh:lem:beta}
\emph{Every class well-order of $(V_\kappa,\mathcal P(V_\kappa))$ is externally
well-founded, and conversely every externally well-founded class order is
internally a well-order.} This is source~32's \cref{swo:dc:lem:rankmodel} for
the full model and source~34's $\beta$-model remark after \cref{swo:bo:spec:full}:
an external descending sequence of elements of $V_\kappa$ has ranks bounded
below $\kappa$ by regularity and uncountability, so it belongs to $V_\kappa$.
\end{note}

\begin{note}[Source~33, Theorem~9.2, ``Exact full-class spectrum'']\label{swo:dh:thm:fullspectrum}
\emph{In the full-class model, the external order types of class well-orders
are exactly
\[\tag{S33.9.1}\label{swo:dh:eq:fullspectrum}
 \{\alpha:\alpha<\kappa^+\};
\]
those with proper-class carriers exactly the $\alpha$ with
$\kappa\le\alpha<\kappa^+$; and the set-like proper-class order $\Omega^M$ has
external type $\kappa$.} This is source~34's \cref{swo:bo:spec:full}, with the
same proof.
\end{note}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1211-1241

The endpoint $\kappa^+$ is an external bound, not a last represented class
order. For each $\alpha<\kappa^+$, its successor still lies below
$\kappa^+$. This reconciles \cref{swo:dh:thm:fullspectrum} with the internal
no-greatest-order theorem.

\subsubsection{Arithmetic viewed from outside}
If a class exponent order $\Gamma$ has external type $\gamma$, the
finite-support construction has external type
\[\tag{S33.9.2}\label{swo:dh:eq:externalpower}
                            \otp(P(\Gamma))=\kappa^\gamma,
\]
where the exponent on the right is \emph{ordinal} exponentiation. Indeed,
all exponent points and ordinal coefficients below $\kappa$ are available
as elements of $M$, and every finite code on them belongs to $M$.
The external collapse is the ordinary finite-support presentation of that
ordinal power.

All powers in \eqref{swo:dh:eq:externalpower} still lie below $\kappa^+$ when
$\gamma<\kappa^+$: their finite-support presentations have cardinality
at most $\kappa$. This gives a concrete sense in which very long ordinal
expressions can have the same underlying class size.

For the fixed point of \cref{swo:dh:thm:fixedpoint}, set
\[
              t_0=\kappa,\qquad t_{n+1}=\kappa^{t_n}.
\]
Its external type is $\sup_{n<\omega}t_n$. Continuity of ordinal
exponentiation shows that this is the least fixed point of
$\xi\mapsto\kappa^\xi$ above $\kappa$. It is still below $\kappa^+$.

\merge\ The external type \eqref{swo:dh:eq:externalpower} is source~29's
full-model check after \cref{swo:bw:ch:surreal-suffices} and source~34's
substitution rule in \cref{swo:bo:sec:formalization}; the type
$\sup_n t_n$ of the fixed point is source~34's \cref{swo:bo:her:calibration},
$\varepsilon_{\kappa+1}$.

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1242-1260
\subsubsection{The smaller definable spectrum}
Fix a set-like global ordering $G$ in the full class model and let
$\Def(M;G)$ consist of all first-order definable subclasses using $G$
and finite tuples of parameters from $M$. This is a legitimate
$\GBC$ class realization: comprehension is built into the definition,
and replacement follows from the same rank and cardinality bound used
above. Its well-orders are externally correct by the proof of
\cref{swo:dh:lem:beta}.

Define, externally,
\[\tag{S33.9.3}\label{swo:dh:eq:delta}
 \delta_G=\sup\{\otp(W):W\text{ has a first-order }G\text{-definable
                          presentation with set parameters in }M\}.
\]
Let $\delta_G^0$ be the same supremum with no set parameters. This
supremum is a set ordinal in the external metatheory. We make no claim
that it is an ordinal or a represented well-order of the definable class
model itself.

\begin{note}[Source~33, Theorem~9.3, ``Countably cofinal definability height'']\label{swo:dh:thm:height}
\emph{Under the inaccessible-rank hypotheses,
\[\tag{S33.9.4}\label{swo:dh:eq:height}
 \delta_G^0=\delta_G,\qquad \kappa<\delta_G<\kappa^+,\qquad \cf(\delta_G)=\omega.
\]
No $G$-definable class well-order has type $\delta_G$.
The full class model does have a class well-order of that external type.} This
is source~34's \cref{swo:bo:spec:cofinal} and \cref{swo:bo:spec:inaccessible-relative}
for $L=\{\in,G\}$, with $\delta_G=\Theta_L$ and $\delta_G^0=\sup\mathcal S_0^L$.
The proof differs: source~34 bounds the instances of one formula pair by one
parameter-free sum; source~33 uses the diagonals $D_n$ of its
\cref{swo:dh:thm:bounded}, one for each complexity level. It is printed as a
second route. The last sentence is source~34's \cref{swo:bo:spec:full}.
\end{note}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1271-1296
\begin{proof}[Source~33's proof]
For each external standard $n$, interpret the parameter-free formula
for $D_n$ from \cref{swo:dh:thm:bounded} in $(M,\in,G)$, and let
$d_n=\otp(D_n)$. The order is externally well-founded. Every
$G$-definable presentation has a fixed standard finite formula complexity,
so it embeds into some $D_n$. Conversely every $D_n$ is itself
$G$-definable without set parameters. Therefore
\[
                         \delta_G=\delta_G^0=\sup_{n<\omega}d_n.
\]
Every $d_n<\kappa^+$ by \cref{swo:dh:thm:fullspectrum}. The successor cardinal
$\kappa^+$ is regular in the external metatheory, so the supremum of
this countable sequence is still strictly below $\kappa^+$.

The definable spectrum has no largest type: taking a tagged successor is
a definable operation and strictly increases external ordinal type.
Thus its supremum is not attained and has no finite cofinal subset.
The countable cofinal family above gives $\cf(\delta_G)=\omega$.
The definable orders $\Omega+1$ and their further successors show that
$\delta_G>\kappa$.

Nonattainment follows again from successor closure. Since
$\delta_G<\kappa^+$, the full-class spectrum theorem supplies a full
class well-order with that type, though not a $G$-definable one.
\end{proof}

\merge\ \Cref{swo:dh:cor:heightclosure} extends source~32's
$\kappa^{\delta_A}=\delta_A$ (\cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling}) to closure under
ordinal sum, product and power and to $\omega^{\delta_G}=\delta_G$. The same
argument gives $\omega^{\Theta_L}=\Theta_L$, and $\theta^{\Theta_L}=\Theta_L$ for the
external type $\theta$ of $\Ord^M$, for every transitive $\beta$-model and
language of \cref{swo:bo:spec:interval}: the parameter spectrum is the interval
$[0,\Theta_L)$; finite-support powers of $L$-definable presentations are
$L$-definable with the joined parameters; and their external types are the
ordinal powers, because the model contains every finite partial function
between its sets and is correct about well-foundedness. \Cref{swo:dh:thm:truthjump}
is weaker than source~32's \cref{swo:dc:thm:truth} on exactness and adds the
upper bound and cofinality of the new height.

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1297-1400
\begin{corollary}[Arithmetic closure of the definability ceiling]\label{swo:dh:cor:heightclosure}
For all external ordinals $\alpha,\beta<\delta_G$,
\[
        \alpha+\beta<\delta_G,\qquad
        \alpha\cdot\beta<\delta_G,\qquad
        \alpha^\beta<\delta_G.
\]
Moreover,
\[\tag{S33.9.5}\label{swo:dh:eq:deltafixed}
                         \omega^{\delta_G}
                         =\kappa^{\delta_G}
                         =\delta_G.
\]
In particular, $\delta_G$ is an external epsilon number, not just an
unspecified ordinal of countable cofinality.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Let $S$ be the spectrum whose supremum is $\delta_G$. Given
$\alpha,\beta<\delta_G$, choose $a,b\in S$ with $a\geq\max(2,\alpha)$
and $b\geq\beta$. The explicit sum, product, and power constructions
preserve first-order definability, allowing the two original parameter
tuples together. Their external types are $a+b$, $a\cdot b$, and
$a^b$, respectively. Each belongs to $S$ and is strictly below its
unattained supremum. Monotonicity of ordinary ordinal arithmetic gives
the first three inequalities; zero and one cause no difficulty.

For $\lambda=\omega$ or $\kappa$, the base order of type $\lambda$
is definable, and $\lambda^a\in S$ whenever $a\in S$.
Continuity in the exponent and cofinality of $S$ give
\[
                    \lambda^{\delta_G}
                      =\sup_{a\in S}\lambda^a\leq\delta_G.
\]
Ordinal exponentiation with base at least two satisfies
$\lambda^\xi\geq\xi$, as follows by transfinite induction. Hence equality
holds. The case $\lambda=\omega$ is the epsilon-number assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Two different cofinalities]\label{swo:dh:n9.5}
The equality $\cf(\delta_G)=\omega$ is entirely external. It does not
say that the internal class $\Ord^M$ has a countable cofinal sequence.
Indeed $\Ord^M$ has external type $\kappa$, which is regular and
uncountable. Nor does it provide a $G$-definable uniform sequence of
relations cofinal in the definable spectrum; \cref{swo:dh:cor:nodefcofinal}
forbids exactly that uniformization.
\end{remark}

\subsubsection{Truth strictly raises the definability height}
A full first-order truth predicate for $(M,\in,G)$ is an external subset
of the class of formula-assignment codes, so it belongs to the full class
part. Call it $T$. It evaluates formulas of $\mathcal L_G$; it does
\emph{not} evaluate formulas of the expanded language containing $T$
itself.

\begin{theorem}[A strict truth jump in order height]\label{swo:dh:thm:truthjump}
Let $\delta_{G,T}$ be the definability height in the fixed expanded
language $\{\in,G,T\}$, allowing set parameters. Then
\[\tag{S33.9.6}\label{swo:dh:eq:truthjump}
                    \delta_G<\delta_{G,T}<\kappa^+,
                    \qquad\cf(\delta_{G,T})=\omega.
\]
The two class realizations have exactly the same set universe and the
same set ordinals.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Using $T$, all $G$-formula pairs together with all finite parameter tuples
can now be evaluated in one uniform family, with no bounded-complexity
restriction. Apply the first-order well-orderhood test from
\cref{swo:dh:lem:wftest} to each decoded relation and replace failures by the
empty order. The resulting family is $G,T$-definable and contains every
$G$-definable class well-order.

Let $K$ be its diagonal sum of successor fibers. Every $G$-definable
well-order embeds into $K$, so externally $\otp(K)\geq\delta_G$.
The $G,T$-definable successor $K+1$ has type strictly greater than
$\delta_G$. Hence $\delta_{G,T}>\delta_G$.

The proof of \cref{swo:dh:thm:height} applies verbatim to any fixed finite
collection of named predicates whose class realization satisfies $\GBC$.
At $V_\kappa$ the rank argument supplies this requirement for $G,T$.
It gives the remaining bound and cofinality in \eqref{swo:dh:eq:truthjump}.
No sets were added; only the allowed class definitions were enlarged.
\end{proof}

This result makes precise a form of ``farther than Ord'' that cannot be
captured merely by listing longer ordinal expressions. The height of
attainable \emph{definable} order types can increase while the set
ordinals, all sets, and even the ambient full-class spectrum remain fixed.
The role of truth expansion is consistent with the broader potentialist
view of changing class resources over a fixed set model \cite{xviBartonWilliams}.

\subsubsection{What fails outside the full inaccessible model}
For any set-sized external model with carrier $M$, genuinely
well-founded orders on subsets of $M$ have external type below
$|M|^+$. Equality with the full interval of types need not follow.
The class part may omit many relations, the set model may not be
externally correct about well-foundedness, and small external subsets
of $M$ need not be sets of $M$.

Accordingly, neither the exact interval \eqref{swo:dh:eq:fullspectrum} nor the
specific cutoff $\kappa$ should be asserted for arbitrary models of
$\GBC$ or $\KM$. The inaccessible construction is an explicit semantic
laboratory, not an additional hypothesis smuggled into the elementary
$\GBC$ theorems of the earlier sections.

% ---- source 34 (batch-96 manuscript 10), lines 1867-1944
\section{How far the constructions reach, and what requires more axioms}
\label{swo:bo:sec:reach}

The preceding results give several answers to ``how much farther than
$\Ord$?'' They answer different versions of the question and should not
be compressed into a single purported largest class ordinal.

First, elementary presentations already go beyond every fixed finite
combination of ordinal blocks. If $\alpha$ is a set ordinal, the
power $\Omega^{[\alpha]}$ is a definable class well-order, and these
are proper initial segments of $\Omega^{[\Omega]}$. Iterating the
same finite-support constructor inside hereditary syntax gives
\[
\Omega,\quad \Omega^{[\Omega]},\quad
\Omega^{[\Omega^{[\Omega]}]},\quad\ldots
\]
as proper initial segments of $\Eps$. Appending an endpoint or a
new block to $\Eps$ immediately gives further orders. None of
these explicit constructions requires the existence of an unknown
class-valued transfinite history.

Second, no single uniform family is cofinal among all class well-orders
under order embedding. This is stronger than saying that there is no
largest element: it blocks a catalog indexed by sets with one uniform
evaluation relation. A syntax can describe an enormous domain and still
have a definable extension outside its reach.

Third, definability imposes a relative ceiling in an external model.
For a fixed transitive $\beta$-model and a fixed finite collection of
named predicates, the set-parameter definable order types form an
initial segment $[0,\Theta)$. Naming a suitable truth predicate
strictly enlarges the range available in that language. Under a named
global well-order, $\Theta$ has external cofinality $\omega$.
This does not make $\Theta$ countable, nor does it make the external
cofinal sequence an admitted uniform class sequence.

Fourth, under the full interpretation over $V_\kappa$, the precise
external ceiling for all class presentations is $\kappa^+$. This
bound is relative to the chosen universe. It is not an absolute
object that can be appended to $\Ord$ inside the original theory.
The difference between explicit definability and arbitrary available
classes is responsible for the difference between $\Theta$ and
$\kappa^+$.

\subsection{The comparison and recursion boundary}

The established class-recursion literature supplies the implications
\[
\GBC+\ETR\ \vdash\ \CWO,
\qquad
\GBC+\ETR\ \vdash\ \CTH.
\]
The first follows by recursively matching the least unmatched points
of two orders; the second also follows from the defining elementary
recursion for the history. Gitman and Hamkins identify full $\ETR$
with clopen class-game determinacy and, in its full all-length
formulation, with iterated elementary truth. Gitman, Hamkins, Holy,
Schlicht, and Williams identify $\ETR_{\Ord}$ with the class
forcing theorem \cite{GitmanHamkins,GHHSW}. These are theorems
about stronger existence principles, not prerequisites for the
finite graph manipulations used here.

For fixed small lengths, iteration conventions matter. For example,
$\ETR_1$ is just an elementary comprehension instance; the existence
of one full truth predicate is already a stronger assertion.
We therefore do not replace the all-length equivalence by the
unqualified formula ``$\ETR_\Gamma$ equals $\Gamma$-iterated
truth'' for every $\Gamma$.

There is also a useful boundary between arbitrary rankings and
continuous rankings. Hamkins and Woodin prove that every well-founded
class relation has a ranking into some class well-order over
$\GBC^-$, while $\ETR$ supplies continuous rankings. Their comparison
question asks whether appropriate converse implications hold
\cite[Theorems 4--6 and Question 7]{HamkinsWoodin}. The present
$\GB$ refinement identifies the strength of the particular
condensation-history principle with $\CWO$; it does not convert
all elementary class recursions into finite normal forms.

\merge\ The implications displayed above are recorded by all four sources and
by this report (\cref{swo:bw:ch:equivalence} and the paragraph after it).
Source~34's last sentence identifies the strength of the condensation-history
principle with $\CWO$ over $\GB$ (\cref{swo:bo:hist:equivalence}); with
source~35's \cref{swo:fc:cor:FPE-CWO} and \cref{swo:xvi:thm:choicefree}, the
fixed-point extension principle $\FPE$ is a further equivalent over $\GB$.
Whether $\CWO$ implies $\ETR$ is Hamkins and Woodin's Question~7, which no
source settles (\cref{swo:xvi:sec:questions}).

% ---- source 35, its Section 8
\subsection{Source 35: the boundary between comparison and class recursion}

% ---- source 35 (batch-96 manuscript 11), lines 2316-2412
\label{swo:fc:sec:recursion-boundary}

The preceding constructions use elementary comprehension, set-valued
recursion, and Class Replacement.  They do not solve arbitrary
recursions whose individual stages are classes.  For an elementary
formula \(\varphi(x,i,F,A)\) and a class well-order \(\Gamma\),
a class recursion asks for a single class \(F\) satisfying
\[
 F_i=\{x:\varphi(x,i,F\mathbin{\upharpoonright}\Gamma_{<i},A)\}
                    \qquad(i\in\Gamma).
\]
The earlier history on the right may be a proper class, even when
\(i\) has a set of predecessors.  This is the content of
elementary transfinite recursion, \(\ETR\), rather than the ordinary
set-valued recursion theorem.

Over \(\GBC\), \(\ETR\) is equivalent to the existence, for every
class parameter and every class well-order, of an iterated first-order
truth predicate along that order.  It is also equivalent to
determinacy of clopen games on classes
\cite[Theorems~8--9]{GitmanHamkins}.
This supplies a precise reason to track the formalism when writing
an iteration beyond \(\Ord\): the length and the type of the values
are separate resources.

For a fixed \(\Gamma\), \(\GBC+\ETR_\Gamma\) proves that \(\Gamma\)
is comparable with every class well-order by initial-segment
embeddings.  One recursively matches each point of \(\Gamma\) with
the least unmatched point of the other order; if that construction
stops, its inverse supplies the opposite comparison
\cite[Lemma~3.17]{Williams}.  Finite concatenations of the
same recursion length add no strength, because the solution on one
piece can be used as a parameter for the next.  This observation
does not justify a uniform iteration over all finite pieces.

The distinction is already visible at the important fragment
\(\ETR_{\Ord}\).  Over \(\GBC\), it is equivalent to the class
forcing theorem and to the existence of \(\Ord\)-iterated truth
predicates, among several other formulations
\cite[Main Theorem]{GHHSW}.  These are established calibration
theorems.  They do not identify arbitrary well-order comparability
with full \(\ETR\).

The name ``elementary transfinite recursion'' also occurs in a
different weak-set-theory setting.  Frittaion and Genovesi prove that
their first-order theory \(\mathbf C\), which includes Axiom Beta,
proves \(\Delta_0\) transfinite recursion and generates relativized
constructible hierarchies \cite{xviFrittaionGenovesi}.  Their base
theory and recursion scheme differ from the class-valued scheme
displayed above.  Applying that result to the present comparison
problem would require an explicit interpretation and a proof that
the relevant class solutions are obtained; the shared terminology
alone supplies no such implication.

For clarity, the established implication chain over \(\GBC\), and
over the weaker \(\mathrm{GBC}^{-}\) base used in the cited paper, is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \ETR
 &\ \Longrightarrow\
 \text{continuous rankings for all well-founded class relations}\\
 &\ \Longrightarrow\ \CWO\\
 &\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{weak class-well-order comparability}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here a continuous ranking assigns to a point the least available rank
strictly exceeding every predecessor rank; weak comparability permits
arbitrary suborder embeddings.  Hamkins and Woodin establish the
first two implications in their Theorems~5--6 and ask in Question~7
whether the displayed principles are equivalent
\cite{HamkinsWoodin}.  The present article neither proves those
converses nor treats the repository's condensation characterization
of \(\CWO\) as a proof of them.

Another independent distinction concerns the ambient model.
Two externally isomorphic orders need not have their isomorphism
available in a specified class realization.  Glazer's question
about definable class well-orders explicitly separates genuine
external well-foundedness from internal recognition, and separates
external isomorphism from definability of the isomorphism
\cite{xviGlazerMO}.  Its discussion includes a truth-encoding proposal
at length \(\Ord^\omega\); we do not require that proposal as a lemma
here.  The bounds and separation theorems above are proved directly
for admitted classes and maps.  In a \(\beta\)-correct realization,
their selected well-orders are also genuine external well-orders.
Without that correctness hypothesis an internally valid construction
may have an externally ill-founded interpretation.

These qualifications suggest a workable formalization policy.
Store a notation, its carrier, its comparison relation, and its
well-foundedness proof as separate data.  State whether an interpreter
is one available class or an external formula scheme.  Record
initial-segment embeddings separately from arbitrary embeddings,
and require an explicit history when class-valued iteration is used.
With these distinctions, long notations remain useful while their
limits are mathematical theorems rather than hidden changes of
universe or truth resources.
