correction to the countdown argument recorded in the revised class-forcing
paper, and of Glazer's MathOverflow question are source~35's; their checking
status is recorded in \cref{swo:xvi:sub:batch96}.

% ---- source 32, its Section 10
\subsection{Source 32: order length is not recursion strength}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 700-730
\label{swo:dc:sec:recursion}

\subsubsection{Three different uses of recursion}

An elementary transfinite recursion along a supplied class well-order $\Gamma$ asks for a class $S\subseteq\Gamma\times V$ whose sections satisfy a rule of the form
\[\tag{S32.18}
\label{swo:dc:eq:etr}
S_\gamma=\{x:\varphi(x,S\restr\Gamma_{<\gamma},Z)\},
\]
where $\varphi$ has only set quantifiers and $Z$ is a fixed class parameter. The sections $S_\gamma$ are classes, not necessarily sets. ETR asserts the existence of solutions for the relevant class well-orders. The distinction between class-valued recursion and finite or set-valued recursion is standard in the literature on second-order set theory \cite{Williams,xviBartonWilliams}.

The proofs in this manuscript use three quite different mechanisms. Finite syntax allows recursive evaluation of a single finite tree. Set-valued recursion with a set history constructs, for example, an $\omega$-sequence of finite term codes or the cofinal map in \cref{swo:dc:prop:cofinality}. Class-valued recursion constructs all the equivalence relations in \cref{swo:dc:thm:termination}, with previous relations themselves as class data. Only the third is an invocation of ETR.

Even a recursion whose stage order is the set $\omega$ can be class-valued: its stages might be increasingly complicated satisfaction classes. Therefore ``the index is only countable'' is not a reason to replace a class-valued recursion by the ordinary recursion theorem of ZFC. Conversely, the existence of $\Eps(\Omega)$ is not an ETR theorem, since its points are finite codes and well-foundedness was proved by support localization.

\subsubsection{Comparison principles and what is left open}

Hamkins and Woodin prove that ETR implies initial-segment comparability of class well-orders and discuss reverse implications relating ETR, continuous rankings, and weaker comparison principles \cite{HamkinsWoodin}. We use their theorem only where explicitly stated. No claimed solution of those reverse-implication questions is part of the present work.

It is tempting to argue that two class well-orders can always be compared by recursively matching their least unmatched points. The difficulty appears when the matched initial history is proper: that history is no longer a set on which the ordinary set recursion theorem operates. It is equally tempting to take the union of all partial class matches, but this invokes a collection of class objects outside elementary class comprehension. Both arguments need additional justification.

Our diagonal theorem was designed to avoid this issue. Its contradiction is local to a single known block $W_i+1$. Likewise, the division theorem obtains canonical isomorphisms from set-sized local ranks. These examples illustrate how to obtain substantial structural results without solving the general comparison problem.

In the external spectrum theorems, ordinary order types can of course be compared in the metatheory. That comparison is not being pulled back as an admitted isomorphism in $\mathcal X_A$. For example, the assertion that a definable suborder has an external ordinal type below another does not, by itself, prove that its initial-segment isomorphism is definable over $(V_\kappa,\in,G,A)$.

\subsubsection{Why there is no universal final ordinal}

Three rigorous negatives replace a vague search for ``the biggest ordinal beyond $\Ord$''. First, $W+1$ is always a strictly larger presentation. Second, \cref{swo:dc:thm:diagonal} defeats any one admitted uniform family. Third, the exact externally realized spectrum changes with the admitted class collection: it is bounded by $\delta_A$ for one definable realization and by $\kappa^+$ for the full realization, with truth strictly increasing the former.

None of this contradicts the fact that every ordinary set well-order is isomorphic to a unique ordinal. The problematic step would be to apply the set collapse theorem to a relation whose predecessor segments are proper. The theorem's set-likeness hypothesis is doing real work.

% ---- source 32, its Section 13
\subsection{Source 32: conclusion}\label{swo:dc:sec:conclusion}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 859-865

The ordinal class is a boundary for set-like orderings, not for definable well-order presentations. Finite tuples, finite supports, and finite hereditary trees already produce a rich arithmetic beyond it. Every class well-order has a canonical first division by $\Omega$, and no admitted uniform family can be cofinal among all admitted class well-orders.

The strongest distinctions arise when uniformity is made explicit. A general condensation history, once admitted, must terminate by the order's own length, but existence of that history is a separate recursion principle. At an inaccessible set-universe cutoff, all definable class well-orders have a sharply structured external ceiling of countable cofinality, yet a truth predicate assembles a presentation of exactly that previously unavailable ceiling. Full classes extend farther still, through every external type below $\kappa^+$.

Thus the rigorous answer to ``how far beyond $\Ord$?'' is not one terminal ordinal. It is an arithmetic of presentations, a hierarchy of admissible constructions, and a model-relative spectrum whose boundary moves when the available definitions become uniform.

% ---- source 33, its Section 13
\subsection{Source 33: conclusion and status of the contribution}\label{swo:dh:sec:conclusion}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1772-1800

The order of all set ordinals is a boundary for set-like orders, not a
boundary for class well-orders. Explicit sums, products, finite-support
powers, and coherent fixed points pass beyond it in elementary class
set theory. The price is not inconsistency but proper-class initial
segments and careful tracking of what is uniformly coded.

The structural analysis is quite concrete. Set intervals divide every
class well-order canonically into $\Omega$-blocks and a final set remainder.
An exhausting condensation tower gives finite ordinal digits and an
embedding into a polynomial class order. The important existential issue
is whether the tower is supplied by an explicit formula or requires a
recursion principle.

The definability analysis has a different conclusion: there is no final
uniform catalogue. Every fixed complexity bound can be diagonally exceeded,
even when arbitrary set parameters are allowed. At an inaccessible rank
model this yields a countably cofinal, arithmetically closed external
ceiling strictly above the internal $\Ord$, and truth strictly raises
that ceiling without changing any set ordinal.

These are proved structural answers and a research program. The article
is not a claim to have settled the general published comparison problem,
not a report of a completed Lean formalization, and not evidence of
historical priority. The most valuable next checks are an independent
mathematical review of the bounded-definability construction and a formal
proof of the supplied-tower digit theorem with every size assertion made
explicit.

% ---- source 34 (batch-96 manuscript 10), lines 1946-2085
\section{Rigorous formalization routes}
\label{swo:bo:sec:formalization}

\subsection{Two-sorted class theory}

For the reverse-mathematical result, a two-sorted formalization is
the most faithful route. Use a type of sets, a type of admitted
classes, membership of sets in classes, and codes for ordered pairs.
Class relations are classes of pair codes. The elementary
comprehension and Class Replacement schemes must be explicit
assumptions of the formalized object theory. A class well-order
quantifies over the admitted class sort, exactly as in the
mathematical definition.

In this setting, a supplied history is one class of stage--point
pairs. Its slices are defined by comprehension; they are not
members of a newly created class of all slices. The polynomial
carrier consists of finite graphs of sets. The greedy proof uses
only a least point in a supplied well-order and ordinary recursion
on a set. The resulting theorem can therefore track the absence
of Choice at the level of the object theory.

A proof assistant's unrestricted collection of predicates on the
set type should not silently replace the admitted class sort.
That would usually provide full external semantics and could make
comparability automatic. Such a proof may be correct for that
strong interpretation while failing to establish a theorem over
arbitrary Henkin models of $\GB$.

\subsection{Universe levels and ordinary order types}

A second route treats $\Omega$ as all ordinals small relative to
one universe. In Lean's ordinary ordinal development,
\texttt{Ordinal.\{u\}} lives in \texttt{Type (u+1)} and represents
order types of \texttt{Type u} carriers. Its complete order can be
assigned an order type at the larger universe level. A tagged
endpoint, finite product, or finite-support function space then
produces an ordinary order in that larger universe. Mathlib's
ordinal library explicitly distinguishes these levels and their
lifts \cite{MathlibOrdinal}.

This route is well suited to validating algebraic laws and the
hereditary tree construction. It also makes clear why
$\Omega+1$ is harmless: it lies beyond the smaller universe's
ordinals, not beyond the ordinals at every level. Moving all objects
back to the smaller universe would require a smallness theorem
that fails at exactly the proper-class boundary.

For a theorem about the exact strength over $\GB$, the universe
route is a semantic test rather than a replacement for a formal
object-theory proof. Its strong ambient supply of subsets and
functions cannot be used as evidence that every weak class
realization contains the required isomorphism or history.

\subsection{Full inaccessible-universe semantics}

Assume an inaccessible $\kappa$ in an external ZFC universe and
interpret sets by $V_\kappa$ and classes by all its external
subsets. Every point and every finite code belongs to $V_\kappa$.
Class relations become external sets, so ordinary ordinal arithmetic
computes their lengths. This interpretation gives the exact
$\kappa^+$ spectrum and the substitution rule
\[
\Omega\rightsquigarrow\kappa,\qquad
 P(B)\rightsquigarrow\kappa^{\otp(B)},\qquad
\Eps\rightsquigarrow\varepsilon_{\kappa+1}.
\]
It provides a strong consistency check on indexing and orientation
of products. It does not prove a universal theorem over weak
class theories simply by being one model of them.

\subsection{Unrolling and higher sorts}

There is a more structural way to pass beyond the original sets.
The unrolling construction uses well-founded extensional class
graphs with a distinguished top to represent virtual sets. A
class well-order with an appended top then represents an ordinal
of the unrolled structure. Williams develops the resulting
interpretations and explains how their strength depends on the
ground class theory \cite[Chapter 2]{Williams}. This is a
natural framework if one wants actual ordinal-like objects for
class-order types, rather than working presentation by presentation.

One must prove the required graph comparisons and the axioms of
the unrolled structure; they are not consequences of having
written down a quotient notation. Similarly, a third sort of
hyperclasses can collect class presentations, but its comprehension
and replacement principles must be stated. Adding a sort moves
the collection problem upward. It does not supply an absolute
class of all orders across every higher level.

\subsection{A concrete formalization plan for ProveIt}

The proof dependencies suggest the following small modules. The
names are proposed organization, not claims of existing checked
files.

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{L{0.25\textwidth}L{0.39\textwidth}L{0.24\textwidth}}
\toprule
Module & Main content & Required boundary \\
\midrule
Class orders & Tagged carriers, admitted-subclass minima,
initial embeddings, anti-embedding & $\GB$ \\
Finite-support powers & Finite list comparison, greedy minimum,
split and flatten isomorphisms & $\GB$; no Choice instance \\
Canonical blocks & Set-interval predicate, local ordinal ranks,
least representatives & $\GB$ \\
Canonical histories & Supplied histories, floors, finite changes,
normal-form initiality, equivalence & $\GB$; existence as a named principle \\
Hereditary syntax & Finite tree validation, structural comparison,
specialization, fixed-point map & $\GB$ via the set-subset criterion \\
Definability and truth & Formula codes, validity compiler, uniform
diagonal, external spectra & Truth and model assumptions tracked separately \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The most valuable first target is the choice-free power theorem.
Its invariant concerns an actual nonempty subclass and the prefix
selected from it; an implementation must not quietly replace this
by a finite sample. Next formalize the fixed-cap step in normal-form
initiality: it is what upgrades an arbitrary embedding to an
initial embedding. These two points carry the mathematical content
of the base-theory refinement.

For the hereditary syntax, define comparison by recursion on the
sizes of two finite trees before asserting that the resulting order
is well-founded. Define the height-bounded stages syntactically.
This avoids accidentally using $\ETR_\omega$ to construct a
sequence of proper-class stages. The ordinary specialization
proof then gives a useful independent semantic specification.

No natural-number program can literally contain an arbitrary ordinal
coefficient. A computational implementation should therefore state
its coefficient interface: natural numbers, a specified notation
system for set ordinals, or an abstract well-order with a comparison
oracle. Claims of decidability apply to the chosen interface, not
to every set ordinal or every formula-defined class presentation.

% ---- source 35, its Sections 9.4--9.5
\subsection{Source 35: five formalization routes and a proof-assistant design}

% ---- source 35 (batch-96 manuscript 11), lines 2620-2724

\paragraph{First-order set theory with definable classes.}
In a $\mathsf{ZFC}$ development, write each class by a formula and regard
theorems involving arbitrary definitions as schemes.  Carrier membership,
comparison, finite supports, finite trees, and the explicit witnesses
constructed in this article can all be handled in this way.  A theorem
for each fixed complexity level is legitimate; substituting a single
purported truth predicate for all levels is not.  This route is economical
when the intended output is a specific notation system with explicitly
defined operations.

\paragraph{$\GB$ and $\GBC$.}
A two-sorted first-order theory makes class quantification explicit.
Elementary comprehension permits fixed class parameters but forbids
class quantifiers in the defining formula.  Finite-support normal forms
and finite-tree evaluation remain ordinary classes of sets.  A family
of classes is represented by one binary class relation with sections,
not by treating its proper-class sections as members.  Global Choice
permits arbitrary carriers to be recoded uniformly and supplies the
general descending-sequence argument; constructions using only ordinal
codes often need less choice.

\paragraph{$\GBC+\ETR$.}
Elementary transfinite recursion supplies a class-coded solution when
each stage may itself be a proper class and the recursion follows an
arbitrary admitted class well-order.  It justifies general recursively
defined comparison and iteration constructions.  Its equivalence with
clopen class-game determinacy, and the related equivalences for
$\ETR_{\Ord}$, explain why this is a substantive additional axiom
rather than a routine use of set recursion
\cite{GitmanHamkins,GHHSW}.  The finite hereditary constructions
in this article were arranged to avoid assuming it.  Producing one
explicit very long class order does not supply arbitrary recursions
along that order.

\paragraph{$\KM$ and unrolling.}
Impredicative comprehension allows classes defined with class
quantifiers.  Unrolling instead represents larger objects by class
membership codes and compares those codes by class isomorphisms.
The exact axiom statement matters: Williams proves that $\KM$ plus
Class Collection is bi-interpretable with
$\mathsf{ZFC}^{-}_{I}$, which includes Separation and Collection and
has a largest inaccessible cardinal.  Here inaccessibility includes
the required powersets below that cardinal.  For $\GBC+\ETR$, the
corresponding theory is the weaker
$\mathsf{wZFC}^{-}_{I}(0)+\Sigma_0$-Transfinite Recursion, not full
$\mathsf{ZFC}^{-}$ with Collection
\cite[Definition~2.1, Theorem~2.2, Corollary~2.32]{Williams}.
An externally well-founded collapse additionally requires the relevant
$\beta$-correctness.  An internal interpretation alone does not turn
every represented order into an externally genuine ordinal.

\paragraph{Higher-order theories and universe hierarchies.}
One may allow hyperclasses whose elements are classes, or work in a
larger universe in which the previous universe is a set.  Such a move
makes a previous collection of class orders available as an object at
the new level.  The level must be recorded: its ordinal operations are
ordinary operations in the larger setting, while its lower-level
interpretation may be a proper class order.  Repeating this construction
never produces a same-level object containing every order at every
level.  It produces a hierarchy of formally distinct domains.

\subsubsection{A proof-assistant design with explicit universes}

A direct Lean development should begin with a model of sets and an
explicit collection of admitted predicates and relations.  Its
class-well-order structure should record a carrier predicate, a strict
linear order on that carrier, and minimality for every admitted nonempty
subclass.  Set-likeness must be a separate field or predicate.  Requiring
it in the definition of every class well-order would exclude the main
examples by construction.

The initial implementation can consist of the following independent
interfaces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Classes and class functions over a fixed set model, together with
      elementary comprehension and Class Replacement.
\item General class well-orders, arbitrary order embeddings, and initial
      embeddings, with each distinction retained in theorem statements.
\item Finite-support polynomials and their greatest-disagreement order,
      followed by explicit sum and product isomorphisms.
\item Finite hereditary syntax, its canonical comparison, and the
      compatible finite-stage embeddings defining the fixed-point order.
\item A separate semantics in an ambient inaccessible-height model,
      including the spectrum and definability theorems above.
\end{enumerate}

An alternative begins with universe-indexed types.  The type of ordinals
of one universe lives in a larger universe; its lexicographic square
and finite hereditary notation types can be formed there.  This is an
effective way to verify explicit order algebra.  It does not by itself
formalize the distinction between an arbitrary subset and an admitted
class of a particular $\GB$ model.  That distinction requires the model
interface just described.

There are likewise two different uses of well-founded recursion.  A
proof assistant's recursion on a genuinely well-founded type can evaluate
finite syntax directly.  Applying the same mechanism to a model's
\emph{internally} well-founded class relation would silently add external
correctness unless its hypotheses are translated and proved.  Keeping
the syntax layer, internal class semantics, and external realization
separate exposes this obligation.  The discussion here is a formalization
design; it is not a claim that a Lean implementation has been compiled
or kernel-checked.

% ---- source 32, its Section 11
\subsection{Source 32: five rigorous formalization routes}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 732-793
\label{swo:dc:sec:formalization}

The right formalization depends on whether the goal is to check the arithmetic, to establish its minimal axioms, or to compare models with different admitted classes. No one encoding makes these three tasks identical.

\subsubsection{ZFC with definable-class schemas}

In a purely first-order treatment, replace each class symbol by a formula with a fixed finite tuple of parameters. A theorem about a fixed finite number of classes becomes a schema of first-order theorems. The constructions of sums, products, finite-support powers, and hereditary terms are syntactic transformations of formulas. Their proofs can be represented in an ordinary first-order proof system.

This route is especially faithful to the phrase ``definable class well-order''. It also exposes the limit of the approach: a variable ranging over formula codes does not come equipped with an internal semantic evaluator. One may manipulate codes syntactically, prove substitution lemmas, and handle each fixed finite collection of formulas; one may not introduce a full satisfaction predicate for the ambient universe without an additional assumption.

A global well-order needs attention. ZFC alone does not assert a parameter-definable global well-order of its universe. One should either work over a structure with an explicitly supplied global predicate, assume a definable global-order hypothesis, or weaken the claims so that they do not require Global Choice. The GBC results above should not be translated into parameter-free ZFC assertions by simply erasing the class parameters.

\subsubsection{A two-sorted admitted-class model}

For questions about GBC itself, use a structure with a set sort $M$, a class sort $\mathcal X$, an internal set-membership relation, and an interpretation relation $x\in C$ for $x\in M$, $C\in\mathcal X$. Tuples and graphs are internally encoded in $M$. An embedding is required to have a graph in $\mathcal X$.

The well-order predicate must quantify over admitted subclasses:
\[
\operatorname{WO}_{\mathcal X}(D,R)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\forall S\in\mathcal X\,
\bigl(\varnothing\ne S\subseteq D\ \Longrightarrow\ S\text{ has an }R\text{-least point}\bigr).
\]
Alternatively, after formalizing \cref{swo:dc:lem:descending}, use the elementary internal condition forbidding descending functions whose codes are \emph{sets of the model}. These are not automatically all external functions from an external $\omega$.

This matters in Lean. A bare declaration \code{R : M -> M -> Prop} followed by ambient \code{WellFounded R} usually means well-foundedness for the proof assistant's full external predicate and sequence universe. It is stronger than the internal condition of an arbitrary Henkin class model. Similarly, setting the class sort equal to all predicates \code{M -> Prop} chooses full external classes, not a general GBC realization. To study $\mathcal X_A$, encode the admissible predicates and admissible graphs explicitly, together with closure under elementary definitions.

For the inaccessible-rank models of \cref{swo:dc:lem:rankmodel}, a separate absoluteness theorem then relates internal well-ordering to external well-foundedness. That theorem is a bridge to be proved, not a convention to apply to all models.

\subsubsection{GBC with explicit recursion packages, or stronger class theory}

An ETR interface should take a stage presentation, an elementary formula code, and admitted parameters, and return an admitted history satisfying \eqref{swo:dc:eq:etr}. The condensation development can then be split cleanly in two: the termination invariant is proved from a supplied history; a separate theorem invokes the ETR interface to obtain that history. A stronger theory such as Morse--Kelley class theory can also supply the requisite recursion, but that should not obscure the weaker conditional theorem \cite{Williams}.

This separation gives an auditable dependency boundary. The explicit polynomial hierarchy needs no recursion package at all: formula \eqref{swo:dc:eq:explicitcond} supplies its code directly. Its verification consists of successor and limit identities. By contrast, an arbitrary $W$ enters the existence theorem only after the ETR assumption has been made.

\subsubsection{Higher universes and ordinary ordinal libraries}

A practical route to checking the arithmetic is to view the ordinals of one Lean universe as a type in a larger universe. Mathlib's current ordinal-universe interface provides \code{Ordinal.univ} and \code{Ordinal.type\_lt\_ordinal}; the latter identifies the order type of the smaller-universe ordinals with the corresponding larger-universe universal ordinal. The old name \code{Ordinal.univ\_id} is marked deprecated in the documentation inspected on 4 October 2026 \cite{xviMathlibUniv}.

This makes the presentation $\Omega$ into an ordinary ordinal in a higher universe, after which the usual ordinal library can verify powers and initial embeddings. It is an excellent arithmetic test bed. It does not identify the predicates admitted by an arbitrary $(M,\mathcal X)$, and it does not establish that a construction was provable in bare GBC. A universe-level smallness notion is also not automatically the model's internal ``is a set'' predicate. The inaccessible-universe interpretation should never be read as a proof in ordinary ZFC that a strongly inaccessible set cardinal exists.

A useful implementation architecture therefore has an abstract presentation layer and a separate realization functor into higher-universe ordinals. The functor certifies arithmetic identities once their maps are defined, while the abstract layer tracks which graphs and histories are admitted by the chosen class theory.

\subsubsection{Unrolling into virtual sets}

Another approach represents virtual sets by well-founded extensional class membership codes. A class well-order, with an added top point, can serve as a code for an ordinal in an unrolled structure. This is a change of interpretation, not a collapse to an actual ordinal in the original set universe. Williams develops the unrolling approach and the dependence of its properties on the underlying second-order theory \cite{Williams}.

For the present project, the attraction is that arithmetic on long orders can be compared with ordinary arithmetic on the corresponding virtual ordinals. The danger is assuming all the axioms of the target theory before proving them. In particular, existence of suitable code comparisons and set-forming operations needs its own theorem. An unrolled ordinal representing $\Omega+\Omega$ is not a counterexample to the original model's assertion that its von Neumann ordinals form the class $\Ord$.

\subsubsection{Connection to the inspected ProveIt foundation}

The inspected file
\begin{center}
\path{SetTheory/ZF/Lean/ZF/Zf.lean}
\end{center}
works with first-order formulas and explicitly coded ZF axioms. Among the declarations inspected are \code{Sep\_form}, \code{Repl\_form}, \code{ZFax}, and \code{ZFprov}; the file imports \code{FirstOrder.Calculus}. Its documented internal-recursion development concerns finite recursion and closure for definable set-like relations \cite{xviZfLean}. These are relevant foundations, but they do not already constitute a formalization of non-set-like class recursion.

A compatible extension would first add syntax for finitely many class predicate parameters and prove substitution and satisfaction bridges. A second layer would package admitted classes and their elementary-comprehension closure. The arithmetic could then be developed with no ETR import. Condensation existence would live in a module whose assumptions explicitly include the recursion package, while termination from a supplied hierarchy would remain in the weak layer.

Within a proposed \code{ClassOrders} namespace, useful modules would be \code{Basic}, \code{FiniteSupport}, \code{Arithmetic}, \code{Condensation}, and \code{DefinabilitySpectrum}. These names describe a proposed organization, not files created in the repository. The first machine-checked milestones should be least-representative quotients, no self-compression, and the finite-support comparison laws. The model-relative ceiling theorem should follow only after the syntax/semantics boundary has been formalized.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Status.} No Lean or Rocq proof was produced or checked for this article. No repository build or modification was performed. The formalization discussion is a source-informed implementation plan, not a verification claim.\par\smallskip

% ---- source 33, its Section 10
\subsection{Source 33: formalization approaches and their tradeoffs}\label{swo:dh:sec:formalization}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1403-1576

\subsubsection{ZFC with definable-class schemas}
One can express each explicit construction as a theorem schema in ordinary
$\ZFC$. Fix formulas defining the domain, order, and any needed global
ordering, substitute those formulas into the construction, and prove the
resulting first-order assertion. This is particularly well suited to
finite-support exponentiation and the bounded-complexity diagonal.

The limitation is quantification. A schema over formulas is not a single
internal quantifier over all definable classes. The diagonal proof makes
this limitation visible rather than hiding it: the evaluator exists at each
fixed level, but a uniform evaluator for every level is not thereby supplied.
For formalization, formula substitution and the distinction between a
metatheoretic natural number and an object-theoretic variable must be explicit.

The use of a named $G$ can be handled either by assuming its defining formula
has the required global-order properties or by working in a language with
an additional class predicate and the corresponding separation/replacement
instances. Pure $\ZFC$ without a definable global order does not automatically
satisfy the parameter-free formulation of \cref{swo:dh:cor:pure}.

\subsubsection{Two-sorted GB, GBC, and NBG}
A two-sorted theory is the most faithful framework for the core article.
The set sort contains every point, finite code, and ordinal coordinate.
The class sort contains domains, relations, embeddings, and uniform towers.
Elementary comprehension creates the needed classes, and replacement
recognizes when their set-indexed images are sets.

Terminology varies: some formulations of NBG include global choice as part
of the default theory and some distinguish it. Here $\GBC$ always includes
a set-like global choice order. No argument should be transferred to a
choiceless or Power-Set-free version merely by changing the theory's name.

The central size invariant is a predicate saying that a specified subclass
has a set with exactly its members. For example,
\[
 \operatorname{SmallInterval}(x,y)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists z\ \forall t\,[t\in z\leftrightarrow t\in[x,y]_W].
\]
It must not be replaced by external cardinality or by the fact that an
implementation stores a finite approximation. Quotient elements should be
least representatives. These design choices let the core statements remain
inside the original two sorts.

\subsubsection{Elementary transfinite recursion and comparison}
A general recursion of the form
\[
 S_\gamma=\{x:\varphi(x,S\restr\gamma,A)\},
 \qquad\gamma\in\Gamma,
\]
with $\varphi$ first-order and $A$ a class parameter, is what
$\ETR_\Gamma$ supplies. The stages $S_\gamma$ are classes, so ordinary
set recursion does not suffice. Even recursion of length $\omega$ with
class-valued stages can encode a full satisfaction predicate
\cite{GitmanHamkins}.

The known implication
\[
    \GBC+\ETR\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \text{initial comparability of class well-orders}
\]
is established in Hamkins--Woodin \cite[Theorem 6]{HamkinsWoodin}. This supplies
a conventional ordinal-style comparison theory when it is needed.
The finite-support operations, canonical division, supplied-tower digit
map, and diagonal theorems do not use that implication.

One should also distinguish $\ETR_\Omega$ from full $\ETR$ over every
class well-order. The exact strength of the class forcing theorem identifies
it with the former, among several equivalent principles
\cite{GHHSW}. A notation such as $\ETR_{\Omega^{[\Omega]}}$ therefore carries
real information about the permitted recursion lengths.

\subsubsection{KM, stronger recursion, and unrolling}
Kelley--Morse theory allows impredicative class comprehension, where the
defining formulas may quantify over classes. The corresponding second-order
transfinite recursion principle is equivalent to $\KM$ over $\GBC$
\cite{HamkinsRecursion}. This is a stronger setting than the elementary
recursions used in the conditional condensation results.

Stronger class comprehension still does not make proper classes ordinary
members of classes. To treat class well-orders as ordinal-like objects in a
larger first-order universe, one may instead \emph{unroll}: use well-founded
extensional class membership codes and identify codes by isomorphism.
Williams describes, in particular, the unrolling of $\KM$ plus Class
Collection to a model of $\ZFC^-$ with a largest cardinal, and analyzes
weaker theories as well \cite{Williams}. Antos--Friedman use a related
coding framework for beta-models of an explicitly strengthened Morse--Kelley
theory \cite{AntosFriedman}.

These are interpretive constructions with hypotheses, not permission to
write ``the class of all class ordinals'' inside ordinary $\GBC$.
Collection, well-foundedness correctness, and the exact set theory obtained
by unrolling must be tracked separately. This manuscript uses unrolling as
a formalization option, not as an unproved shortcut in its elementary proofs.

\subsubsection{Inaccessible universes and full semantics}
The $V_\kappa$ model of \cref{swo:dh:sec:spectra} translates the class orders into
ordinary external ordinals. It is particularly effective for testing
arithmetic formulas and explaining the spectrum endpoint $\kappa^+$.
It also supports all full subclasses, so it is stronger than a minimal
definable-class realization.

A full powerset of classes is not harmless over an arbitrary set model.
For example, if a transitive model is externally countable, its full class
part includes an external countable cofinal enumeration of its ordinals.
Treating that enumeration as a class function on its $\omega$ contradicts
class replacement. The regular inaccessible cutoff avoids exactly this
failure. This is why the hypothesis is proved relevant, rather than being
used only as an informal picture of a ``large enough universe.''

\subsubsection{Lean universes: relative largeness rather than an absolute class}
Mathlib's ordinal type is universe indexed. In its documented interface,
\texttt{Ordinal.\{u\}} lives in \texttt{Type (u+1)}, and
\texttt{Ordinal.type} assigns an ordinal to a well-order on a type of the
chosen universe \cite{MathlibOrdinal}. Thus the order on all
\texttt{Ordinal.\{u\}} can itself receive an order type one universe
higher. Abstractly, define
\[
 \Omega_u=\operatorname{type}\bigl(\mathrm{Ordinal}^{\{u\}},<\bigr)
       \in\mathrm{Ordinal}^{\{u+1\}}.
\]
Its successor, square, and higher powers then use ordinary ordinal arithmetic
at that higher level.

This approach is excellent for concrete relative-universe models. It does
not identify the smaller-universe ordinals with a set ordinal in the same
smaller universe. Nor does Lean provide a single type of ordinals over
\emph{all} universes. Universe lifting is part of the result, not a
technicality to suppress.

There are two distinct formalization projects:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),itemsep=2pt]
\item \textbf{Ambient type-theoretic mathematics.} Use ordinary well-orders
      on large types, smallness predicates for predecessor types, and
      larger-universe ordinals. This is the shorter route to arithmetic and
      representation theorems.
\item \textbf{A theorem about class set theory.} Define a two-sorted model
      interface, an explicit available-class sort, elementary comprehension,
      class replacement, and a named global order. Prove each implication
      using only that interface. This is the route that can certify a stated
      $\GBC$ versus $\ETR$ axiom bound.
\end{enumerate}

A structure that simply interprets ``class'' as \emph{every} predicate
$U\to\mathrm{Prop}$ gives full external semantics. It must not be used to
claim an elementary $\GBC$ proof when the argument secretly quantifies over
predicates unavailable in a weaker realization. The explicit available-class
sort prevents this mistake.

The current article provides interfaces and proof obligations, not a Lean
implementation. No displayed mathematical interface is advertised as
compiler-tested code.

\subsubsection{Transport to surreal carriers}
Under global choice, every proper class of sets can be enumerated in a
set-like order of type $\Omega$ by restricting a global order. Hence proper
class carriers of the orders studied here can be put in class bijection
with the surreal numbers $\No$, and their order relations transported to
that carrier. This connects the article with the repository's surreal
well-order projects.

The transported order is not the natural ordered-field relation on
$\No$. That relation is not a well-order; for example, the negative
integers descend indefinitely. Nor is the symbol $\Omega$ a surreal number
larger than every set ordinal. Each surreal is represented by a set-length
sign sequence, and an ordinal longer than its birthday bounds it above.
There is no surreal with proper-class birthday in the ordinary construction.

Finally, ordinal arithmetic is not surreal field arithmetic. Already
$1+\omega=\omega$ in ordinal addition, whereas adding the surreal number
$1$ to the surreal $\omega$ gives a strictly larger number. Reusing symbols
must not erase which operations or which ordering are being studied.

\subsection{Source 33: a formalization and verification plan for ProveIt}\label{swo:dh:sec:plan}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1578-1649

\subsubsection{Suggested module boundary}
A proposed new development could live under
\texttt{SetTheory/ClassWellOrders/}; this is a suggested location, not a
claim that the directory already exists. Its mathematical dependency graph
should separate the following components.

\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.24\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.43\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.26\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Component} & \textbf{Main specification} & \textbf{Trust boundary}\\
\midrule
\endhead
Presentations & Domains, class relations, embeddings, initial images;
least-subclass and descending-sequence formulations. & Explicit class-model
interface.\\[4pt]
FiniteSupport & Finite maps with a greatest-difference comparison;
split, group, and flatten maps. & Finite combinatorics plus ordinary set
well-orders.\\[4pt]
Arithmetic & Sums, products, powers, and uniform lexicographic sums. &
Elementary comprehension and replacement.\\[4pt]
SetIntervals & Convexity, least representatives, set-like blocks,
and canonical $\Omega$-division. & Internal sethood, not external size.\\[4pt]
Condensation & Supplied towers, polynomial truncations, ordinal digits,
termination and order preservation. & Separate supplied-tower theorem
from existence under ETR.\\[4pt]
Definability & Formula codes, each partial satisfaction predicate, the
well-orderhood test, and the diagonal compiler. & Schema-level indexing
must remain explicit.\\[4pt]
RankModels & Correctness of $V_\kappa$, full spectrum, definability height,
and truth jump. & External inaccessible hypothesis.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

The successor obstruction should be proved early and imported by every
diagonal argument. It is short, robust, and avoids the temptation to assume
initial comparability as an unrecorded global fact.

\subsubsection{The most important proof obligations}
For the structural side, the critical obligations are that interval sethood
is internal, quotient representatives are sets, the ordinal coordinate in
\eqref{swo:dh:eq:digit} exists, and the digit-extraction process terminates by
well-foundedness of the stage order. For the definability side, they are
that bounded satisfaction is genuinely available, the well-orderhood test
has only set quantifiers, and the family of all parameter tuples is jointly
definable before the diagonal sum is formed.

A formalization of \cref{swo:dh:thm:bounded} should not package all the evaluators
into a predicate assumed to satisfy unrestricted truth. A syntactic compiler
that takes a \emph{metatheoretic} numeral $n$ to the formula defining $D_n$
is appropriate. A purported internal evaluator for every resulting formula
would need a separate existence theorem and would contradict cofinality
if it were definable in the unchanged language.

\subsubsection{Executable checks included with this article}
The archive includes a small Python verification program for finite
positional models. It checks greatest-difference comparison, splitting an
exponent sum, flattening nested powers, and the partition into fibers of
truncation. These tests can catch a reversed product convention or an
incorrect significance order in the finite coding layer.

They do \emph{not} verify that a proper-class order is well-founded, that a
class relation is a set, that partial truth exists, or that a class recursion
is licensed. In a genuinely finite order every interval is a set, so replacing
set-interval condensation by naive finite testing would collapse everything
at the first step. The tests intentionally avoid that false analogy.

A useful next implementation would prove the finite checker correct, then
prove that the class construction uses the verified combinatorial maps.
Until that bridge and the foundational arguments are formalized, the Python
output remains a consistency check on conventions, not a mathematical
certificate for the class-theoretic theorems.

\merge\ The program described above is shipped as
\path{code/33-heights-finite_checks.py}, its recorded run as
\path{data/33-heights-verification_results.json} (\cref{swo:xvi:sub:delivery96}).

as finite recursion, a noninitial embedding used as an initial one,
and an external well-order assertion without the required model
hypothesis. These checks are mathematical review within this

The hereditary finite-tree pattern is standard in ordinal notation.
Its appearance in the BIRS problem collection concerns a set-sized
$\Omega$, commonly $\omega_1$ \cite{xviWeiermann}. The present
development supplies proper-class semantics, finite-code
well-foundedness, and the corresponding fixed-point interpretation.
It does not claim to have invented hereditary Cantor normal form.

The uniform-sum and parameter-spectrum arguments are proved in full
and presented as a synthesis. No bibliographic search can certify

The explicit resolution claimed here is limited to the
base-theory question in the inspected ProveIt report.

The most important proof checks concern size rather than algebraic manipulation. A quotient uses least representatives instead of class-valued elements. A uniformly coded family is one relation on set tuples. A limit condensation stage is one admitted section of one admitted history. A finite list of formulas is evaluated by finitely many substitutions, whereas evaluation at a variable formula code requires truth. Finally, external ordinal spectra are formed only after moving to a set-sized external model.

% ---- source 32, its Appendix B
\subsection{Source 32: computational checks and reproducibility}

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 901-908
\label{swo:dc:app:checks}

The accompanying Python script checks finite digit comparisons, support splitting, grouping of nested exponents, initial support embeddings, and hereditary base representations of ordinary natural numbers. It also checks the algebra of tail-deletion equivalence relations on bounded digit arrays. The run completed 689,808 exact assertions without failure; the category counts are recorded in \path{finite_checks.json}.

These computations are regression tests for the concrete coding conventions. They do not prove the infinitary results. In particular, every interval in a finite order is a set, so an actual finite test of the distinction between a set interval and a proper-class interval would be vacuous. The tail-deletion tests therefore verify only the stated finite mask formulas; they do not claim to simulate class condensation. Likewise, no finite program here verifies GBC, ETR, an inaccessible cardinal, or an external truth predicate.

The source is self-contained LaTeX with an internal bibliography. Build it with a standard TeX distribution, for example by running \code{pdflatex beyond\_ord.tex} repeatedly until references stabilize. No nonstandard font files or external bibliography database are required. The separate verification-status file records the compilation and rendering checks performed for the delivered PDF.

\merge\ The ``accompanying Python script'' is \path{code/32-ceilings-finite_checks.py},
\path{finite_checks.json} is \path{data/32-ceilings-finite_checks.json}, and the
``separate verification-status file'' is \path{32-ceilings-PROOF_STATUS.md}.
The source and its PDF are not shipped.

% ---- source 33, its Appendix B
\subsection{Source 33: notation and error-prevention guide}\label{swo:dh:app:notation}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1849-1884

\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.20\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.73\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Notation} & \textbf{Meaning}\\
\midrule
\endhead
$\Omega$ & The class order $(\Ord,\in)$, not a set ordinal.\\[3pt]
$A\cong B$ & An available class order isomorphism, or its explicit
external interpretation where specified.\\[3pt]
$A\emb B$ & An available order embedding; its image need not be initial.\\[3pt]
$A\iemb B$ & An order embedding whose image is an initial segment.\\[3pt]
$A\cdot B$ & $B$-many ordered copies of $A$, with $B$ the significant
coordinate.\\[3pt]
$A^{[B]}$ & Finite-support ordinal exponentiation; not all functions $B\to A$.\\[3pt]
$P(\Gamma)$ & The class of finite $\Ord$-coefficient polynomials on
exponent order $\Gamma$.\\[3pt]
$\Gamma^+$ & The order $\Gamma+1$ with a new top stage; not a successor
cardinal.\\[3pt]
$\kappa^+$ & The external successor cardinal of the inaccessible
$\kappa$ in the spectrum analysis.\\[3pt]
$F_b$ & A section of one uniform condensation-tower relation.\\[3pt]
$D_n$ & A separately defined diagonal presentation for each fixed
standard finite syntax level $n$.\\[3pt]
$\delta_G$ & The external supremum of types definable with $G$ and
set parameters over $V_\kappa$.\\[3pt]
$T$ & Truth for the language with $G$, not truth for its own expanded
language.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

The most common invalid shortcuts are collecting proper classes as members,
using a full truth evaluator in a bounded-truth argument, confusing a schema
with one uniform class, treating internal well-foundedness as automatically
external, and using an arbitrary class recursion without recording ETR.
The constructions above were organized to avoid these shortcuts.

\merge\ In this report source~33's $\Omega$ is printed $\Omega$, its $A^B$ is
$A^{[B]}$, its $P_\Gamma$ is $P(\Gamma)$, and its direct limit $E$ is $\mathbb T$
(\cref{swo:xvi:sub:notation96}).

\section{What this Part answers}\label{swo:xvi:sec:status}

\merge\ Dated notes, 4 October 2026, in the form of \cref{swo:xiv:sec:status};
where an earlier status section or question index says otherwise, these notes
supersede it, and the places concerned carry dated notes of their own.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item \emph{The strength of complete condensation histories over $\GB$
without global choice} (\cref{swo:xiv:note:strength}; item~(b) of
\cref{swo:xiv:sec:status}; source~20's \cref{swo:lm:n11.5}; the $\GBC$
theorem is source~29's \cref{swo:bw:ch:equivalence}): \textbf{answered}, twice
independently. Over $\GB$ with $\ZF$ sets and no form of choice, $\CWO$,
$\CTH$, terminating histories on some schedule, and initial embeddings
$W\iemb P(W)$ are equivalent (\cref{swo:bo:hist:equivalence,swo:fc:gb-comparability}),
and so is the fixed-point extension principle $\FPE$
(\cref{swo:fc:cor:FPE-CWO,swo:xvi:thm:choicefree}). Not answered: whether $\GB$
proves $\CWO$ (no source claims it), and whether $\CWO$ implies $\ETR$
(Hamkins and Woodin's Question~7; source~29's \cref{swo:bw:n13.8}).
\item \emph{The strength of tower or hierarchy existence} (source~32's
\cref{swo:dc:n12.1}, source~33's \cref{swo:dh:n12.6}, and the ledgers'
``optimality not established'' in \cref{swo:dc:app:audit,swo:dh:app:ledger}):
\textbf{answered} by item~(a) and, over $\GBC$, already by source~29, because
towers and hierarchies of equivalence relations are nested histories
(\cref{swo:xvi:rem:towers}); only $\CWO\Rightarrow\ETR$ remains. Source~32's
claim to answer the termination question repeats source~20
(\cref{swo:xvi:rem:termination}).
\item \emph{Source~33's \cref{swo:dh:n5.5} and research question
\cref{swo:dh:n12.7}, initial image of the digit map}: \textbf{answered}: the map
is always initial (\cref{swo:xvi:rem:digits}); under $\ETR_{\Gamma+1}$ an
arbitrary embedding into $P(\Gamma)$ yields an initial one
(\cref{swo:xvi:rem:converse}).
\item \emph{Source~35's \cref{swo:fc:n10.6}, a choice-free completion
theorem}: \textbf{answered} positively by this write
(\cref{swo:xvi:thm:choicefree}).
\item \emph{Source~31's \cref{swo:gcz:n7}, definable-class versions of the
spectra}: answered in part, for the external order types at a strongly
inaccessible height. For the classes definable over $V_\kappa$ in a fixed
finite language with set parameters, the realized types form an interval
$[0,\Theta_L)$ with $\kappa<\Theta_L<\kappa^+$ (\cref{swo:bo:spec:interval});
with a named global well-order $\cf(\Theta_L)=\omega$ and parameter-free
definitions are cofinal (\cref{swo:bo:spec:cofinal,swo:bo:spec:inaccessible-relative}),
$\kappa^{\Theta_L}=\omega^{\Theta_L}=\Theta_L$
(\cref{swo:dc:thm:ceiling,swo:dh:cor:heightclosure}), the ceilings exhaust
$\kappa^+$ as the predicate varies (\cref{swo:dc:cor:ceilingsvary}), and a
truth predicate represents the old ceiling exactly and raises it
(\cref{swo:dc:thm:truth,swo:dh:thm:truthjump}); in the pure language,
$\kappa<\delta_0\le\delta_{\mathrm{ord}}\le\delta_{\mathrm{set}}<\kappa^+$ with
$\cf(\delta_0)=\omega$ (\cref{swo:fc:thm:definability-spectrum}). The rest of
\cref{swo:gcz:n7} stays open: the analogues of source~31's thresholds for
global choice, enumeration, coding and Class Replacement, heights $\lambda$
that are not inaccessible, and the exact values of the ceilings.
\item \emph{Source~12's full-class model} (\cref{swo:st:thm:model}~(iv), a
theorem): proved again by all four sources
(\cref{swo:bo:spec:full,swo:fc:thm:full-spectrum,swo:dc:thm:fullspectrum,swo:dh:thm:fullspectrum});
its hereditary calibration $\otp(\Eps)=\varepsilon_{\kappa+1}$ is new
(\cref{swo:bo:her:calibration}).
\item \emph{Not settled}: Hamkins and Woodin's Question~7; source~15's
\cref{swo:cb:n13.3}, whether $\GB$ codes all finite condensations uniformly,
which source~35 asks again (\cref{swo:fc:n10.4}); and the questions of
\cref{swo:xvi:sec:questions}.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Source 11's research questions and topics}\label{swo:sec:research}

The questions below are proposed extensions of the present
development. Except where a source is explicitly named, they
are not asserted to be established open problems in the
literature. Several ask for a stronger classification than
the proved results supply.

\subsubsection{A precise description of the represented cuts}

Fix the dense ordinary class \(\Pbd\cong\No\). Every
set-like global enumeration determines a lower cut of
\(\Pbd\), and so does every injective nonexhaustive
\(\Ord\)-word. The omitted-range example shows that the
first collection does not fill every cut generated by the
second.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.1}
Characterize, using the prefix tree and its numerical
labels, exactly which class cuts of \(\Pbd\) arise from
injective \(\Ord\)-words, and which of these words are
exhaustive.
\end{question}

A useful first target is a necessary-and-sufficient
compatibility condition on the intersections of a cut with
prefix cylinders. The challenge is to separate missing
labels, impossible repeated labels, and cuts that escape
every coherent branch. This should first be stated for a
fixed uniform class cut, before quantifying over an entire
hyperclass of cuts.

\subsubsection{The embedding relationship between the two global orders}

The set-like fragment and binary class words are
equimorphic, while the unrestricted order has additional
convex fibers. Theorem~\ref{swo:thm:universe-nonembedding}
rules out a reverse embedding in the full universe
interpretation. Theorem~\ref{swo:thm:km-nonembedding} also
rules out a definable uniform reverse embedding in
\(\KM+\GC\).

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.2}
What is the weakest comprehension scheme over \(\GBC\)
that proves the uniform nonembedding result? Can the
inverse-evaluation step be replaced by an elementary
argument, or is a genuine strengthening necessary?
\end{question}

A precise project should specify the syntactic complexity
of the proposed transformation and of the comprehension
used to invert its code assignment. In the bounded
setting one can instead compare the density and
cellularity of all well-orders of \(\No_{<\kappa}\)
with their minimum-length stratum, especially when
\(\kappa\) is not inaccessible. The full-universe case
is already settled above; the remaining questions
concern strength and wider hypotheses.

\subsubsection{Iterated residual decomposition}

One extraction of the canonical initial \(\Ord\)-part
requires only elementary class comprehension. A residual
proper class has another such part, suggesting a hierarchy
of successive blocks.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.3}
What is the exact recursion strength needed to organize
iterated residual decompositions uniformly, and what
class order types can occur as their block-index orders?
\end{question}

An initial project could analyze finitely many blocks and
specified set-length constructions, recording where the
recursion state becomes a class. The general case should
be compared with known \(\ETR\) results on class
well-order comparability, rather than assumed to follow
from the one-step theorem.

\subsubsection{Recovering the prefix structure from the bare order}

The definitions exhibit a labeled tree of prefixes.
An automorphism of the bare lexicographic order need not
obviously preserve its displayed labels or cylinders.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.4}
Which prefix cones, canonical-core fibers, and finite
permutation blocks are definable from the linear order
alone? What extra predicates make the reconstruction
unique?
\end{question}

Adjacency directly detects finite stretches, but a
singleton fiber can be exhaustive or can omit one label.
Thus local block size alone cannot recover set-likeness.
An analysis of the automorphism group may clarify what
the order remembers about the original enumeration.

\subsubsection{The bounded-support choice of baseline}

Every baseline enumeration gives an ordinary class
\(\Pbd\) abstractly isomorphic to \(\No\). If two
baselines differ on a proper class of positions, their
bounded-support subfamilies can be disjoint.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.5}
How do the two dense classes sit inside the same
\(\Hsl(\No)\), and when does an automorphism of that
higher-order order carry one onto the other?
\end{question}

The abstract isomorphism of the two dense orders does
not automatically extend to all global enumerations.
The represented-cut problem is likely relevant. A
restricted first case is a baseline change obtained by
an order automorphism of the numerical surreal line.

\subsubsection{Sharper birthday bounds and minimal codes}

The explicit code gives a usable bound
\[
 \bd(E(f))=\sum_{i<\dom f}
              \bigl(1+2\cdot\bd(f(i))+2\bigr).
\]
It is designed for a transparent proof, not asserted
to be optimal.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.6}
Which birthday bounds are optimal for uniform embeddings
of injective surreal words? Can shorter prefix-free
coefficient codes preserve useful simplicity relations?
\end{question}

Regular cutoffs permit same-stage compression; singular
cutoffs show why a cardinal bound alone is insufficient.
A sharpened result should specify whether it preserves
only numerical order, prefix extension, simplicity, or
all of these.

\subsubsection{Saturation of more general bounded alphabets}

If \(X\) is an \(\eta_\kappa\) order of cardinality
\(\kappa\), its minimal-length permutation order inherits
\(\eta_\kappa\). Birthday fragments often have cardinality
\(2^{<\kappa}\), which may exceed \(\kappa\).

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.7}
Determine the exact cut spectrum and point characters of
\(\WO_\lambda(\No_{<\kappa})\), where
\(\lambda=2^{<\kappa}\), without assuming
\(2^{<\kappa}=\kappa\).
\end{question}

The issue combines the size of a used prefix with the
number and birthdays of possible numerical separators.
The real-alphabet formulas in the precursor report
cannot settle this case by substitution.

\subsubsection{Class extensions and available global orders}

Two models may have the same sets and hence the same
individual surreal numbers, but different available
classes and different global well-orders.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.8}
Which features of the lexicographic theory are invariant
under extensions of the class part, and how does the
represented-cut collection change?
\end{question}

Uniform formulas such as first divergence remain the
same for the existing relations. Existence of additional
enumerations changes the larger totality. This offers a
way to distinguish properties of the labeled surreal
order from properties of the surrounding class theory.

\subsubsection{A verified first milestone for ProveIt}

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.9}
Can the explicit word compression and the direct
predecessor comparison be formalized first, with a small,
reusable interface independent of surreal arithmetic?
\end{question}

These are concrete, finite-dependency targets:
ordinal concatenation, numerical first difference,
injectivity, and well-order predecessor sets. The next
milestone is the general successor-cardinal obstruction,
followed by bounded-support completion and the
small-family interpolation theorem. This ordering keeps
the central algorithms separate from a formalization of
an entire higher-order set theory.

\subsubsection{Uniform mathematical constructions indexed by well-orders}

The Kanovei--Shelah method suggests using a definable
linear order of codes to index constructions without
selecting one privileged code. The surreal setting
raises additional smallness conditions.

\begin{question}\label{swo:n16.10}
Which finite-support or bounded-support constructions
can be indexed by a uniform class family of global
well-orders, and which require a genuine higher-order
index object?
\end{question}

A first investigation should specify its support sets,
evaluation maps, and quantifier domains before adding
algebra or model theory. The diagonal theorem prevents
an exhaustive class-code shortcut, but leaves many
useful uniform families available.

\subsection{Source 12's research questions and prioritized program}
\label{swo:st:sec:questions}

The following are proposed continuations. Except where an older question
is explicitly attributed, they are not claimed to be recognized open
problems in the literature.

\begin{question}[All fixed enumeration types]\label{swo:st:n14.1}
Determine $\bl(\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa}))$ for every ordinal $\alpha$ of
cardinality $2^{<\kappa}$, not only the minimal type. Can the answer be
expressed by a precise ordinal-sum invariant of admissible entry-code
lengths, together with the finite terminal permutation factor?
\end{question}
The singular theorem identifies the first obstruction that any such
formula must capture. A useful initial target is
$\alpha=\mu\cdot2$ and then $\mu\cdot\gamma+n$ for finite $n$.

\begin{question}[Noncardinal birthday bounds]\label{swo:st:n14.2}
For an arbitrary infinite ordinal $\theta$, classify the minimal
permutation order of $\No_{<\theta}$. Which features of the ordinal tail of
$\theta$, beyond $|\theta|$ and $|\No_{<\theta}|$, survive in its coding
rank and local character?
\end{question}
The cone argument for an initial cardinal relies on closure under
$i+1+\alpha$ below the cutoff. At a noncardinal cutoff that closure can
fail and should be replaced by a stratified family of cones.

\begin{question}[Isomorphism, not merely equimorphism]\label{swo:st:n14.3}
Classify the order topology and isomorphism invariants of
$\WO_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$. At regular cutoffs, and at singular strong limits,
what are its density, cellularity, cut-character spectra, and degrees of
homogeneity? Which distinguish it from other orders of the same binary
rank?
\end{question}
The binary cube itself cannot be the literal answer: it has endpoints
and adjacent pairs, while the surreal permutation order has different
local behavior. A dense suborder equimorphic with a cube can retain
substantial information not measured by rank.

\begin{question}[The hierarchy of proper-class blocks]\label{swo:st:n14.4}
Study the subpredicates of $\Hall(\No)$ with types
$\Ord\cdot\gamma+\alpha$ for fixed set ordinals $\gamma,\alpha$.
Give explicit, size-safe embedding and nonembedding theorems between
these subpredicates and the set-like order.
\end{question}
The inaccessible-model calculation provides concrete bounded targets and
shows that the full order is strictly more complex than the set-like
order there. Extending binary fusion to uniform transformations on
class predicates may require stronger comprehension; that dependence
should be proved, not assumed away.

\begin{remark}[Source 12's question ``The exact weak-choice strength'', answered]\label{swo:st:n14.5}
\emph{Source 12's text:} Remove set-level AC from the base theory in \cref{swo:st:thm:choice}. What
principle is equivalent to a class well-order of the sign-sequence
surreals then? Compare it with coherent well-ordering of power sets of
ordinals and with uniform ordinal presentations of transitive closures.

\merge\ \emph{Answered (2 October 2026).} Source 11's \cref{swo:cf:choice} proves the
equivalence over GB with no set-level choice: a class well-order of the
sign-sequence surreals is equivalent to global choice. Its proof is
precisely a uniform well-ordering of the power sets $V_{\beta+1}$,
obtained by set-valued recursion from the given well-order on the sign
sequences of each length $\theta$; see \cref{swo:rem:answered-choice}.
(Corrected on 3 October 2026 after the Hilbert's-tenth review
\path{review_surreal_synthesis_0be9b9134.md}: ``uniform'' replaces
``coherent'', since these orders need not extend one another;
\cref{swo:rem:answered-choice} gives a finite example.)
\end{remark}
This is separate from the question whether surreal universality for
class linear orders itself implies global choice, raised by Hamkins
\cite{HamkinsUnivChoice}. The present equivalence concerns a well-order of
all surreal labels and does not settle that universality question.

\begin{question}[Elementary common-prefix theory]\label{swo:st:n14.6}
Formalize \cref{swo:st:thm:fulllex} over a precisely chosen weak class theory.
How little comprehension and class well-foundedness are needed? Can one
characterize the same relation directly by a formula avoiding explicit
mention of the common-prefix class?
\end{question}
The definition already expands to elementary quantifiers. A mechanized
proof would make the separation from abstract class comparability
particularly transparent and yield a reusable theorem for other carriers.

\begin{question}[Automorphisms and finite condensation]\label{swo:st:n14.7}
Determine natural automorphism groups of the full lexicographic order,
and of the order after collapsing finite residual blocks. Which
operations arise from numerical automorphisms or permutations of the
underlying surreal carrier, and which genuinely act on enumeration
structure?
\end{question}
Finite-tail blocks are now characterized intrinsically by adjacency.
That makes condensation a plausible first invariant, but no complete
classification of its quotient is claimed here.

\begin{question}[Dependence on the class realization]\label{swo:st:n14.8}
Fix a transitive set universe $M$ and vary its admissible class collection
$\mathcal X$. Which external order invariants of the admitted global
well-orders detect this change? Can the order reconstruct useful
information about available truth predicates or class choice functions?
\end{question}
The diagonal obstruction persists internally, while external cardinality
can vary. This makes the distinction between full and Henkin semantics a
source of mathematical questions rather than merely a formal warning.

\begin{question}[Compatibility between birthday cutoffs]\label{swo:st:n14.9}
Construct and analyze coherent embeddings from the well-order spaces at
smaller birthday cutoffs into those at larger cutoffs. Which choices of
reserve labels and tail enumerations are functorial, and which preserve
finite condensation, coding ranks, or canonical cylinders?
\end{question}
Naively extending every enumeration by an arbitrary tail can change
minimal length, and fixed choices need not be compatible across three
cutoffs. A coherence theorem would make universe-lifting arguments much
more useful in a proof assistant.

\subsection{Source 09's research directions}
\label{swo:ec:sec:research}
The following are proposed problems emerging from the development, not
a claim that all are already catalogued open problems. Each is stated
with a foundational level so that its intended meaning is clear.

\subsubsection{Formal proof of the surreal core theorem}
\textbf{Framework:} universe-indexed Lean with explicit smallness and a
baseline parameter. Complete the prefix-extension and interpolation
modules, then prove the back-and-forth isomorphism. The difficult part
is expected to be the bookkeeping of small histories and variable
ordinal prefixes, not the finite first-disagreement arguments. A useful
first milestone is the inaccessible or regular-cardinal set-sized
version, parameterized by an abstract saturated alphabet.

\subsubsection{Exact axiomatic strength of the global conclusions}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GB$ with ordinary set choice but without global
choice. \Cref{swo:ec:prop:baseline-choice} settles the baseline question: a
set-like global well-order of $\No$ is equivalent to global choice.
Determine the exact strength of alternative universality and homogeneity
assertions that do not already assume such a baseline. In particular,
which conclusions can be stated and proved for individually definable
class orders without supplying a single uniform global enumeration?
Distinguish uniform existence assertions from a schema treating one
fixed definition at a time; the latter is not automatically a uniform
class construction.

\subsubsection{Which cuts of the core represent exhaustive branches?}
\textbf{Framework:} class cut parameters over $\Psupp(b)$ or an explicitly
higher-sorted completion. Every global enumeration determines a cut
in the dense core, and density makes this representation injective.
Characterize its image intrinsically. The missing-branch construction
shows that injectivity of a class word is insufficient: exhaustiveness
must be detected. A promising formulation separates coherence of set
prefixes, realizability of each next-coordinate cut, and eventual
coverage of every surreal value.

\subsubsection{Automorphisms beyond set-sized partial maps}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GBC$ for the core; higher-sort or universe-bounded
versions for the full comparison object. Set-sized partial
isomorphisms extend in the core, but proper-class partial maps need not.
Classify which preserve enough prefix or support structure to extend.
Also distinguish automorphisms of the bare order from those preserving
the preferred filtration by support bounds. These are different
classification problems even though the bare core is always $\No$.

\subsubsection{Non-set-like well-order relations}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GBC$ or $\GBC+\ETR$, with a fixed relation-code
coordinate order. Study the alternative binary comparison of all global
well-order relations. Which order properties depend on the coordinate
enumeration? Does it contain a natural set-coded dense core, and when
are its cuts represented by actual class well-orders? No conclusion
about that different comparison follows merely from the enumeration
results proved here.

\subsubsection{Sharp birthday and support bounds}
\textbf{Framework:} $\ZFC$ on bounded fragments. Given bounds on the
birthdays and first-disagreement coordinates of a set family, determine
optimal bounds for an interpolating prefix and its supported completion.
The present proof bounds the forced prefix length by
$\sup\{\Delta(E_i,F_j)+1:i\in I,j\in J\}+1$ and uses an oversized
cardinal for support. That bound is
safe but not generally minimal. This direction could yield concrete
complexity estimates for symbolic surreal order calculations.

\subsubsection{What survives away from inaccessible truncations?}
\textbf{Framework:} $\ZFC$ with specified cardinal arithmetic. Replace
the inaccessible $\kappa$ by a regular cardinal and a set alphabet with
appropriate cut saturation. Separate the roles of regularity,
$\kappa^{<\kappa}=\kappa$, and closure under the required cut constructor.
At singular cardinals, the first-disagreement bound can reach the
ambient length even for relatively small families; identify the
resulting interpolation spectrum and construct sharp counterexamples.

\subsubsection{Other termination conventions for set words}
\textbf{Framework:} $\GBC$ or bounded $\ZFC$. Our dictionary order makes
proper prefixes smaller and therefore creates the limit-prefix
suprema of \cref{swo:ec:prop:prefix-cf}. Study a distinguished internal
termination value, restricted alphabets, or prefix-free codes of set
well-orders. Determine exactly which variants have the set-cut property
and hence are isomorphic to $\No$. The convention must be part of the
statement, not an implicit analogy with surreal signs.

\subsubsection{Uniform infinitary constructions indexed by redundant codes}
\textbf{Framework:} bounded universes first. Kanovei--Shelah-style
redundant indexing suggests avoiding a choice of one representative
for each well-order or auxiliary object. Investigate constructions
using the support core or bounded strata as indices, while checking
that the resulting products, functions, and quotient relations remain
at the declared level. The diagonal theorem forbids a uniform
same-level list of all global enumerations, but does not preclude
purpose-built redundant families adequate for a particular theorem.

\subsection{Source 08's research questions and topics}\label{swo:sk:sec:research}

The following are directions not resolved by the present manuscript.
They are not blanket assertions that no relevant answer exists in the
literature. Each should begin with a targeted literature search and a
precise choice of size level.

\subsubsection{Set-sized enumeration orders}

\paragraph{1. Isomorphism classification beyond the common spectrum.}
The ordinal spectrum and cardinality of $\W(X)$ depend only on $|X|$,
while its local cylinder structure remembers the numerical order of
residual alphabets. Which additional invariants of $X$ can be recovered
from $\W(X)$? Determine sufficient and necessary conditions for
$\W(X)\cong\W(Y)$, rather than merely embeddings in both directions.
Dense alphabets, well-orders, and mixed sums provide natural test cases.

\paragraph{2. Exact invariants at regular cutoffs (\merge\ partly answered; answered 3 October 2026; see the notes after this list).}
For regular $\kappa$ with $2^{<\kappa}=\kappa$, compute the density,
cellularity, point characters, and cut cofinalities of
$\W_\kappa(\No_{<\kappa})$. The binary equimorphism in \eqref{swo:sk:eq:t6} does not by
itself determine its order-topological isomorphism type. Investigate
whether the support skeleton construction has a natural $\kappa$-sized
dense realization inside this set order under weaker assumptions than
strong inaccessibility.

\paragraph{3. Singular birthdays and code lengths (\merge\ answered in part; see the notes after this list).}
At singular $\kappa$, exactly which cuts of size below $\kappa$ fail to
be realized in $\No_{<\kappa}$ or in its fixed-length enumeration
order? Determine the least binary coding lengths for these orders and
how they depend on cofinality and cardinal arithmetic. The three
specific uses of regularity in \cref{swo:sk:thm:cutoff} identify where a new
argument is needed.

\paragraph{4. Prescribed noninitial lengths.}
For $\alpha$ of cardinality $\kappa$, classify
$\W_\alpha(\No_{<\lambda})$. Finite tails are understood through
\cref{swo:sk:thm:adjacent}, but noninitial limit lengths may preserve finer
lexicographic complexity. Compare this problem with the fixed-type
analysis proposed in the continuum manuscript \cite{Batch76Source02}, checking
its hypotheses and proofs independently for nonseparable alphabets.

\subsubsection{The skeleton and the virtual ambient order}

\paragraph{5. Definable choices of the surreal isomorphism.}
The back-and-forth isomorphism $\Psupp(b)\cong\No$ depends on witness
choices. With a specified global well-order, can it be chosen to
respect useful support or birthday bounds? What additional
normalization gives uniqueness, if any? Distinguish definability from
parameters, parameter-free definability, and invariance under a change
of baseline.

\paragraph{6. Automorphisms and extension from a skeleton.}
An order automorphism $\varphi$ of $\No$ acts on $\Hsl$ by
$e\mapsto\varphi\circ e$ and sends $O_b$ onto $O_{\varphi\circ b}$.
Which automorphisms of one skeleton extend to uniform automorphisms of
the full virtual order? Can order alone recognize eventual-agreement
orbits, or are these additional structure supplied by the coordinate
presentation?

\paragraph{7. Full virtual lexicographic products (\merge\ answered 3 October 2026; see the notes after this list).}
For an ordinary class carrier, every set-indexed lexicographic power
of $\No$ embeds into a skeleton. The \emph{full virtual} product
$\Hsl\times_{\lex}\Hsl$ is a different object. Does it admit a uniform
order embedding into $\Hsl$? More generally, determine an absorption
spectrum for uniform virtual powers. Simply concatenating two
$\Ord$-long words has domain $\Ord+\Ord$, not a set-like $\Ord$
domain, so the set-sized concatenation argument is unavailable.

\paragraph{8. Higher-size cuts and completion (\merge\ answered 3 October 2026 for cuts of the core; see the notes after this list).}
The set-cut theorem deliberately leaves out cuts specified by proper
class families of enumeration codes or by higher collections of
classes. Classify which such cuts are realized once a precise
higher-type language is chosen. A proposed Dedekind completion must
identify the type of its cut objects and cannot be treated as another
ordinary class without a size proof.

\paragraph{9. Classification of relation-code orders.}
For two global coordinate enumerations $q,q'$ of $\No^2$, the
relation-code orders have the same binary equimorphism type. Are there
useful hypotheses yielding an isomorphism? Determine which invariants
are artifacts of the coordinate order and which reflect genuine
properties of class well-orders.

\subsubsection{Foundations and formalization}

\paragraph{10. Minimal axioms, stated theorem by theorem.}
Separate the strength of a baseline $\Ord\cong\No$, uniform prefix
completion, orbit cut filling, and the global back-and-forth theorem.
Over variants of $\GB$ with set Choice, which global selection
principles are necessary for their uniform formulations? The present
proofs establish sufficiency of $\GBC$, not an exact reverse-mathematical
classification.

\paragraph{11. Comparison of non-set-like class well-orders (\merge\ answered; see the note after this list).}
Formulate an explicit alignment or comparison principle for arbitrary
class well-orders and locate its recursion requirements. Which
restricted domains, such as finite sums of $\Ord$ and set ordinals,
admit direct elementary algorithms? A theorem about all class domains
should not be extrapolated from these examples without proof.

\paragraph{12. Dependence on the class collection.}
For fixed $M$ and $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal D$, compare the virtual
orders of global enumerations in $(M,\mathcal C)$ and
$(M,\mathcal D)$. The same set-coded skeleton relative to a shared
baseline remains available, but new class rows may appear. Study which
higher-size cut properties, operator embeddings, and definability
properties change.

\paragraph{13. Quantitative and certified prefix extension.}
Formalize the support bound in \cref{swo:sk:lem:extension}, the forced-prefix
length in \cref{swo:sk:thm:orbitcut}, and the birthday of its stopping entry.
This would make the central theorem a sequence of explicit bounded
lemmas rather than one monolithic existence proof. It is a strong
first target for the repository's existing small-cut interface.

\paragraph{14. Increasing-subset and alternate-termination orders (\merge\ answered 3 October 2026 except one type; see the notes after this list).}
Study lexicographic orders of numerically increasing set sequences,
as opposed to arbitrary enumerations, and compare prefix-small,
prefix-large, and centered-termination conventions. The limit-prefix
counterexample shows that these choices affect local cofinalities even
when the alphabet is $\No$.

\paragraph{15. An order-theoretic interface for class nonstandard models.}
Determine which part of a Kanovei--Shelah-style indexing construction
can use a set-coded skeleton and which genuinely needs a larger
collection. Keep the order embedding problem separate from the
existence of a class ultrafilter, satisfaction relation, or transfer
principle. A successful construction should include an explicit
uniform-family and smallness audit at every step.
