\subsection{Source 13: further research questions and proposed projects}\label{swo:fs:sec:questions}

These questions are proposed continuations of the present development,
not a claim that each is a previously published open problem. The
prefix-trace criterion, the first-failure classification, and the
negative pure-order cylinder result settle the versions stated here;
the questions below ask for stronger or different conclusions.

\subsubsection{Cuts, trees, and enriched structure}

\begin{question}[Minimal extra structure for recognizing branches]\label{swo:fs:n15.1}
What is the weakest expansion of the pure core order $\Psupp(b)\cong\No$
that makes its branch traces recognizable? Is the family of all
cylinders enough as an unranked family, or must one retain the
prefix-length relation? Can a support filtration recover the necessary
levels without explicitly naming prefixes?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:fs:thm:nonrigidity} shows that the pure order alone cannot
canonically recover the original cylinder family. The positive target
is therefore an enriched reconstruction theorem, not a repetition of
the disproved pure-order assertion.

\begin{question}[Automorphisms preserving a chosen core]\label{swo:fs:n15.2}
Classify the uniform order automorphisms of $\Hsl$ that preserve the
specific eventual-agreement core $\Psupp(b)$. Which preserve its support
filtration, and which preserve the set of exhaustive traces after an
isomorphism between two cores? Does adding birthday or simplicity
information force a substantial rigidity theorem?
\end{question}
The finite-block automorphisms need not preserve the baseline orbit.
A useful initial project is to characterize tail alphabet
transformations that do preserve it.

\begin{question}[A normal form for class cuts]\label{swo:fs:n15.3}
Can the branch/horizontal/limit-boundary trichotomy be organized into a
canonical recursive notation for every available normalized cut?
For horizontal cuts, how much of the next-label cut can be encoded by
surreal simplicity data? What uniqueness survives when changes of
prefix presentation are allowed?
\end{question}
A complete class-cut collection is not an ordinary class object in
$\GBC$. The first implementation should concern one supplied class cut
or one uniform class-indexed family, before introducing a higher sort.

\begin{question}[Sharp cutoff analogues]\label{swo:fs:n15.4}
For a birthday fragment $X_\kappa$, determine which part of the
first-failure classification survives when prefix extension can fail
through exhaustion, complement-cardinality mismatch, or a missing
label separator. Can these three obstructions be combined with the
singular strong-limit transition into a practical classification of
cut characters in fixed-length strata?
\end{question}
This asks for more than substituting $X_\kappa$ into the global theorem;
the hypotheses that must be replaced are explicitly identified in
\Cref{swo:fs:swf:sec:fixed}.

\subsubsection{Products, comprehension, and model dependence}

\begin{question}[The weakest uniform split obstruction]\label{swo:fs:n15.5}
Over $\GBC$, what additional comprehension principle suffices to rule
out a fixed-formula uniform embedding $\Hsl\times_{\lex}2\to \Hsl$?
Can the inverse-evaluator argument be reduced to a restricted
existential-class comprehension schema? For more restrictive formulas
defining the proposed embedding, is there an elementary diagonal
argument avoiding that comprehension altogether?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:fs:thm:kmsplit} gives a sufficient theory and identifies
the point to optimize. It is not a proof that full $\KM$ is necessary.

\begin{question}[A hierarchy beyond one split]\label{swo:fs:n15.6}
In a full inaccessible universe, classify the mutual embeddability
of ${\Hsl}^n_{\lex}$ for finite $n\geq2$, of $\Hsl\times_{\lex}K$ for
various right factors $K$, and of iterated point-splittings. Which
invariants distinguish these orders after the first dense-core
obstruction has saturated at cardinality $2^\kappa$?
\end{question}
All these orders can have the same cardinality, so a useful invariant
must record more than the number of elements. Families of disjoint
intervals, patterns of adjacent pairs, and iterated condensation are
natural candidates.

\begin{question}[Class realizations with intermediate behavior]\label{swo:fs:n15.7}
For a fixed set model $M$, how do different collections of available
classes $\mathcal C$ affect the external density, cellularity, and
product-embedding behavior of its enumeration order? Which
intermediate behaviors lie between the externally countable rational
case and the full inaccessible-universe obstruction?
\end{question}
A precise answer should state whether a map is arbitrary external,
definable over the two-sorted model, or coded in an additional sort.
Those are distinct classification problems.

\begin{question}[Uniformity versus external isomorphism]\label{swo:fs:n15.8}
For an externally countable model, can the complexity of an external
isomorphism $\Hsl\cong\mathbb Q$ be measured relative to presentations
of its set and class sorts? What information about the model is
necessary to compute, define, or select such an isomorphism?
\end{question}
This connects the order-theoretic collapse to computability and model
presentation without mistaking an external construction for a class
available internally.

\subsubsection{Termination, bounds, and residual orders}

\begin{question}[A classification of termination cuts]\label{swo:fs:n15.9}
For a class alphabet order-isomorphic to $\No$, characterize the
placements of an extra terminal marker for which arbitrary set-word
or injective set-word lexicography is set-cut saturated. What happens
when the marker is placed immediately on one side of an existing
label, rather than reserving that label? Can the answer be expressed
in terms of the two characters of the marker cut?
\end{question}
The end-first and end-last failures and the reserved-central success
are settled here. They need not exhaust all intermediate behavior.

\begin{question}[Optimal birthday and support bounds]\label{swo:fs:n15.10}
For prescribed bounds on input birthdays, word length, and baseline
indices, sharpen the prefix-length and support-cardinality bounds in
\Cref{swo:fs:thm:interpolate}. Is the explicit central-code birthday
sum optimal within a useful class of prefix-free local codes? Which
bounds are compatible with embeddings across birthday cutoffs?
\end{question}
The current support completion deliberately chooses a large cardinal
to equalize complements. It proves existence, not optimality.

\begin{question}[Iterating raw residual decomposition]\label{swo:fs:n15.11}
The ordinal-head fiber theorem removes one set-like initial part.
How far can residual decomposition be iterated with set-valued codes,
and what class-recursion principles are needed when an iteration has
class-valued stages? Is there a canonical rank or notation for a
substantial family of raw class well-orders beyond the first head?
\end{question}
This is where $\ETR$ or a stronger scheme could become genuinely
relevant. The elementary one-head construction alone does not justify
an arbitrary iteration.

\begin{question}[Relation-code dependence]\label{swo:fs:n15.12}
For two set-like enumerations of pairs, determine which
transformations relate their relation-bit orders on raw well-orders.
When do the two induced orders become isomorphic, merely equimorphic,
or distinct under definability restrictions? Which code orders can
be characterized by simple invariants of the pair enumeration?
\end{question}

\subsubsection{A concrete formalization milestone}

\begin{question}[First checked extension]\label{swo:fs:n15.13}
Formalize the split-order density lemma and the crossing-prefix
uniqueness/reconstruction argument in a size-explicit abstract setting.
Then instantiate the small-cut and fresh-value interfaces using
\code{SignSequenceCut.lean}. Can the central-word saturation theorem
be completed without introducing surreal field arithmetic?
\end{question}
The answer to the last design question should be positive at the
mathematical level: the proof uses only order, the reserved marker,
smallness, and fresh set-cut separators. Establishing this dependency
boundary in Lean would be a useful substantial first checked result.

% ---- source 14 (batch-81 manuscript 02), lines 1766-1926
\subsection{Source 14: further research questions and priorities}
\label{swo:tc:sec:questions}
The following are proposed continuations of the present work. They are
not all established named open problems in the literature. In particular,
the prefix-structured exhaustive-cut question and the support-cardinal
threshold are now answered by the theorems above; the questions here
state stronger or different targets rather than restating those results.

\subsubsection{Cut recognition beyond the named prefix structure}
\begin{question}[The exhaustive-trace stabilizer]\label{swo:tc:n14.1}
Characterize the subgroup of class order automorphisms of $\Psupp(b)$
that preserves the exhaustive-trace collection. How does it compare
with the groups preserving all prefix cylinders, or all label incidences?
Can it be generated by explicit transformations of enumeration structure?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:tc:thm:orbits} classifies the bare-order cut orbits and
\Cref{swo:tc:cor:nonintrinsic} proves that this stabilizer is proper.
What remains is its structure, not the now-answered yes/no question
whether every core automorphism preserves exhaustive representability.

\begin{question}[Minimal enrichment for exhaustiveness]\label{swo:tc:n14.2}
Can the coverage predicate be recovered from cylinder inclusion and
numerical order of children without naming the label evaluation itself?
What additional incidence relation records that the same surreal label
appears at different possible coordinates?
\end{question}
Coherence is essentially a branch property of the cylinder tree, whereas
exhaustiveness compares labels along that branch with the entire
alphabet. Separating these logical resources should clarify exactly
what the recognition theorem uses.

\subsubsection{The support hierarchy beyond one saturation invariant}
\begin{question}[Isomorphism of support layers]\label{swo:tc:n14.3}
For infinite cardinals $\kappa,\lambda$ with
$\cf\kappa=\cf\lambda$, when are
$\mathcal P_{<\kappa}(b)$ and $\mathcal P_{<\lambda}(b)$ isomorphic
as bare class linear orders? Does some cut invariant recover more than
the cofinality of the support threshold?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:tc:thm:support} separates layers with different cofinalities
but leaves this equal-cofinality case untouched. Their shared embedded
copy of $\No$ is too weak to decide it. The attained minimum support
cost is an invariant of the \emph{support-enriched} structure, not yet
an invariant of its bare order.

\begin{question}[Support ideals]\label{swo:tc:n14.4}
Replace the cardinality condition by an ideal of permitted set supports.
Under what closure and permutation-invariance hypotheses is saturation
controlled by the ideal's additivity? Can a failure of union closure
always be converted into a coherent prefix configuration forcing a
support outside the ideal?
\end{question}
The compression lemma bounds cardinality, not membership in an arbitrary
ideal: it can adjoin images of moved coordinates and a buffer. Therefore
a general ideal theorem needs explicit closure under those operations.
It would be incorrect simply to replace $<\kappa$ by ``belongs to the
ideal'' in the existing proof.

\begin{question}[Optimal simultaneous support cost]\label{swo:tc:n14.5}
Given a specific separated set family, characterize the least support
cardinality of a separator by its forced-prefix tree, rather than only
by the union of all input supports. Can the finite version be computed
without enumerating all possible separator permutations?
\end{question}
The sharp examples attain the threshold, but many input supports contain
coordinates irrelevant to their comparisons. The first-outside-support
argument suggests an algorithmic pruning principle. Finite optimization
and the transfinite cardinal minimum should be studied separately.

\subsubsection{Raw tails, condensation, and alternative comparison orders}
\begin{question}[Iterated initial-branch quotients]\label{swo:tc:n14.6}
After quotienting raw well-orders by their first $\Ord$-long branch,
can one iterate a similarly explicit trace construction to recover
successive proper-class blocks? What can be proved for prescribed
block patterns without assuming a canonical class ordinal for every
well-order?
\end{question}
The trace-fiber theorem completely describes the first loss of
information. Iterating it along class-valued histories may require
stronger recursion principles. The exact point at which elementary
comprehension ceases to suffice should be isolated as a theorem.

\begin{question}[Automorphisms of raw trace fibers]\label{swo:tc:n14.7}
Which automorphisms of the branch order extend to the unrestricted
well-order order, and what compatibility conditions do the residual
alphabets impose? Which automorphisms preserve finite residual blocks
but fail to preserve the core-trace quotient?
\end{question}
The singleton omitted-label fiber shows that being a singleton is not
enough to recognize the exhaustive suborder. Any extension theorem must
also account for residual alphabets with more than one label.

\begin{question}[Relation-code comparison]\label{swo:tc:n14.8}
For a specified coordinate schedule on pairs of surreal labels, classify
the class cuts represented by genuine well-order relations. Is there a
useful analogue of crossing cylinders that detects transitivity,
linearity, and well-foundedness from a coherent branch of relation bits?
\end{question}
Coherent binary bits always define a relation, but well-foundedness is a
global constraint. The strong reconstruction phenomenon for exhaustive
enumerations may not carry over. A schedule-independent theorem must
explicitly quantify which coordinate changes it tolerates.

\subsubsection{Birthday cutoffs and universe coherence}
\begin{question}[Exact local geometry of set slices]\label{swo:tc:n14.9}
For $\mu=2^{<\kappa}$, determine the complete cut-character spectrum of
$\W_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$, especially when $\mu>\kappa$ and at
singular cutoffs. Which parts of the crossing-cylinder proof survive
when deleting a long used prefix can exhaust intervals of the alphabet?
\end{question}
This continues an unfilled target of the predecessor. The global proof
uses the fact that deleting \emph{any set} leaves plentiful fresh
surreals; a fixed birthday fragment lacks that unrestricted property.
The inherited binary equimorphism does not decide the local characters.

\begin{question}[Coherent embeddings across cutoffs]\label{swo:tc:n14.10}
Construct explicit embeddings between enumeration spaces for increasing
birthday bounds that compose coherently. Which preserve the minimal
allowed enumeration type, the prefix cylinders, or the relevant support
filtration?
\end{question}
Appending an arbitrary tail preserves a first disagreement but may
change the ordinal type. A functorial construction should record both
the alphabet inclusion and the position schedule, rather than silently
identify cardinally equivalent domains.

\subsubsection{Class realizations and proof strength}
\begin{question}[Which new cuts can a class extension add?]\label{swo:tc:n14.11}
For a fixed set model and old baseline, characterize the additional
exhaustive trace cuts admitted by specified class extensions. Can the
new-cut collection distinguish natural classes of realizations even
when their old-cut realizability relations agree?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:tc:thm:absolute} supplies a rigidity constraint: no old cut
changes status. It does not classify the new parameters. The tail fibers
also suggest studying extensions that add raw orders with an old trace
but a new tail.

\begin{question}[Axiomatic economy]\label{swo:tc:n14.12}
What is the weakest class theory proving the crossing-chain trichotomy
and its reconstruction theorem once a baseline and fresh-separator
property are supplied? Can the proof of the support threshold be
formalized in a set-only regular-cardinal model before passing to
classes?
\end{question}
The existing proofs visibly use elementary comprehension and class
Replacement, plus set Choice for extensions. Identifying which are
essential is more informative than merely observing that a stronger
class theory also proves the theorem.

\begin{question}[First kernel-verified milestone]\label{swo:tc:n14.13}
Can the common-prefix comparison and the support-compression lemma be
formalized as small reusable Lean modules, then independently connected
to the pinned surreal sign-sequence library?
\end{question}
These targets avoid the largest foundational infrastructure while
capturing the most error-prone finite and cardinal bookkeeping. A
useful deliverable would include separate tests for fixed-position
preservation, complement cardinalities, and the distinction between
strict right character and the character of a normalized cut complement.

multiplicities, \cref{swo:sh:thm:gap-multiplicities}), at every cutoff,
including $\mu>\kappa$ and singular $\kappa$. \Cref{swo:tc:n14.11} is answered
in part by source~17's \cref{swo:gs:thm:class-extension} (every proper same-set
extension adds new represented cuts), \cref{swo:tc:n14.6} in part by the block
decomposition (\cref{swo:ix:note:blocks}), and \cref{swo:tc:n14.1} bears on
source~17's extension criterion (\cref{swo:gs:thm:extension-criterion}), which
identifies the stabilizer of the represented-cut predicate abstractly.
\Cref{swo:tc:n14.10} is source~12's \cref{swo:st:n14.9}. The others remain
open.

\subsection{Source 15: further research questions and a prioritized program}\label{swo:cb:sec:questions}

\begin{question}[All fixed enumeration types]\label{swo:cb:n13.1}
Write $\alpha=\mu\cdot\gamma+\zeta$ with $\zeta<\mu$ infinite.
Classify the possible residual numerical suborders left after the long
prefix, and use them to compute $\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa})$.
The theorem here handles exactly finite $\zeta$. A useful first family
is $\zeta=\omega$, followed by regular and singular infinite remainders.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Noncardinal birthday bounds]\label{swo:cb:n13.2}
For an arbitrary ordinal $\theta$, determine the order structure of
$\No_{<\theta}$ and its permutation strata. The cone and ordinal
absorption arguments for an initial cardinal need not survive unchanged.
Identify which ordinal invariants of $\theta$ replace the present
regular/singular dichotomy.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[The exact strength of arbitrary-input condensation]\label{swo:cb:n13.3}
Does GB prove a uniform class coding all finite condensations of every
class well-order? If not, determine a sharp sufficient and necessary
principle. Then study longer histories with specified limit intersections.
The explicit polynomial examples show that existence for particular long
histories alone is insufficient to calibrate the general scheme.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Intrinsic information in the full raw order]\label{swo:cb:n13.4}
Which prefix cones, first-block fibres, and finite residual blocks are
definable from the bare lexicographic order of raw well-orders?
\Cref{swo:cb:thm:automorphism} shows that the abstract core does not
determine its represented cuts. Determine how much extra structure is
needed for reconstruction, and whether the full raw order restores any
of the lost distinctions.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Completion with residual data]\label{swo:cb:n13.5}
Construct and characterize a stratified completion that contains all
terminal cuts while recording the residual well-order fibres over persistent
branches. Determine its universal property and its minimum required size
level. Ordinary Dedekind completion alone loses the residual data.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Automorphism extension]\label{swo:cb:n13.6}
Characterize those automorphisms of a bounded-support core that preserve
persistent cuts, preserve exhaustive cuts, or extend to native global
enumerations. Compare cores built from baselines differing on a proper
class of positions. The abstract isomorphism of two cores does not decide
their placement inside the surrounding order.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Finer topology of bounded slices]\label{swo:cb:n13.7}
After the density, cellularity, and point-character calculations, classify
the exact gap spectra, local bases, and isomorphism types of the bounded
permutation spaces. Equimorphism with a binary product does not determine
all these invariants. Study which distinctions survive when cardinal
arithmetic makes displayed density values coincide.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Inverse ranks and prescribed relation scans]\label{swo:cb:n13.8}
Classify the cuts and point characters of ordinal-rank lexicography beyond
the points $M_\lambda$. For table lexicography, use endpoint transfer to
characterize scans whose extremal linear-order table is well-founded or
set-like. Then seek invariants beyond the three possible endpoint patterns.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Coherent restricted filtrations]\label{swo:cb:n13.9}
The three-label theorem rules out monotonicity for every restriction.
Which nested chains of carriers, or which restricted families of orders,
admit a useful monotone restriction system? Can birthday cutoffs be linked
by canonical order embeddings rather than by unrestricted deletion?
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Naturally well-ordered supports]\label{swo:cb:n13.10}
Characterize the image and omitted cuts of
$A\mapsto-\sum_{a\in A}\omega^{-a}$. Compare shorter-first and
longer-first orders on increasing set words, and develop a higher-level
analogue that treats proper-class supports without calling the result a
single surreal normal form.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Class-model dependence]\label{swo:cb:n13.11}
For a fixed set universe $M$, study changes in the lexicographic theory as
the class realization grows from $\mathcal C$ to $\mathcal C'$.
Which statements about existing orders are absolute, which require
well-foundedness preservation, and which detect newly available cuts or
enumerations? Keep full-class and Henkin interpretations separate.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[First formal milestones]\label{swo:cb:n13.12}
Formalize the set-prefix common-disagreement formula and the elementary
set-interval quotient before the entire class theory. Next verify the
binary scheduler and finite-fibre fusion; then the persistent-cut
reconstruction with explicit smallness. These have concise interfaces and
clear failure cases, making them useful independent additions to ProveIt.
\end{question}

The most concrete next mathematical projects are the smaller infinite-tail
classification, exact bounded gap spectra, and the automorphism-extension
criterion. The most concrete foundational project is the arbitrary-input
condensation scheme. Each now has a precise point where the proved
construction stops, rather than an undifferentiated request to study
``all well-orders.''

\subsection{Source 16: further research questions, with the resolved parts removed}
\label{swo:ds:sec:research}

The following are proposed continuation problems, not a census of
currently open problems in the literature. In particular, the exact
termination family, represented-cut recognition with the labelled prefix
tree, simultaneous residual blocks, and the stated regular-stage
topological invariants have been settled under the assumptions of this
article. They should not be relisted as wholly open.

\subsubsection{Highest-priority structural problems}

\begin{question}[Longer-stratum binary coding ranks]\label{swo:ds:n16.1}
For $\No_{<\kappa}$ and $\mu=2^{<\kappa}$, determine the least
ordinal $\rho$ for which $\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa})\emb2^\rho_{\lex}$ for
every $|\alpha|=\mu$, and determine the reverse cube embeddings.
\end{question}
The topology is now known for all these strata, but it does not determine
binary coding rank. The singular strong-limit transition
\eqref{swo:ds:eq:singular} and the finite residual permutation blocks give
concrete starting cases. The first targets should be $\alpha=\mu+1$,
$\mu+2$, and $\mu+\omega$, with separate treatment of singular
strong-limit $\kappa$.

\begin{question}[Singular birthday gaps]\label{swo:ds:n16.2}
Determine the unfilled cut-character spectrum of
$\WO_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$ when $\kappa$ is singular, and when $\kappa$ is
regular but $\mu>\kappa$.
\end{question}
The global characters $\cf(\kappa)$ and the exact density
$\mu^{<\mu}$ are known here. The missing information is local: which
numerical gaps in the truncated alphabet combine with exhaustion and
prefix edges to produce each pair of cofinalities? The bounded
first-failure analysis should be formulated before attempting a general
classification by cardinal arithmetic alone.

\begin{question}[Centered increasing words]\label{swo:ds:n16.3}
Classify the order of numerically increasing set-length words when the
termination symbol is placed at a fixed interior numerical threshold.
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:ds:thm:alltermination} covers unrestricted and injective
words. The increasing case has prefix-dependent available alphabets and
already fails the centered saturation theorem. A useful first problem is
to determine all point characters for the $0^-$ and $0^+$ placements,
including words that cross the threshold only at a limit stage.

\begin{question}[Recovering prefix structure from order alone]\label{swo:ds:n16.4}
Which features of the labelled prefix tree can be reconstructed from the
bare order $\Pbd(b)$, from $\Hsl$ as a definable comparison, or from $\Hall$?
\end{question}
Our cut recognition uses the family of cylinders and numerical labels as
extra predicates. A bare core is isomorphic to $\No$, and singleton
raw fibers can arise either from an exhaustive branch or from a branch
omitting one label. Thus neither the core order nor the size of a fiber
immediately identifies exhaustion. One can ask for the least additional
predicates that make the tree and exhaustion relation definable.

\begin{question}[Changing baselines and extending automorphisms]\label{swo:ds:n16.5}
For two baselines $b,c$, characterize when an automorphism of the
set-like global comparison carries $\Pbd(b)$ onto
$\Pbd(c)$.
\end{question}
An increasing numerical automorphism $h$ gives the explicit example
$E\mapsto h\circ E$, carrying $\Pbd(b)$ onto
$\Pbd(h\circ b)$. General abstract isomorphisms between the
two cores need not preserve the distinguished set of exhaustive
branch cuts. \Cref{swo:ds:thm:cutrecognition} suggests an extension
criterion stated in terms of precisely those cuts.

\subsubsection{Foundational problems with explicit targets}

\begin{question}[Exact strength of uniform nonembedding]\label{swo:ds:n16.6}
Can the conclusion of \Cref{swo:ds:thm:sigma} for elementary
transformation formulas be proved in GBC alone? If not, what is its
reverse-mathematical strength?
\end{question}
The missing step is sharply localized: forming the inverse evaluator
\eqref{swo:ds:eq:inverseeval}. A lower bound would need a model in which a
specified elementary transformation exists or a reduction from a
comprehension principle. The mere presence of an existential class
quantifier in the present proof does not establish necessity.

\begin{question}[Repeated condensation of the quotient]\label{swo:ds:n16.7}
Determine the strength and possible stabilization behavior of the
transfinite tower obtained by repeatedly taking least representatives
of set-interval blocks and intersecting at limits.
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:ds:thm:blocks} has removed the need for ETR to extract all
blocks of one order. The new question concerns repeated condensation
of the resulting index orders. Suitable ETR is a sufficient bound;
whether this particular operator needs it, and which class orders can
remain nontrivial at prescribed stages, are separate questions.

\begin{question}[Choice needed for the word isomorphisms]\label{swo:ds:n16.8}
How far can \Cref{swo:ds:thm:wordisomorphism,swo:ds:thm:alltermination} be proved without a global well-order?
\end{question}
Their explicit embeddings and the termination saturation criterion use
less than the GBC back-and-forth isomorphisms. Investigate whether
set choice, a restricted class-enumeration principle, or a canonical
sign construction suffices for particular cases. This does not settle
the broader historical question about the choice strength of universal
embeddability into $\No$.

\begin{question}[Class extensions and canonical data]\label{swo:ds:n16.9}
For a fixed set universe with two admitted-class expansions, describe
which new branch cuts, global well-orders, and uniform transformations
become available.
\end{question}
Shared relations retain the same internal well-foundedness under GBC,
but the available class graphs can change. It is useful to distinguish
absoluteness of the elementary formulas for blocks and recognition
from existence of their class parameters or of the transformations
being considered.

\subsubsection{Formalization and quantitative coding}

\begin{question}[A first verified theorem package]\label{swo:ds:n16.10}
Implement the set-alphabet ordinal spectrum and the
$\mu,\mu+1,\mu+2$ versus later-strata density theorem, then
instantiate them at the small birthday carriers already in ProveIt.
\end{question}
This package would verify both the combinatorial mechanism and its
smallness boundaries without first formalizing arbitrary class models.
The two-point-fiber case is a particularly useful regression target:
counting jumps as disjoint open intervals would produce a false proof.

\begin{question}[Quantitative compatibility of the constructions]\label{swo:ds:n16.11}
Find sharp birthday and support bounds for prefix completion,
termination encodings, and the tree isomorphisms; determine which maps
commute with increasing birthday cutoffs.
\end{question}
Equation~\eqref{swo:ds:eq:centeredbirthday} is explicit, while the global
back-and-forth isomorphisms generally are not birthday-minimal.
Compatibility should mean equality or a specified coherent commuting
diagram of maps, not only the existence of unrelated embeddings at
each stage.

\subsection{Source 17: further research questions and a prioritized program}
\label{swo:gs:sec:questions}

These questions are continuations of this article, not claims that each
is a historically catalogued open problem. The results above narrow their
scope: questions about minimal-slice characters, the displayed gap
spectrum, or mere recognition with the full labelled prefix structure
are no longer left open within this development.

\subsubsection{Set-sized order geometry}
\begin{question}[Nonminimal enumeration types]\label{swo:gs:n15.1}
For $|\alpha|=\mu=2^{<\kappa}$, classify the characters, gap spectrum,
density, and binary coding length of $\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa})$.
Begin with $\alpha=\mu\cdot2$ and $\mu+n$.
\end{question}
A prefix can now use $\mu$ labels before exhausting its coordinate
domain, so residual alphabets can be small, have endpoints, or be finite.
The proof of \Cref{swo:gs:thm:gap-spectrum} suggests replacing the single
residual-alphabet interface by a tree whose nodes carry their actual
residual order types. A theorem expressed only in $|\alpha|$ cannot
capture all such effects.

\begin{question}[Noncardinal birthday cutoffs]\label{swo:gs:n15.2}
Replace the initial cardinal $\kappa$ by an arbitrary infinite ordinal
$\theta$. Which local invariants depend on the ordinal tail of $\theta$,
not merely on $|\theta|$ and $|\No_{<\theta}|$?
\end{question}
Our cone argument uses $\delta+\gamma<\kappa$ for smaller ordinals.
That property fails at many noncardinal cutoffs. A useful first target
is a cutoff of the form $\kappa+\omega$, followed by $\kappa\cdot2$,
with the contributions of each birthday layer kept separate.

\begin{question}[Isomorphism after the invariant calculation]\label{swo:gs:n15.3}
When do two minimal permutation orders with the same values of $r,q$,
$\mu^{<\mu}$ and the same gap spectrum have the same order type?
Which additional invariants distinguish them?
\end{question}
The explicit gap classification provides more information than binary
equimorphism, but still need not determine an order. Candidate invariants
include the arrangement of cylinder-boundary cuts, densities of particular
convex suborders, and the interaction of branch cuts with a chosen prefix
filtration. No general isomorphism conclusion is asserted here.

\begin{question}[Beyond the proved fusion length]\label{swo:gs:n15.4}
Determine the least size of a family of dense open sets whose intersection
fails to be dense. When $q=\omega$, determine complete metrizability and
more precise descriptive topological properties directly from the
permutation presentation.
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:gs:thm:fusion} supplies a lower bound: every family of size at
most $q$ succeeds. For longer constructions, intermediate prefixes can
already have length $\mu$, so the simple small-history argument no longer
applies. This is an obstruction to that proof, not a proof that longer
fusion always fails.

\subsubsection{Global branches, automorphisms, and class realizations}
\begin{question}[The extendible automorphism group]\label{swo:gs:n15.5}
Describe the stabilizer of the represented-cut predicate in
$\operatorname{Aut}(\Psupp(b))$. Can one characterize it by preservation of fewer predicates
than the entire labelled cylinder and coverage structure?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:gs:thm:extension-criterion} identifies this stabilizer abstractly,
and \Cref{swo:gs:thm:nonextension} shows it is proper. The remaining task
is a useful structural description. Numerical relabellings give a
natural family, but need not exhaust it.

\begin{question}[Changing baselines]\label{swo:gs:n15.6}
For two baselines $b,b'$, when does an automorphism of $\Hsl$ carry
$\Psupp(b)$ onto $\Psupp(b')$? How does the answer depend on their
eventual-agreement classes and on their represented-cut predicates?
\end{question}
Relabelling by an increasing numerical bijection is sufficient when it
carries one baseline to the other. Abstract order-isomorphism of the two
cores is not sufficient by itself; the obstruction proved here explains
why the represented cuts must enter the analysis.

\begin{question}[Recovering a class realization]\label{swo:gs:n15.7}
What information about $\mathcal X$ can be reconstructed from the labelled
core together with its admitted represented cuts? What is lost if the
baseline and cylinder predicates are forgotten?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:gs:thm:class-extension} detects every proper same-set extension
through new represented cuts. Its pair encoding recovers an individual
ordinal subclass from a suitable enumeration. A stronger reconstruction
should specify the decoding language and distinguish existence of
individual codes from a universal truth or satisfaction predicate.

\begin{question}[Iterated proper-class blocks]\label{swo:gs:n15.8}
Determine the precise recursion strength needed to organize successive
canonical $\Ord$-blocks of a raw well-order along a prescribed index
order. Compare finite iteration, set-length iteration, and class-length
iteration.
\end{question}
One extraction is elementary; iterating a procedure whose state is a
class can require more. The distinctions involving $\ETR$ in
\cite{GitmanHamkins} provide the appropriate setting for a reverse-
mathematical analysis. Our direct comparison and branch recognition do
not by themselves solve this recursion problem.

\begin{question}[The condensed unrestricted order]\label{swo:gs:n15.9}
Classify the dense comparison obtained by collapsing the finite components
of \Cref{swo:gs:thm:condensation}. Which residual fibres remain detectable
from its bare order, and what embeds into it?
\end{question}
Finite adjacency is now fully described. The quotient can still contain
nontrivial fibres with infinite or proper-class residual carrier. It
would be incorrect to conclude from density alone that it is the set-like
order or an ordinary surreal-sized class.

\subsubsection{Effective bounds, coherence, and verification}
\begin{question}[Ordinal and birthday optima for supported completion]\label{swo:gs:n15.10}
Refine the cardinal reserve formula to optimal ordinal support bounds and
optimal birthdays of canonical support codes. Which optima are uniform
without an additional global choice parameter?
\end{question}
Two fresh reserves of the same cardinality can occupy very different
ordinal intervals. \Cref{swo:gs:thm:reserve} isolates the unavoidable
cardinality; ordinal placement and coding complexity remain separate.
A constructive version should specify the representation of partial
injections and the operation used to choose a complement bijection.

\begin{question}[Coherent cutoff embeddings]\label{swo:gs:n15.11}
Construct embeddings between the orders at different birthday cutoffs
which compose exactly and preserve a useful prefix filtration. Determine
which can also preserve cut types or finite condensation.
\end{question}
Appending an arbitrary tail preserves some comparisons but can change
the required enumeration type. A coherent reserve mechanism should be
chosen once for the whole system rather than separately at each pair of
cutoffs. The support theorem may help isolate its minimal size costs.

\begin{question}[First checked milestones]\label{swo:gs:n15.12}
Formalize the reserve theorem, elementary common-prefix comparison, and
set-sized cut trichotomy before attempting the class automorphism theorem.
Can the abstract alphabet interface support other saturated or
non-Archimedean ordered alphabets without changes to the proofs?
\end{question}
These milestones have explicit input and output types and no dependency
on a formal universe of all class well-orders. Their value is not merely
in reproducing finite tests, but in certifying the limit and cardinal
arguments that the tests cannot inspect.

\begin{question}[Typed constructions indexed by presentations]\label{swo:gs:n15.13}
Which algebraic or model-theoretic constructions can use the set orders
$\WO_\alpha(X)$ or uniformly coded global subfamilies as index orders,
while keeping every support and evaluation map within a specified
size level?
\end{question}
A promising first investigation should use a bounded index set, verify
that the output is independent of the chosen presentation in the intended
sense, and only then consider a uniform class version. The analogy with
Kanovei--Shelah is a guide to construction, not permission to use an
uncoded higher-order totality as a set.

\subsection{Source 18: revised research questions and priorities}
\label{swo:sh:sec:research}

The following are proposed directions left after the theorems above.
They are not presented as a list of previously catalogued open
problems. Each states the extra information that is still needed.

\subsubsection{Bounded order types and their completions}

\begin{question}[The arrangement of gaps]\label{swo:sh:n19.1}
For fixed $\kappa$, classify $\WO_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$ up to order
isomorphism, or classify its completion together with the subset of
realized points. Which features go beyond the complete character
spectrum and the multiplicities proved here?
\end{question}
The new spectrum and counting formulas turn this into an arrangement
problem. In particular, a large family of gaps of one character may
have a highly nontrivial induced order. A first target is
$\kappa=\omega$, followed by $\omega_1$ under specified continuum
arithmetic. Equimorphism with a binary cube does not settle this.

\begin{question}[Longer fixed enumeration types]\label{swo:sh:n19.2}
Determine gap spectra and binary coding lengths for
$\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa})$ when $\alpha>\mu+1$, especially
$\alpha=\mu\cdot2$ and $\mu\cdot\gamma+n$.
\end{question}
Density and cellularity are now known for every $\alpha$ of
cardinality $\mu$, and finite-tail point characters are explicit.
Later infinite blocks can use up an entire $\mu$-sized residual
region, so the minimal-type proof cannot simply be repeated.

\begin{question}[Noncardinal birthday bounds]\label{swo:sh:n19.3}
For a noninitial ordinal $\theta$, determine the spectrum of
$\WO_{|\No_{<\theta}|}(\No_{<\theta})$. Which ordinal features of
$\theta$ survive in interval sizes and cut characters?
\end{question}
The present proof uses the closure $\beta+\gamma<\kappa$ for
$\beta,\gamma<\kappa$, which may fail for $\theta$. The appropriate
replacement is a stratified description of sign cones, not a
substitution of $|\theta|$ for $\theta$.

\begin{question}[Coherent enlargement of cutoffs]\label{swo:sh:n19.4}
Construct embeddings between order spaces for increasing birthday
cutoffs that compose exactly, and specify whether they preserve
minimal enumeration length, prefix cylinders, finite condensation,
or selected cut characters.
\end{question}
Appending a fixed tail gives an embedding of full well-order spaces,
but need not preserve minimum-length strata or compose with a second
independently chosen tail. A global rank-layer schedule gives a
candidate for coherent full spaces; the sharper minimal-stratum
requirements remain separate.

\subsubsection{Class cuts, blocks, and automorphisms}

\begin{question}[Iterating the quotient rather than removing blocks]\label{swo:sh:n19.5}
Choose a precise limit rule and determine the strength of iterating
$R\mapsto B_R$ along specified class well-orders. Which fixed points,
periodic behaviors, or invariants occur?
\end{question}
The single decomposition and ordinary ordinal-indexed block removal
are elementary. The finite-support example is already a fixed point
up to isomorphism. Any claim that repeated condensation automatically
reduces complexity must confront that example. The axiomatic strength
of the genuinely iterated operation is not determined here.

\begin{question}[Order structure on represented class cuts]\label{swo:sh:n19.6}
Study the class cuts satisfying the straddling-prefix criterion,
with predicates marking exhaustive branches and residual tail types.
Which natural automorphisms of the bounded-support core preserve
that distinguished collection of cuts?
\end{question}
The criterion gives a recognition theorem. It does not classify the
automorphism action on all class cuts, or show that every automorphism
of the core extends to the global order. Baseline changes differing
on a proper class of positions are a concrete first case.

\begin{question}[The expanded countable model]\label{swo:sh:n19.7}
Classify
$({\Hall}^{\mathcal M},{\Hsl}^{\mathcal M})$, and then add
the evaluation relation to the surreal labels. Which features depend
on the countable class realization once the pure order has become
the same factorial shuffle?
\end{question}
The pure order cannot define set-likeness even with finite parameters.
An added predicate can therefore retain information that the shuffle
classification necessarily discards.

\begin{question}[$\omega$-nonstandard class models]\label{swo:sh:n19.8}
Describe the external finite-condensation blocks and the elementary
theory of $\Hall$ for countable $\omega$-nonstandard GBC models.
Do these orders share the first-order theory of the standard
factorial shuffle, while realizing additional types?
\end{question}
Internally finite permutation cylinders become externally infinite
discrete intervals. Standard finite adjacency chains inside them
already invalidate the standard classification. Determining the
possible global assembly of these intervals is a concrete
model-theoretic problem; no positive answer to the question is
claimed here.

\subsubsection{Words, encoding, and formalization}

\begin{question}[Sharp word-code bounds]\label{swo:sh:n19.9}
Optimize the birthday of explicit order embeddings of injective and
increasing words, recording separately preservation of numerical
order, prefix extension, and simplicity. Can the centered encodings
be made comparably efficient at singular stages?
\end{question}
The duplicated-sign delimiters provide transparent proofs, rather
than optimal codes. Uniform tree isomorphisms obtained by
back-and-forth supply little direct birthday control.

\begin{question}[The centered increasing order itself]\label{swo:sh:n19.10}
Classify the entire centered increasing-word order up to isomorphism
and determine the intrinsic definability of its all-negative cones
and its positive-limit points.
\end{question}
Its local characters, its complete set-cut obstruction, and the two
types of rooted cones are known here. The contrast between that
intrinsic information and the displayed entry signs makes the
automorphism problem meaningful.

\begin{question}[Weak choice and uniform constructions]\label{swo:sh:n19.11}
Which word-tree isomorphisms and class-core identifications can be
proved without Global Choice? For a specified operation, distinguish
existence, a uniform definable implementation, and an effective
implementation on concrete codes.
\end{question}
The explicit sign embeddings and many cut arguments need no Global
Choice. Our class isomorphisms use deterministic global
back-and-forth. These are different strength claims; a uniform
family of class maps should not be selected without proof.

\begin{question}[A first machine-checked milestone]\label{swo:sh:n19.12}
Formalize the elementary common-prefix relation and the
set-interval decomposition for a supplied class-model relation,
alongside the set-level ordinal spectrum and minimal permutation
cut trichotomy. Can one order-theoretic interface serve all four?
\end{question}
This is a realistic modular target because it avoids almost all
surreal arithmetic. The initial deliverables should expose their
size assumptions in the theorem signatures and make the
conventional proof-to-formal-statement correspondence reviewable.

\subsection{Source 19: further research questions after the new results}
\label{swo:rs:sec:agenda}

These questions are proposed continuations of the present work. They
are not asserted to be a catalogue of historically established open
problems. The distinction matters because a question may already have
an answer in the wider literature even when the project has not yet
identified it.

\subsubsection{Fixed enumeration types and bounded completions}

\begin{question}[The remaining coding gap]\label{swo:rs:n14.1}
When a singular non-strong-limit residual cardinal at most $\kappa$
produces different lower and upper weighted ranks $\varrho_{\mathrm{lo}}<\varrho_{\mathrm{up}}$, determine
the least binary coding length of $\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\kappa})$. Is
the lower bound always attained? A stronger and especially useful
target is an embedding into $\BB_{\varrho_{\mathrm{lo}}}\times n!$.
\end{question}
The embedded-cube spectrum is already settled by the constant-cylinder
argument. The unresolved issue is an upper coding construction, not
the existence of a still larger binary cube inside the order. The
generic subproblem is whether $\WO_\lambda(Y)$ embeds into
$\BB_\lambda$ for every alphabet $Y$ of singular non-strong-limit
size $\lambda$. Birthday-controlled insertion shows that all such
alphabets occur in the relevant residual range when $\lambda\le\kappa$.

\begin{question}[From equimorphism to isomorphism]\label{swo:rs:n14.2}
Classify the actual order types of the fixed strata whose binary
coding ranks and cube spectra agree. Which additional arrangements
of numerical gaps, residual alphabets, and finite cylinders distinguish
equimorphic examples?
\end{question}
The first-cutoff theorem gives a warning: two familiar topological
models can have the same ordered completion $\mathbb R$ and different
complements inside it. The canonical decorated-word completion is a more
informative object than a list of cardinal invariants.

\begin{question}[Gap arrangements in longer strata]\label{swo:rs:n14.3}
Extend the bounded normal forms from minimum-length permutations
to every fixed enumeration type, using the residual lexicographic
sum and the cardinal-layer decomposition. Compute the order of the
gap loci, together with their point characters and multiplicities.
\end{question}
Infinite tails introduce several successive residual alphabets.
The completion should record those transitions; merely adding the
minimal-stratum spectra cannot determine how the gaps are arranged.

\begin{question}[Noninitial birthday bounds]\label{swo:rs:n14.4}
For an arbitrary ordinal $\theta$, study
$\WO_{|\No_{<\theta}|}(\No_{<\theta})$ and its longer strata.
Which features depend on $\theta$ as an ordinal rather than just
on its cardinality?
\end{question}
The full-interval-size and sign-cone arguments above use the closure
of an infinite initial cardinal under sums of two smaller ordinals.
A noninitial bound requires a finer decomposition of its sign tree.

\subsubsection{Residual class alphabets and automorphisms}

\begin{question}[Stability of first-block separation]\label{swo:rs:n14.5}
Analyze the set-deletion criterion of
Proposition~\ref{swo:rs:rf:prop:alphabetcriterion} in residual surreal alphabets
defined by sign, birthday, or algebraic conditions. Which natural
embeddings, convex restrictions, or extensions of the class realization
preserve injectivity of the initial-word trace map?
\end{question}
The surreal fresh-label property is sufficient: at a first difference
$a<b$ after a set prefix, an unused label strictly between them
gives an exhaustive separator. Requiring every open interval of $Y$
to remain nonempty after deleting any set guarantees this step.
The exact obstruction is now an initial $\Ord$-segment and a final
$\Ord^*$-segment exposed by deleting a set, with admitted witnesses.
The $\Ord+\Ord^*$ counterexample shows that cardinality of the
carrier alone is insufficient. Applying the criterion systematically,
and tracking the admission of its witnesses under a change of class
realization, would make recursive residual analysis more effective.

\begin{question}[Residual fiber isomorphism types]\label{swo:rs:n14.6}
Determine which orders $\WO^{\mathcal M}(Y)$ occur as fibers over
core cuts and when two such fibers are isomorphic. Can useful
invariants be extracted from the numerical order on $Y$ without
classifying its entire family of well-orders?
\end{question}
This is the remaining mathematical content in the automorphism
extension criterion. The decorated reconstruction is exact, but a
decoration by the full fiber order type is not by itself a simple
classification of those fibers.

\begin{question}[Which core automorphisms extend?]\label{swo:rs:n14.7}
Compute the decoration-preserving subgroup of $\Aut(C)$ in
specified external class models. How does it depend on the chosen
baseline enumeration and on a change of baseline with proper-class
support?
\end{question}
Preservation of represented versus unrepresented cuts is necessary
but may omit the residual order type. The exact criterion requires
preserving that full type. It would be valuable to replace it with
more concrete combinatorial invariants in important models.

\begin{question}[Enrichments that remember the class theory]\label{swo:rs:n14.8}
Expand the pure global order by its set-like suborder, a selected
core, its prefix tree, and an evaluation relation. Which fragments
of the underlying class theory become interpretable in these
successively richer structures?
\end{question}
The common pure first-order theory cannot distinguish even
$\omega$-standardness. This makes the question of the smallest
informative enrichment precise. Retaining the numerical alphabet
and the prefix-evaluation relation is a natural first experiment.

\subsubsection{External models and foundational strength}

\begin{question}[Uncountable external isomorphism spectra]\label{swo:rs:n14.9}
Classify $\Hall^{\mathcal M}$ and
$\Hsl^{\mathcal M}$ for specified uncountable class models.
What additional conditions on their quotients and nonstandard
internally finite cylinders are forced by saturation or by a
full-class realization?
\end{question}
The common elementary theory is already fixed. Uncountable
isomorphism types must retain information beyond finite games,
including cut cofinalities and the external geometry of internally
finite intervals. The full-class model at an inaccessible cardinal
is a concrete first case.

\begin{question}[Admitted versus amenable branches]\label{swo:rs:n14.10}
Study the order and descriptive complexity of the persistent
external cuts whose bounded prefixes are all internally coded but
whose full branches are not admitted. How does this family change
when the class realization is enlarged while the set universe is
kept fixed?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:rs:rf:thm:missingbranches} produces continuum many such
cuts in every countable realization. The next issue is how these
cuts are arranged and which extensions admit selected branches
without adding sets.

\begin{question}[Iterating set-interval condensation]\label{swo:rs:n14.11}
Specify a limit-stage rule for iterating $R\mapsto J_R$ and
determine the exact recursion or comprehension principles needed
for the resulting construction. Which fixed points and strictly
changing orbits occur?
\end{question}
The one-step quotient is elementary and may preserve isomorphism
type. Any iteration theorem must therefore prove its own structural
or well-foundedness claim rather than infer descent from the word
``quotient.''

\subsubsection{Coherence and formal proof development}

\begin{question}[Coherent enlargement maps]\label{swo:rs:n14.12}
Construct a directed system of embeddings between birthday-cutoff
well-order spaces, with explicitly stated preservation of prefixes,
finite-tail cylinders, or selected completion data.
\end{question}
The restriction theorem proves that arbitrary carrier restriction
cannot provide the required monotone maps. A construction should
instead specify how new labels are inserted and how the schedules
compose. Full well-order spaces and minimum-length strata impose
different scheduling requirements.

\begin{question}[A small certified core of the theory]\label{swo:rs:n14.13}
Formalize the restriction classification, first-disagreement
comparison, prefix-code concatenation, and cylinder fusion as
general set-level lemmas, then derive the weighted fixed-type
spectrum from them.
\end{question}
This would convert the most reusable part of the present analysis
into a compact foundation for later work. It also provides a clear
test of which cardinal-arithmetic lemmas and ordinal-sum bounds are
actually needed by the proof.

\subsection{Source 20: a revised research agenda}
\label{swo:lm:agenda:section}

The following questions concern extensions not established by this
article. They are project proposals, except where their background is
explicitly cited. The previous broad question whether \emph{every} core
automorphism extends has a negative answer in
\cref{swo:lm:aut:thm:localfailure}; it should no longer appear as unresolved.

\begin{question}[The extendible subgroup]\label{swo:lm:agenda:automorphisms}
Give useful generators or intrinsic descriptions of the subgroup of
core automorphisms preserving exhaustive represented cuts. How does it
depend on the chosen baseline and the displayed prefix structure?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:lm:aut:thm:extensioncriterion} supplies an exact criterion, but it
does not compute that subgroup. A concrete starting point is the
automorphism group of the labelled prefix structure together with its
exhaustion predicate. Numerical relabelling alone does not stabilize
a fixed core, by \cref{swo:lm:aut:prop:labelmoves}.

\begin{question}[Extensions across raw residual fibers]\label{swo:lm:n11.2}
Which core automorphisms preserving all injective represented cuts
extend to the entire raw comparison structure? Formulate necessary and
sufficient conditions including the order types of residual fibers
and the uniformity of the chosen fiber identifications.
\end{question}
Different raw well-orders can have the same first ordinal block and
hence the same core cut. A cut-preservation criterion alone cannot
choose their relative images. The local-size blocks of
\cref{swo:lm:loc:blocks} offer a first manageable family of fibers.

\begin{question}[The expanded countable structure]\label{swo:lm:n11.3}
Classify the external pairs $(\Hall^{\mathcal M},\Hsl^{\mathcal M})$,
or expand further by prefix evaluation. Which distinctions between
class realizations survive after the pure order has collapsed to the
two types in \cref{swo:lm:mod:dichotomy}?
\end{question}
The pure order forgets almost all class-theoretic information. Set-likeness
is a natural first predicate to restore, but its distribution inside
singleton or larger cut fibers can depend on admitted branches. A full
answer should specify whether the underlying set model is fixed.

\begin{question}[Effective theory with additional predicates]\label{swo:lm:n11.4}
Determine the theory and decision complexity after adding a named
set-like fragment, selected prefix predicates, or a baseline evaluation
relation to the pure countable order.
\end{question}
The pure order theory is decidable by \cref{swo:lm:mod:decidability}; adding
the enumeration data can reintroduce much more information. It is
useful to identify the smallest expansion that detects a change of
class realization, rather than assuming that the pure order already
does so.

\begin{question}[The strength of complete condensation histories]\label{swo:lm:n11.5}
Over GB or GBC, what is the exact strength of the assertion that every
supplied class well-order admits its nested least-representative
condensation history through the input order plus one stage?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:lm:con:termination} proves the terminal behavior conditional on the
history and gives ETR as a sufficient existence principle. A reversal
would require encoding a genuinely class-valued recursion into this
particular elementary operator. Merely observing its transfinite
appearance would not establish such a reversal.

\merge\ (4 October 2026, batch~96.) Answered over $\GBC$ by source~29 and over
$\GB$ by sources~34 and~35: the assertion is equivalent to strong
comparability $\CWO$
(\cref{swo:bw:ch:equivalence,swo:bo:hist:equivalence,swo:fc:gb-comparability});
whether it implies $\ETR$ is open (\cref{swo:bw:n13.8}).

\begin{question}[Alternative limits for quotient iteration]\label{swo:lm:n11.6}
Which other mathematically natural limit rules give canonical
condensation histories, and how do their heights compare with
$h_\kappa(\theta)$ in the full model?
\end{question}
The nested-carrier convention retains embedding information at limits.
An isomorphism-type-only process discards that information. One should
first define any replacement rule as an actual operator and examine
the self-similar examples before seeking a general height theorem.

\begin{question}[Embeddings that retain more than order]\label{swo:lm:n11.7}
Can birthday-stage embeddings preserve designated cylinders, finite
condensation blocks, or chosen cut characters while composing exactly?
What is possible for specified minimal enumeration strata?
\end{question}
The append-tail maps in \cref{swo:lm:lim:direct} solve coherence for all
enumeration types. They need not stay in a prescribed minimal stratum.
The local-rank criterion identifies the obstruction to set-likeness;
preserving exact local ordinal types is a stricter requirement.

\begin{question}[Exact birthday profiles and club diagnostics]\label{swo:lm:n11.8}
Classify the attainable functions
$\kappa\mapsto\otp(R\restr \No_{<\kappa}^2)$ and the associated classes
$\operatorname{Min}_R$ of strong-limit cutoffs at which the minimum type is attained.
Which finer invariants remain after passing to equivalence modulo the
club filter?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:lm:lim:club} detects set-likeness: $\operatorname{Min}_R$ contains a club in the
set-like case and misses a club otherwise (source~20 writes $A_R$). Unboundedness alone does
not suffice, as the sparse-beth example shows. A natural next step is
to apply analogous diagnostics to the successive canonical ordinal
blocks and ask whether their combined profiles recover more of a
raw class well-order.

\begin{question}[Gap arrangements beyond spectra]\label{swo:lm:n11.9}
Classify the ordered pair consisting of the Dedekind completion of
$\WO_\mu(\No_{<\kappa})$ and its distinguished realized subset. At the
countable cutoff, how much of the prefix tree is recoverable from that
pair?
\end{question}
\Cref{swo:lm:top:main} identifies the countable completion and the topological
complexity of the realized points. Equal gap counts and equal topology
do not by themselves identify the arrangement of the missing cuts.
At uncountable stages a generalized topology must first be specified.

\begin{question}[Longer strata and noninitial birthdays]\label{swo:lm:n11.10}
Determine the full proper-gap spectra and their arrangement for
$\WO_{\mu\cdot2}(\No_{<\kappa})$ and longer strata, and for birthday
cutoffs which are not initial cardinals.
\end{question}
The known density transition and binary coding ranks do not determine
these arrangements. At noninitial cutoffs, ordinal tails can destroy
the closure of the cones used in the cardinal-cutoff proofs. A first
target is a single additional infinite enumeration block with a fixed
finite terminal tail.

\begin{question}[Robustness under class extensions]\label{swo:lm:n11.11}
For extensions of the class collection with the same sets, characterize
which new represented cuts, automorphisms, and condensation histories
can appear while all old comparisons remain fixed.
\end{question}
The absoluteness result in \cref{swo:lm:form:section} rules out changing the
well-foundedness of an old common relation. The remaining freedom lies
in new relations and in new uniform witnesses. This sharper formulation
avoids a false source of model dependence.

\begin{question}[A verified generic first-divergence library]\label{swo:lm:n11.12}
Formalize common-prefix comparison, two-label persistence, finite
changes along restrictions, and the sharp coherent-gluing criterion
for arbitrary ordered carriers. Then instantiate at the inspected
ProveIt sign carrier.
\end{question}
This is a concrete first milestone: its dependencies are relation
restriction, set-valued recursion, ordinal first difference, and
well-foundedness. It would verify several central mechanisms before
the more demanding task of formalizing the class automorphism and
nonstandard-model arguments.

\subsection{Source 21: further research questions and concrete targets}\label{swo:fu:sec:questions}

The following are proposed continuations. They are not a claim that
each question has already appeared as an established open problem in
the literature. Each is formulated after the results proved here, so
it does not ask again whether core extension always works or whether
noncardinal cutoffs have computable basic invariants.

\begin{question}[Classify the extendable subgroup]\label{swo:fu:rq:subgroup}
For a fixed baseline $b$, describe
$\operatorname{Stab}_{\Aut({\Pbd(b)})}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{exh}})$ by useful
generators, definability conditions, or an intrinsic expansion of the
core. Which such descriptions avoid explicitly naming every exhaustive
represented cut?
\end{question}
The stabilizer criterion is exact, and the subgroup is proper. The
remaining task is a structural description. Cofinalities alone cannot
suffice: exhaustive, nonexhaustive, and vertical large cuts are
conjugate in the unexpanded core order.

\begin{question}[Extension to the full class-well-order space]
\label{swo:fu:rq:full-extension}
Which core automorphisms preserve the represented injective cuts and
the order types of their residual fibers, and when can their induced
fiber isomorphisms be made uniform?
\end{question}
The full extension problem requires more than the set-like criterion:
two orders with the same initial word may have different residual
well-orders. A sufficient theorem should construct the fiber maps
explicitly or state the additional choice principle used to assemble
them. The vertical-cut obstruction already rules out arbitrary extension.

\begin{question}[Prefix-preserving automorphisms]
\label{swo:fu:rq:tree-automorphisms}
Classify automorphisms of the displayed prefix tree that preserve its
exhaustive branches. Which numerical relabelings and coordinate-dependent
successor-order isomorphisms generate them?
\end{question}
The countable theorem shows that bare-order automorphisms can destroy
the cylinder family. Even a tree automorphism need not visibly preserve
the global requirement that every label eventually occurs. This asks
for the precise extra condition, rather than assuming that local
compatibility implies exhaustivity.

\begin{question}[Noncardinal cut spectra and isomorphism types]
\label{swo:fu:rq:noncardinal-types}
Determine the complete cofinality spectrum of missing cuts in
$\WO_{2^{|\theta|}}(\No_{<\theta})$ for noncardinal $\theta$.
When do two such spaces with equal basic invariants have the same
order type?
\end{question}
For example, the cutoffs $\omega+1$, $\omega\cdot2$, and $\omega^2$
have the same cardinality, density, global cofinalities, point
characters, and binary coding rank calculated here. These equalities
do not prove an isomorphism. The finite numerical end blocks and the
different sign-prefix structures suggest concrete cut configurations
to compare first.

\begin{question}[Fixed nonminimal enumeration types]
\label{swo:fu:rq:fixed-types}
Extend fixed-type cardinal and character formulas to full isomorphism
and embedding classifications for $\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\theta})$, with
$|\alpha|=|\No_{<\theta}|$, and describe the relative closures of these strata.
\end{question}
Existing finite-terminal and density calculations are not by themselves
a classification. The first-cardinality decomposition and closure
theorem give a starting point that tracks the unused alphabet, not
only the ordinal length. A useful next case is to compare consecutive
finite terminal lengths while retaining the prefix-fiber structure.

\begin{question}[Coherence across a change of cardinality]
\label{swo:fu:rq:coherence}
Can the fixed-slot construction be replaced by embeddings between
minimum-length spaces when their cardinalities change, with strict
composition identities along a specified chain of birthday cutoffs?
\end{question}
Within a fixed band, \cref{swo:fu:bs:thm:coherence} supplies such a system.
Across a cardinal jump the coordinate domains change; across a proper
class of cutoffs, the uniform family itself requires a size audit.
Specify whether the embeddings should preserve the order topology,
prefix structure, or both.

\begin{question}[The uncountable colored quotient]
\label{swo:fu:rq:condensation}
For uncountable external realizations, classify the quotient of
$\Hall$ by its canonical terminal permutation blocks, with the
factorial-size colors retained. Which saturation and homogeneity
properties follow from the underlying class realization?
\end{question}
The countable standard and nonstandard types are completely described
here. Their local block analysis remains available in larger models,
but dense colors no longer imply uniqueness of the quotient order.
This is a natural setting for separating cardinal invariants from
actual order type.

\begin{question}[How much model structure does a marked core retain?]
\label{swo:fu:rq:marked-models}
When are two pairs $(H_{\mathcal X},{\Pbd(b)})$ and
$(H_{\mathcal Y},\Pbd(c))$ isomorphic if the core is preserved setwise but
its individual codes are allowed to move?
\end{question}
Pointwise identification of a common core detects proper class
expansions through represented cuts, while the unmarked countable
orders are always rational. The intermediate classification should be
expressed through the action of core automorphisms on represented-cut
families. It could distinguish model-theoretic information that
neither extreme viewpoint captures.

\begin{question}[Automorphism and descriptive complexity of the countable-alphabet space]
\label{swo:fu:rq:descriptive}
Give an explicit description of the subgroup of $\Aut(\mathbb{R},<)$
preserving the embedded set $P=\WO_\omega(\mathbb{Q})$ in its Dedekind
completion. Classify its orbits on omitted cuts and determine the
complexity of the branch-exhaustivity condition in a chosen completion
code.
\end{question}
The Baire homeomorphism, finite homogeneity, and continuum many missing
cuts are already proved. A sharper description would separate vertical
numerical cuts, omitted-range branch cuts, and any further cut types
by explicit invariants.

\begin{question}[Presentation orders under forcing]
\label{swo:fu:rq:forcing}
Under hypotheses preserving old class well-order types, which
lexicographic presentation orders acquire new cuts or new
automorphism obstructions? What changes after identifying old and new
carriers through specified interleavings?
\end{question}
Preservation of old relations is proved above; preservation of all new
abstract types is a different issue studied under stronger hypotheses
in \cite{HamkinsWoodin}. New sign sequences can enlarge the carrier
even when ordinals are unchanged. A useful first target is a forcing
extension adding one real, with the old carrier named explicitly.

\begin{question}[Relation-table comparison with extra structure]
\label{swo:fu:rq:tables}
Which choices of the coordinate enumeration of $\No^2$ give isomorphic
expanded relation-table orders, and which preserve a specified
set-coded dense family? Can any of them recover the numerical
first-prefix comparison after adding a small amount of structure?
\end{question}
Binary equimorphism does not settle these questions. The two-label
example already rules out identifying the comparisons on the nose.

\begin{question}[Formal verification of the obstruction]
\label{swo:fu:rq:formal}
Formalize first the small-carrier prefix comparison and fixed-slot
coherence theorem, then the abstract cut-reconstruction and
nonextension argument over a universe-relative class interface.
\end{question}
The theorem dependencies are short and arithmetic-free. A verified
result should include an axiom report and an explicit smallness
boundary. In particular, the final nonextension theorem should be
checked as a statement about permitted uniform operators or about a
specified larger-universe collection, not an undeclared type of all
classes.

\subsection{Source 22: further research questions and proposed projects}\label{swo:rg:sec:questions}
The following questions are continuations of the present program. They are not advertised as a list of historically established famous open problems. In particular, the fixed-length density/cellularity/weight table and the redundancy of cylinder heights are now treated as proved results rather than left open.

\subsubsection{Residual orders and topology}
\begin{question}[Nonminimal cut spectra]\label{swo:rg:n12.1}
Classify the nonprincipal cut-character spectra of $\WO_{\mu+n}(\No_{<\kappa})$, $\WO_{\mu+\omega}(\No_{<\kappa})$, and $\WO_{\mu\cdot2}(\No_{<\kappa})$. Which cuts arise inside a residual fibre, and which occur at a boundary where a limiting prefix loses extendibility?
\end{question}
The general first-disagreement formula settles point characters only after the relevant residual orders are understood. A cut may follow a coherent prefix chain whose union exhausts too many labels. Such a failure is not detected by the three cardinal topological invariants.

\begin{question}[The dense quotient orders $Q_n(X)$]\label{swo:rg:n12.2}
When are $Q_n(X)$ and $Q_m(X)$ isomorphic for distinct finite $n,m$? Does the answer depend only on the numerical order type of $X$, or on additional saturation properties not implied by richness?
\end{question}
They share the invariants computed in \cref{swo:rg:prop:finite-normal}, but equality of those invariants is not an isomorphism theorem. An isomorphism would sharpen the finite-tail normal forms and compare their nonisolated derivatives.

\begin{question}[Long-tail local characters]\label{swo:rg:n12.3}
Describe the possible point characters for $\alpha=\mu\cdot2$ by a tractable invariant of the residual alphabet. Can the iterated first-disagreement reduction be organized as a useful normal form rather than an arbitrary tree of residual orders?
\end{question}
The main topological table already applies. The remaining issue is local order structure, including endpoints of residual permutation orders and cofinalities of their extremal fibres.

\begin{question}[Descriptive topology when cofinalities are countable]\label{swo:rg:n12.4}
For which alphabets and lengths are these first-countable spaces metrizable, completely metrizable, or representable by familiar ordered spaces? In particular, analyze the split space at $\mu+2$ without mistaking separability for second countability.
\end{question}
The countable-alphabet examples provide controlled test cases: $\omega+2$ has many jumps, $\omega+3$ has a dense set of isolated points, and $\omega+\omega$ has no jumps but continuum cellularity.

\subsubsection{What structure must be retained?}
\begin{question}[Eliminating label data]\label{swo:rg:n12.5}
After unranked cylinder incidence is supplied, what is the weakest additional relation that recognizes exhaustive branches? Can label occurrence be replaced by a coarser invariant, or can two incidence presentations with identical unlabelled data disagree on the exhaustive-trace predicate?
\end{question}
Height is no longer an unknown ingredient: \cref{swo:rg:thm:height} recovers it. The open issue is label coverage. No claim that it is eliminable, or provably indispensable in every presentation, is made here.

\begin{question}[Reconstruction without fixed coding parameters]\label{swo:rg:n12.6}
How much of \cref{swo:rg:thm:faithful} survives when $b$ or $g$ is not named? Can one formulate a functorial reconstruction up to isomorphism of two-sorted models, rather than inclusion over an identical set universe with shared parameters?
\end{question}
The elementary decoder is exact once the parameters are fixed. Removing them introduces an automorphism and definability problem, not a failure of the existing decoder.

\begin{question}[Automorphisms preserving admitted traces]\label{swo:rg:n12.7}
Characterize the automorphisms of the unranked incidence structure which preserve exhaustive traces in a given class realization. Which core-order automorphisms extend to this incidence structure, and which preserve the binary-swap trace substructure after changing the baseline?
\end{question}
The earlier reports supply extension obstructions for pure core automorphisms. The present reconstruction suggests that preservation of admitted traces can constrain the induced action on the entire class sort.

\subsubsection{Bounds, foundations, and verification}
\begin{question}[Noncardinal birthday cutoffs]\label{swo:rg:n12.8}
For an ordinal cutoff such as $\kappa+\omega$ or $\kappa\cdot2$, determine exactly which intervals retain full alphabet cardinality. Extend the topological classification to fragments where richness fails or varies from interval to interval.
\end{question}
The proof of \cref{swo:rg:lem:rich} uses $\delta+\eta<\kappa$ for smaller ordinals at an initial-cardinal cutoff. That mechanism must be replaced, not assumed, for arbitrary ordinal cutoffs.

\begin{question}[Coherent length and cutoff embeddings]\label{swo:rg:n12.9}
Construct embeddings among different birthday fragments and enumeration strata which compose exactly and preserve a useful prefix filtration. Determine the optimal additional support or reserve needed for this coherence.
\end{question}
An arbitrary appended tail preserves a comparison but may change the prescribed order type or destroy compatibility with another embedding. The earlier optimal support-cardinality theorem is a natural input; optimal ordinal placement remains separate.

\begin{question}[Iterated raw heads and recursion strength]\label{swo:rg:n12.10}
Determine the exact class-recursion strength needed to iterate the canonical common-head or ordinal-head decomposition through set and class lengths. Which bounded iterations are elementary, and which imply fragments of $\ETR$?
\end{question}
The elementary direct comparison in \cref{swo:rg:prop:raw} does not settle this. A reverse-mathematical treatment should specify whether a stage is a set object or a whole class relation.

\begin{question}[Binary coding lengths for long strata]\label{swo:rg:n12.11}
Extend the earlier binary equimorphism and singular strong-limit coding-length results to nonminimal lengths. How do finite jumps, infinite residual orders, and failures of residual extendibility affect the least binary-word length admitting an order embedding?
\end{question}
The constant ordinal embedding spectrum does not answer this finer question. Nor does cardinality $2^\mu$ alone determine a binary lexicographic coding length.

\begin{question}[First kernel-checked milestones]\label{swo:rg:n12.12}
Formalize the residual-cylinder identity, the first-disagreement character formula, and height recovery from unranked incidence. Then instantiate the richness and fresh-separator interfaces using the repository's sign carrier.
\end{question}
These milestones are small enough to isolate precise size hypotheses but substantial enough to verify the limit arguments which finite regression checks cannot reach. Only after they are checked should the class-realization decoder be encoded in an explicit model interface.
