\subsection{Source 23: further research questions and proposed projects}\label{swo:tm:sec:questions}

The termination question for the two unrestricted set-word carriers is
settled by Theorem~\ref{swo:tm:thm:termination}; the questions below begin beyond
that result. The explicit polynomial hierarchies likewise answer an
existence problem, not the full classification or proof-strength problem
for arbitrary raw orders.

\subsubsection{Word orders and enriched lexicographic structure}

\begin{question}[Classification of the nonsaturated marker orders]\label{swo:tm:n16.1}
For a fixed infinite regular $\theta$, are all word orders arising from
marker cuts of type $(\theta,\Ord)$ isomorphic? Does the answer change
between arbitrary and injective words? Which cut spectra, beyond point
characters, decide the answer?
\end{question}
The character computation gives necessary invariants but not a complete
classification. A focused first step is a cut reconstruction theorem for
the nonsaturated word orders, keeping their named cylinders.

\begin{question}[Restricted increasing-word repairs]\label{swo:tm:n16.2}
Which length restrictions or endpoint decorations make an increasing-word
order saturated at a prescribed small cardinal? Can one characterize the
obstruction by cofinal subsets of the terminally available alphabet at
each prefix, rather than by one global marker?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:tm:thm:increasing} rules out every fixed marker for all set
lengths. Prefix-dependent markers or extra continuation labels are
substantive new structures, not exceptions to that theorem.

\begin{question}[Intrinsic versus named cylinders]\label{swo:tm:n16.3}
For which expansions of the outer linear order are prefix cylinders,
termination points, or inherited monotonicity recoverable? Can one find
a minimal additional relation that distinguishes these presentations
without naming every prefix individually?
\end{question}
The previous work's prefix non-rigidity makes a claim of recovery from
bare order alone unsafe. The new admissible-marker isomorphisms supply
further examples in which the same linear order has different alphabet
presentations.

\begin{question}[Quantitative birthday bounds]\label{swo:tm:n16.4}
For a small input cut of words, bound the separator's length and the
birthdays of its letters in terms of the input and forbidden-label
bounds. Can the two-cut fresh-separator construction be arranged to use
one prescribed extra birthday level?
\end{question}
The crossing chain already gives a set length bound from the input.
Optimizing the label bound would connect the abstract proof directly to
\texttt{exists\_cut\_separator\_of\_birthday\_lt}.

\subsubsection{Raw orders and condensation}

\begin{question}[Proof strength of general condensation iteration]\label{swo:tm:n16.5}
Over $\GBC$, what is the exact strength of the assertion that every raw
class well-order admits its set-interval condensation hierarchy along a
given class well-order? Is a restricted form of $\ETR$ sufficient and
necessary, or does this particular operator admit a weaker construction?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:tm:thm:polyhierarchy} shows that long explicit examples by
themselves cannot establish a lower bound on the recursion principle.
A reversal would need to encode genuinely arbitrary recursive information.

\begin{question}[Which orders eventually collapse?]\label{swo:tm:n16.6}
In a theory providing the required hierarchy, does every raw class
well-order collapse at some admitted class-well-order stage? How should
collapse length be represented without an illegitimate order type
object for every proper-class well-order?
\end{question}
The polynomial theorem realizes every prescribed admitted length. It does
not give a universal bound or prove eventual collapse for all raw orders.

\begin{question}[Lexicographic distribution of internal invariants]\label{swo:tm:n16.7}
Can Theorem~\ref{swo:tm:thm:densecomplexity} be sharpened from existence in every
set-like interval to a uniform embedding of a specified parameter order,
with its points carrying prescribed condensation hierarchies? Which such
families remain definable from a fixed baseline enumeration?
\end{question}
The quantifier order matters: a single class parameter $\Gamma$ is
allowed in the proved theorem. A uniform family ranging over all class
well-orders needs an explicitly higher-order interpretation.

\begin{question}[Condensation versus finite residual adjacency]\label{swo:tm:n16.8}
How do set-interval blocks inside a raw well-order interact with finite
adjacency components in the outer lexicographic order? Can an enriched
outer order describe the distinction between an exhausted finite
residual tail and a proper residual class?
\end{question}
These are different condensations on different orders. Treating them
as one operation would erase the key carrier distinction.

\subsubsection{Foundations and implementation}

\begin{question}[Choice strength of the new classification]\label{swo:tm:n16.9}
What is the weakest class theory proving the separator part of
Theorem~\ref{swo:tm:thm:termination}, with a supplied saturated alphabet and
marker cut? Can its order-isomorphism conclusion be proved without a
supplied global enumeration, for the special surreal presentations?
\end{question}
Most local proofs use only set-sized constructions with class parameters.
The back-and-forth conclusion deliberately uses global choice. These
should be optimized separately.

\begin{question}[A checked pair of contrasting theorems]\label{swo:tm:n16.10}
Formalize the admissible-marker theorem for the injective sign-carrier
word order and, in the same framework, the failure for increasing words.
Then formalize the explicit $\omega$ polynomial hierarchy and its
non-stabilizing limit, before addressing arbitrary $\Gamma$.
\end{question}
This yields a manageable development with positive and negative tests.
The finite diagnostics supplied here can guide examples, but the kernel
proof must retain the universe and cofinality distinctions.

\subsection{Source 24: further research questions and proposed projects}\label{swo:pc:sec:questions}

These are proposed continuations of the results proved here. They are not all claimed to be previously published open problems. Questions about structured cut recognition, prefix non-rigidity, optimal support reserves, and some automorphism extensions have already been addressed in the earlier drafts; a new project should use those results instead of restating them as untouched.

\subsubsection{Singular topology and completeness}

\begin{question}[Complete metrizability at uncountable countable cofinality]\label{swo:pc:q:singularmetric}
Let $\mu>\omega$ be singular with $\cf\mu=\omega$. Is the forward-prefix space $\WO_\mu(X)$ completely metrizable? Equivalently, can the dense permutation subspace of its metrizable injection completion be characterized as a $G_\delta$ subset? Determine whether the answer depends on cardinal arithmetic.
\end{question}
The equivalence is justified directly in Appendix~\ref{swo:pc:app:gdelta}; its ambient injection space is completely metrizable by Theorem~\ref{swo:pc:thm:completion} and Proposition~\ref{swo:pc:prop:metric}. The question concerns the original topology, not the finer two-sided topology. The shift-type counterexample proves only the incompleteness of one uniformity. A constructive positive answer would need to enforce uncountably many coverage requirements while keeping the appropriate neighborhoods; a negative answer could be obtained by showing that no countable open intersection in the injection space characterizes exhaustiveness.

\begin{question}[A singular replacement for the exhaustion tree]\label{swo:pc:n13.2}
Classify $\WO_\mu(X)$ up to homeomorphism when $\mu$ is singular. Can it be represented as the body of a tree with an explicit acceptance condition at prematurely full prefixes, rather than as the unrestricted body of a regular-height tree?
\end{question}
The exact obstruction in Section~\ref{swo:pc:sec:regular} suggests retaining both domain-length growth and coverage growth as separate coordinates. A useful result would identify an invariant that distinguishes singular spaces with the same cofinality and weight.

\begin{question}[Dense-open intersection thresholds]\label{swo:pc:n13.3}
Determine the least cardinality of a family of dense open subsets of $\WO_\mu(X)$ whose intersection is not dense. Compare that number with $\cf\mu$, the exhaustion family in $\I_\mu(X)$, and any stronger point-preserving fusion properties.
\end{question}
The existing fusion theorem is a lower bound, not a complete classification. An intersection theorem in the permutation space and one in the injection completion are different statements: the latter has all the closed missing-label boundaries available.

\subsubsection{Order structure beyond the topological classification}

\begin{question}[The embedded real-line model at countable size]\label{swo:pc:n13.4}
Describe the complement $\mathbb{R}\setminus\WO_\omega(X)$, up to increasing homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}$, using its cylinder-edge, numerical-gap, and nonexhaustive-branch parts. Which of these parts are recoverable from the bare linear order and which require named prefix predicates?
\end{question}
The present paper gives its Borel class, category, density, and cardinality, but not a complete orbit classification of its placement in $\mathbb{R}$. The earlier non-rigidity results warn that a prefix-based description need not be intrinsic to the bare order.

\begin{question}[Regular homeomorphisms versus order embeddings]\label{swo:pc:n13.5}
Theorem~\ref{swo:pc:thm:regular} forgets the numerical alphabet. Which additional data on the exhaustion tree recover lexicographic order, and what order-embedding or order-isomorphism criteria can be proved from those data?
\end{question}
Even the countable case shows that recognizing Baire topology does not identify the order with its standard irrational model. Quantitative versions could track birthday bounds and support costs during the tree coding.

\begin{question}[Completion-preserving automorphisms]\label{swo:pc:n13.6}
Characterize those order or topological automorphisms of the permutation space that extend to its forward injection completion, its two-sided completion, or its Dedekind completion while preserving specified boundary types.
\end{question}
Every order isomorphism extends to the Dedekind completion, but preservation of the branch subspace is an extra condition. Earlier represented-cut criteria should be combined with the uniform-continuity obstruction, rather than replaced by a blanket extension claim.

\subsubsection{Permutation algebra at singular cardinals}

\begin{question}[The boundedness-preserving subgroup]\label{swo:pc:n13.7}
Analyze $H_\mu$ intrinsically at singular $\mu$: its closure properties in the two ambient topologies, its normalizers, and the possible topological-group structures on larger natural subgroups. How much of the ordinal bounded-set ideal is recoverable from this group together with its topology?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:pc:thm:continuity} is an exact local criterion, but it does not classify the subgroup algebraically. The explicit transposition between a bounded cofinality-sized set and a cofinal set provides a basic test witness for any proposed extension.

\begin{question}[Uniformities with an exhaustion interpretation]\label{swo:pc:n13.8}
Classify compatible complete uniformities on the regular permutation space that admit a direct label-coverage interpretation. At singular sizes, determine which inverse-control conditions can be added without changing the original topology on a specified subspace.
\end{question}
The forward, two-sided, and exhaustion-tree uniformities already separate three natural notions. A useful classification should distinguish equality of topology, uniform equivalence, and equality of completion boundary.

\subsubsection{Class theory, models, and formal verification}

\begin{question}[An axiomatization of virtual completion]\label{swo:pc:n13.9}
Give a reusable formal theory of prefix-completion schemes for class-coded structures, with the exact hypotheses needed for coherent unions, small-net rigidity, and inverse reconstruction. Can the whole theory be developed over a fragment weaker than the full assumptions used here?
\end{question}
The small-net argument isolates Class Replacement as the source of the uniform disagreement bound. An appropriate reverse-mathematical analysis would test that dependency, rather than assuming all class-theoretic principles have the same strength.

\begin{question}[Changing the class part without changing the sets]\label{swo:pc:n13.10}
For models $(M,\mathcal X)\subseteq(M,\mathcal Y)$, characterize which newly available injective branches are exhaustive and which new boundary traces they induce. Relate this to the existing preservation results for old, prefix-structured cuts.
\end{question}
A new class may be a new net, a new limit, or a new parameter defining a cut. Those are different mechanisms. Any forcing interpretation should separately verify the relevant class-forcing theorem and preservation hypotheses; none is assumed in this article.

\begin{question}[Unrestricted tails and their completion theory]\label{swo:pc:n13.11}
Develop analogues of the present completion constructions for arbitrary non-set-like labelled class well-orders. What prefix index structures are appropriate after a proper-class common segment, and how does finite-tail adjacency interact with those structures?
\end{question}
An $\Ord$-word model cannot merely be reused: it forgets the very tail that makes such an order non-set-like. The elementary common-prefix relation is a starting point that does not presuppose a comparison theorem for all class order types.

\begin{question}[A small trusted Lean core]\label{swo:pc:n13.12}
Formalize, without admitted new mathematical axioms, the short-prefix extension lemma, the cylinder-base theorem, forward completion, and the regular exhaustion-tree homeomorphism. Then instantiate them at $\No_{<\kappa}$ and separately formalize the class-model comparison theorem.
\end{question}
This would convert the main set-sized advances into checked mathematics while preserving the explicit boundary around global class semantics. The inspected simplicity interface can be reused when simplest separators are needed, but its existence hypothesis must still be discharged by an independent small-cut theorem.

\subsection{Source 25: further research questions and proposed projects}\label{swo:ph:sec:questions}

The questions below continue beyond the results proved here. They are proposed research problems arising from this investigation, not assertions that each is a previously published open problem.

\begin{question}[The exhaustive-branch stabilizer]\label{swo:ph:n16.1}
Characterize the subgroup of cylinder-preserving core automorphisms whose induced action permutes $\Hsl$. Can it be described by local compatibility conditions on the increasing maps between residual alphabets, rather than the global requirement that every branch still cover every label?
\end{question}
The represented-trace criterion is exact but global. Theorem~\ref{swo:ph:thm:noextension} shows that the entire cylinder group is too large. The countable rational-alphabet case is already a substantial, concrete version of this classification problem.

\begin{question}[Recognition without full rigidity]\label{swo:ph:n16.2}
Find natural enrichments strictly weaker than edge-label equality that recognize exhaustive branches while still admitting nontrivial automorphisms. Which relations are necessary to connect label occurrences across different depths, and which merely overdetermine that information?
\end{question}
Our negative result rules out recognition from the unlabelled core and any set of parameters. Our positive enrichment is sufficient and rigid. It does not establish a minimal language between those two extremes.

\begin{question}[Preserving a support filtration]\label{swo:ph:n16.3}
Let ${\Psupp(b)}_\alpha$ consist of core branches whose transition permutation is supported below $\alpha$. What remains of the automorphism group after requiring preservation of every ${\Psupp(b)}_\alpha$, or a cofinal subsequence of these levels? Does a support filtration recover any part of edge-label coherence?
\end{question}
The present back-and-forth preserves membership in the whole core but does not control the support of each image. The filtration is additional structure, distinct from the prefix-height relation, which is already recovered by cylinders.

\begin{question}[Larger configurations and exact obstruction patterns]\label{swo:ph:n16.4}
Which uniformly class-indexed configurations admit a simultaneous profile-preserving automorphism? Is there a useful criterion combining boundedness of divergence constraints at each stage with the avoidance of already determined noncore limit branches?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:ph:thm:cofinal-obstruction} supplies one necessary obstruction. A full characterization would need to distinguish failure of one-point realization from failure of completing an otherwise compatible partial automorphism.

\begin{question}[Singular-cardinal automorphism groups]\label{swo:ph:n16.5}
For singular $\kappa$, compare the cylinder structures of bounded-support and less-than-$\kappa$-support cores. Determine their orbit invariants, first-disagreement realization spectra, and automorphism-group cardinalities for saturated fragments or specified surreal birthday alphabets.
\end{question}
One must keep track of $|\No_{<\kappa}|=2^{<\kappa}$ as well as $\cf\kappa$. Remark~\ref{swo:ph:rem:singular-prefix} shows that even the underlying prefix families can differ. The regular formula $2^\kappa$ cannot simply be transferred by notation.

\begin{question}[Two baselines at once]\label{swo:ph:n16.6}
Given global enumerations $b,c$, study the structure carrying both cores ${\Psupp(b)}$ and ${\Psupp(b)}_c$ and their common prefix tree. How does the transition permutation $b^{-1}\circ c$ affect the joint automorphism group and recognition of exhaustive branches?
\end{question}
The elementary intersection question has an immediate answer: the two cores coincide exactly when $b$ and $c$ eventually agree, and otherwise they are disjoint. Indeed, a common core member would express both baselines as set-supported modifications of that member, making their transition permutation set-supported. A second, disjointly positioned core may constrain the symmetries of the first without naming every label; that joint structure is the unresolved part of the question.

\begin{question}[The bare order of exhaustive enumerations]\label{swo:ph:n16.7}
Classify order automorphisms of $\Hsl$ without assuming that they preserve a chosen core or its cylinder family. Which invariants of the enriched structures survive after both are forgotten? How do answers depend on the admitted class realization and on permitted uniformity of maps?
\end{question}
The earlier pure-order nonrigidity results and the present cylinder-preserving nonextension theorem constrain different directions. Neither is a classification of the full bare-order automorphism problem.

\begin{question}[Raw tails and outer-order invariants]\label{swo:ph:n16.8}
Can structural properties of the non-set-like tail of a raw class well-order be recognized from the outer lexicographic order, perhaps after adding a natural incidence relation? Which convex-fibre invariants distinguish raw well-orders that share the same initial set-like head?
\end{question}
Earlier condensation constructions produce complicated encoded tail orders \cite{swoSrc23}. The complication of an order encoded by a point is not automatically an invariant definable from the outer order of points. An explicit reconstruction or non-invariance argument is needed.

\begin{question}[The increasing-word analogue]\label{swo:ph:n16.9}
For the subtree of numerically increasing set-length words, determine the exact one-point extension property and its obstructions. Can an appropriate language of cross-coordinate inequalities yield an orbit classification analogous to Theorem~\ref{swo:ph:thm:homogeneity}?
\end{question}
The present automorphism group does not preserve this subtree. A successful analogue must retain more than sibling order and divergence, but perhaps less than full equality of labels across all edges.

\begin{question}[Class-realization reconstruction after forgetting labels]\label{swo:ph:n16.10}
Earlier continuation work reconstructs an admitted class realization from exhaustive traces over a labelled core. What part of that reconstruction survives under unlabelled isomorphism of core-and-cylinder structures? Which additional relations recover the lost distinction between exhaustive and nonexhaustive traces?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:ph:thm:invisible} prevents a direct label-free transfer of the coverage test. The question is now to identify surviving invariants, not to assume that the original decoder remains canonical in the reduct.

\begin{question}[A checked minimal development]\label{swo:ph:n16.11}
Formalize the regular set theorem, the countable two-orbit case, and the edge-coherent rigidity theorem with a common abstract alphabet interface. Can the maximum/no-maximum extension lemma be isolated as a reusable ordered-tree theorem independent of surreal numbers?
\end{question}
The suggested first deliverable is a kernel-checked one-point lemma plus supported completion. These are the two nontrivial inputs on which the longer back-and-forth proof depends.

\subsection{Source 26: further research questions and proposed projects}\label{swo:nb:sec:questions}

The following questions are proposed continuations. They are not all claimed to be previously published open problems. The singular complete-metrizability question of the earlier draft is no longer on this list: it is answered by Theorem~\ref{swo:nb:thm:completeclassification}. Likewise, the existence of direct comparison for non-set-like orders and the basic support-core coding are established background, not unresolved proposals.

\subsubsection{Descriptive complexity and closed subspaces}

\begin{question}[Generalized Borel complexity]\label{swo:nb:n14.1}
Determine the sharp complexity of $\WO_\mu(X)$ in appropriate generalized Borel and projective hierarchies when $\mu>\omega$ and $\cf\mu=\omega$. Which hierarchy matches the actual weight of the prefix space, rather than merely the cardinality of its index set?
\end{question}
The ordinary non-Borel theorem is a lower bound, not a complete answer to a generalized hierarchy question. The exhaustion formula is a $\mu$-indexed intersection of opens, and should be compared with the definitions and weight assumptions in singular generalized descriptive set theory~\cite{b83DimonteMottoRos}.

\begin{question}[Closed universality without $\mu>\mathfrak{c}$]\label{swo:nb:n14.2}
For an uncountable cardinal of countable cofinality with $\mu\le\mathfrak{c}$, characterize the separable metrizable spaces occurring as closed subspaces of $\WO_\mu(X)$. Must a closed copy of $\mathbb Q$ exist in $\ZFC$?
\end{question}
The present coding handles complements indexed by fewer than $\mu$ branches. It settles noncomplete metrizability in this regime but does not supply arbitrary Cantor traces. Improving the reservoir scheme or finding a genuinely different closed-subspace construction would be meaningful progress.

\begin{question}[Higher cofinality coding]\label{swo:nb:n14.3}
For $\cf\mu=\tau>\omega$, is there an analogue of Theorem~\ref{swo:nb:thm:coding} with a bounded-topology binary space of height $\tau$? What compactness, closed-image, and perfect-set substitutes remain valid?
\end{question}
A transfinite release schedule retains the least-disagreement combinatorics, but its topology is no longer ordinary compact metrizable Cantor space. The continuity and closed-image arguments must be replaced, not merely relabelled.

\begin{question}[The exact role of bounded inverse images]\label{swo:nb:n14.4}
Classify the topological and descriptive complexity of the intermediate spaces between $H_\mu$ and $\I^{\mathrm b}_\mu\cap\WO_\mu(\mu)$ (source~26's $\mathcal B^+\cap\mathcal P_\kappa(\kappa)$). Can the trace calculation involving $A$ and $\overline A$ be extended to higher closure or derived-set operations by additional inverse-control conditions?
\end{question}
Proposition~\ref{swo:nb:prop:closuretrace} provides a concrete starting model: the inverse condition transforms arbitrary exclusion of $A$ into exclusion of its topological closure. Any proposed hierarchy should state the controlled family of label sets exactly.

\subsubsection{Enumeration lengths and order structure}

\begin{question}[A classification across nonminimal strata]\label{swo:nb:n14.5}
For every ordinal $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|=|X|$, classify the prefix topology of $\WO_\lambda(X)$ and determine when it agrees with the enumeration order topology. Which residual-tail invariants govern complete metrizability?
\end{question}
Successor lengths are prefix-discrete, whereas initial infinite cardinal lengths have the classification proved here. Limit lengths with long finite or small-cardinal residual configurations form the next natural family. A statement depending only on $|\lambda|$ cannot suffice.

\begin{question}[Closed order embeddings versus topological embeddings]\label{swo:nb:n14.6}
For thick surreal alphabets, characterize which linear orders admit embeddings with closed image in the minimal enumeration space, and distinguish this from merely embedding their order topologies. Can prescribed Cantor traces be required to be convex or to respect named cylinder relations?
\end{question}
The marker construction gives closed images relative to the permutation space, but does not generally give convex images. Earlier prefix non-rigidity results caution that bare order automorphisms need not preserve an externally named prefix structure.

\begin{question}[Embedding spectra refined by topology]\label{swo:nb:n14.7}
Refine the earlier cardinal and ordinal embedding spectra by asking for continuous, closed, or prefix-preserving embeddings. Which of these spectra distinguish equimorphic surreal enumeration slices?
\end{question}
The new obstruction shows that mutual order embeddings alone leave substantial topology unresolved. The unconditional $\beth_\omega$ example is a useful test case because it does not depend on additional cardinal arithmetic.

\begin{question}[Dense-open intersection thresholds]\label{swo:nb:n14.8}
Determine the least cardinality of a family of dense open subsets of $\WO_\mu(X)$ whose intersection is not dense, and compare it with the corresponding invariant of $\I_\mu(X)$ and of $H_\mu$.
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:nb:thm:baire} settles the countable lower bound. The injection space has the explicit missing-label closed sets, while the bounded subgroup has the countable uniform-exhaustion description~\eqref{swo:nb:eq:H-gdelta}. These different structures may lead to different thresholds.

\subsubsection{Foundations, global orders, and verification}

\begin{question}[A topology that retains unrestricted class tails]\label{swo:nb:n14.9}
Develop a precise higher-sort or model-relative topology for arbitrary labelled class well-orders that distinguishes tails after a common proper-class prefix. How do the finite residual adjacent pairs sit in its completion theory?
\end{question}
Set-length prefix agreement alone is not Hausdorff on the unrestricted domain. The common-labelled-prefix formula gives an elementary comparison, but not by itself a full higher-order topology.

\begin{question}[Reverse foundations of uniform approximation]\label{swo:nb:n14.10}
What fragments of Class Replacement and choice suffice for small-net rigidity, the reserve extension theorem, and the diagonal noncoding theorem? Which implications can be reversed over a weak two-sorted base theory?
\end{question}
The proofs isolate different resources: set collection of disagreement bounds, completion of set partial permutations, and an elementary pair-swap diagonal. They need not all have the same axiomatic strength.

\begin{question}[Changing admitted class families]\label{swo:nb:n14.11}
For class-model extensions with the same sets, describe which new injective or exhaustive branches become available and how their traces interact with old uniformly coded cuts. What preservation principles keep the relevant prefix-completion schemes intact?
\end{question}
The problem concerns new relations and new uniform families, not a change in the internal well-foundedness of an old fixed relation under the $\GBC$ hypotheses explained in Section~\ref{swo:nb:sec:models}.

\begin{question}[A minimal kernel-checked continuation]\label{swo:nb:n14.12}
Formalize the compact omitted-label theorem, the non-Borel corollary, and the complete-metrizability classification on a general alphabet, then instantiate the result at $\No_{<\beth_\omega}$. How small can the trusted interface to classical descriptive set theory be made?
\end{question}
A useful milestone is a machine-checked exact range equation for the code, before any Borel hierarchy formalization. That theorem captures the main construction and can be reused independently of the final topological obstruction.

\subsection{Source 27: further research questions and priorities}
\label{swo:sc:sec:questions}

The following questions are continuations motivated by the proved
results. They are not asserted to be a catalogue of open problems
recognized in the published literature.

\begin{question}[Classify intermediate scan types]\label{swo:sc:q:scans}
For a set carrier of cardinality $\mu$, classify density,
cellularity, point characters, and finite convex blocks in
$\WO_{\mathsf s}(X)$ when the scan has type $\vartheta$ with $|\vartheta|=\mu$.
The cases $\vartheta=\mu$ and a carefully chosen $\mu+6$ are
settled here; the arrangement of dependencies between scanned pairs,
not only $\theta$, may matter. A first target is the complete
classification of countable scans of type $\omega+n$.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Recover the effective scan]\label{swo:sc:n12.2}
Which oriented pair priorities are determined by the labelled order
on well-orders? Swapping a single adjacent pair recovers its first
orientation; swapping two disjoint adjacent pairs recovers their
relative priority. Priorities of pairs sharing a label can be
redundant because transitivity constrains their bits. Classify
effective scans modulo equality of their induced labelled orders.
The three-label diagnostic gives $36$ orders from $48$ scans.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[The table-ordered bounded-support core]\label{swo:sc:n12.3}
The same set-coded core is dense in the raw table order under a
set-like scan, but its order now depends on that scan. Determine
when it has endpoints, which uniform set cuts it fills, and which
scan invariants control its isomorphism type. Its numerical-enumeration
order is isomorphic to $\No$; that fact cannot simply be transferred
to its table order.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[A sharper type for centered increasing words]\label{swo:sc:n12.4}
Is
\[
 \mathbf{T}_{\min}^{\op}\times_{\lex}\mathbf{T}_{\min}
 \ \cong\ \mathbf{T}_{\min}^{+}?
\]
The product theorem answers the factorization problem, and
\eqref{swo:sc:eq:wordabsorption} proves several sum identities, but neither
settles this isomorphism. Determine a distinguishing invariant or
construct an isomorphism. Equality of known local character spectra
would not alone suffice.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Orders at genuine surreal gaps]\label{swo:sc:n12.5}
Classify $\WordsInc_\varepsilon(\No)$ (source~27's $\mathrm{Inc}_C(\No)$) for cuts $\No=L+R$ with one side of set
cofinality or coinitiality. \Cref{swo:sc:prop:gapcharacters} computes point
characters, and a gap with a set-coinitial right side is separated
from the standard centered order. Do those characters classify all
such constructions? A stronger classification of every unfilled
set cut has not been proved here and should be treated as a new
theorem to establish, not inferred from the point table.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[The subgroup preserving exhaustive branches]\label{swo:sc:n12.6}
Classify the ordered-prefix-tree automorphisms for which both the
map and its inverse preserve exhaustive $\Ord$-branches. The exact
obstruction is an exhaustive branch through a subtree avoiding one
output label. Uniform birthday bounds are sufficient but not
necessary, and antichain tail transformations give additional
examples. An ordinal-valued progress condition for the varying
forbidden labels is a concrete next target.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Weaker enrichments than label equality]\label{swo:sc:n12.7}
Cross-node equality of appended labels yields exactly global
numerical relabellings. Which strictly weaker predicates already
force preservation of exhaustiveness? Possible data include birthday
strata, equality of birthdays, and incidence with designated bounded
label sets. These enrichments should be tested separately; preserving
the unlabelled tree and sibling orders is now known to be insufficient.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Raw extensions of core automorphisms]\label{swo:sc:n12.8}
For a class part fixed externally, characterize automorphisms of
a chosen core that extend to the full raw order, taking account
of the complete tail fiber over each represented nonexhaustive
branch. The set-like extension criterion concerns exhaustive
traces; raw extensions must also preserve the residual orders.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Marked model reconstruction with fewer constants]\label{swo:sc:n12.9}
\Cref{swo:sc:thm:markedmodels} fixes every core element pointwise. What
smaller collection of predicates or distinguished subsets suffices
to recover the class part, perhaps up to an automorphism of the
set universe? Investigate expanded countable models before claiming
an intrinsic invariant of the unmarked order.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Optimize the interpolant, not just a fixed prefix]\label{swo:sc:n12.10}
The ordinal support optimum is exact for a prescribed partial
injection. For a separated cut, many prefixes may yield an
interpolant. Minimize the optimum over those prefixes, then compare
ordinal support height with sign-code birthday. This may produce
sharper constructive bounds for the dense-core realization theorem.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Controlled bounded approximations]\label{swo:sc:n12.11}
Determine which class constructions admit coherent versions across
birthday stages, especially singular and noninitial cutoffs.
The set self-copy theorem here works at every infinite cutoff, but
the homogeneous back-and-forth used for word and prefix isomorphisms
requires additional closure at a fixed stage. Preserve the difference
between full set-word trees and trees truncated before their terminal
level.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[First machine-checked theorem package]\label{swo:sc:n12.12}
Implement the generic terminal-cut factorization, the six-coordinate
scan theorem, and the support cutoff criterion first. These give
small, independently useful milestones with explicit set-level
statements. The next milestone should be the elementary labelled
class-prefix comparison inside an explicit model, followed by the
uniform diagonal theorem. This ordering resolves concrete foundational
obligations before attempting the larger automorphism constructions.
\end{question}

\subsubsection{What the continuation has resolved}

The new results locate several boundaries more sharply than an ordinal
spectrum alone can. A scan can retain that spectrum while changing
isolation and density. An ordered prefix tree can retain every local
numerical comparison while losing exhaustive coverage. An ordinary
class core can be dense for relation tables while no uniform ordinary
class family is dense for raw enumeration comparison. A support bound
can be optimal in cardinality while far from optimal in ordinal
height. The surviving questions ask which additional structure
recovers the information lost at each boundary.

\subsection{Source 28: further research questions and topics}\label{swo:ge:sec:questions}

\subsubsection{Singular topology and descriptive complexity}

\begin{question}[Complete metrizability of the full singular space]\label{swo:ge:q:complete}
Let $\mu>\omega$ be singular with $\cf\mu=\omega$. Is $\Sym(\mu)$, with its bounded-prefix topology, completely metrizable? Equivalently, is it a $G_\delta$ subspace of the complete forward injection space?
\end{question}
The dense complete locus ${B_\mu^-}$ and the Baire property do not decide this question. Nor does the incompleteness of the forward metric. A positive proof must organize all label-coverage requirements into countably many ambient open requirements, or construct a complete compatible metric directly. A negative proof must rule out all compatible complete metrics, not just the chosen forward one. Appendix~\ref{swo:ge:app:metric} supplies the precise equivalence.

\begin{question}[The singular envelope's exact character]\label{swo:ge:n2}
Determine $\cof([\mu]^{<\mu},\subseteq)$ for significant singular cardinals, and isolate which additional cardinal-arithmetic hypotheses yield an exact value between $\mu^+$ and $\mu^{<\mu}$.
\end{question}
The elementary diagonal gives a uniform strict lower bound, not an exact formula. Further work should compare the cofinality of the whole small-subset poset with fixed-size subset cofinalities and with appropriate possible-cofinality methods, without replacing one invariant by another on the basis of notation alone.

\begin{question}[Descriptive complexity of the one-sided loci]\label{swo:ge:n3}
For uncountable $\cf\mu$, determine the natural generalized Borel complexity of ${B_\mu^+}$, ${B_\mu^-}$, and ${H_\mu}$ in the forward injection and permutation spaces. For countable cofinality, classify ${B_\mu^-}$ as a complete nonseparable metric space and its placement inside $S_\mu$.
\end{question}
The formulas in Section~\ref{swo:ge:sec:onesided} are exact starting points. A classification should keep track of the actual weight $\mu^{<\mu}$, which can exceed $\mu$. The singular descriptive-set-theoretic framework of Dimonte and Motto Ros~\cite{b83DimonteMottoRos} is relevant background, but applying its results requires matching the space's weight and topology rather than only its indexing cardinal.

\subsubsection{Algebra and reconstruction}

\begin{question}[Abstract automorphisms versus the natural normalizer]\label{swo:ge:n4}
Is every abstract or continuous automorphism of ${H_\mu}$ induced by a permutation of its natural carrier? Under what hypotheses can the action, or the bounded-set ideal, be reconstructed intrinsically?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{swo:ge:thm:normalizer} only classifies conjugations by carrier permutations that preserve the subgroup. Proposition~\ref{swo:ge:prop:recover} reconstructs the ideal when the action is already named. These are useful constraints, but neither is an automatic solution of the abstract automorphism problem.

\begin{question}[Subgroups without all finitary permutations]\label{swo:ge:n5}
Classify natural subgroups not contained in ${H_\mu}$ and not containing all finitary permutations on which the inherited forward topology is a group topology. Which non-discrete examples exist?
\end{question}
The maximality theorem identifies its exact hypothesis rather than forbidding every alternative subgroup. Such a classification should determine when internal transposition witnesses are absent and whether that absence reflects a useful structural constraint or merely a very small group.

\begin{question}[Intermediate coordinate ideals]\label{swo:ge:n6}
For admissible ideals $\mathcal{J}$, classify $H_\mathcal{J}$, the closure of $H_\mathcal{J}$ in $\tau_\mathcal{J}$, and the gap between $\mathcal{J}$ and $\mathcal{J}^{\mathrm{sym}}$. Which ideals lead to self-normalizing ideal-preserving subgroups?
\end{question}
The general continuity and envelope theorems already apply. The self-normalizer proof for boundedness uses a special ``bounded part plus cofinal part'' lemma, so its extension should isolate an analogue of that lemma rather than assume every ideal behaves like the bounded ideal.

\subsubsection{Numerical order and nonminimal enumerations}

\begin{question}[Order automorphisms and the coordinate bornology]\label{swo:ge:n7}
Which order automorphisms of a thick minimal enumeration order preserve its forward uniformity, its injective completion, or the small-set group envelope? What additional named structure is needed to recover prefix cylinders or the chosen label filtration?
\end{question}
The earlier continuation~\cite{swoSrc13} exhibits prefix non-rigidity, so a universal reconstruction claim from the pure order alone is not the right target. The question is to identify the appropriate expanded structure or the exact extension criterion.

\begin{question}[Nonminimal ordinal lengths and residual tails]\label{swo:ge:n8}
For $\Bij(\alpha,X)$ with $|\alpha|=|X|$ but $\alpha$ not the initial cardinal, develop analogues of the ideal-continuity and completion results. How do finite residual tails and limit positions change local character, adjacency, and the supply of extendible prefixes?
\end{question}
The initial-cardinal hypothesis in Lemma~\ref{swo:ge:lem:prefix} should be replaced by exact residual-domain and residual-range conditions. This is likely a more informative approach than trying to transfer the minimal-slice theorems wholesale to the full fixed-carrier order.

\begin{question}[Order-type classification beyond topology]\label{swo:ge:n9}
Which numerical features of two thick alphabets force their minimal enumeration orders to be isomorphic, equimorphic, or nonisomorphic? Which invariants survive after their homeomorphic prefix spaces have forgotten the alphabet order?
\end{question}
The countable comparison with the irrationals already shows that topological classification is insufficient. Dedekind boundary types, interval decompositions, and the interaction with label order provide concrete candidates, whereas cardinality and ordinal spectrum alone are too coarse.

\subsubsection{Class foundations and verification}

\begin{question}[Global control schemes over weaker theories]\label{swo:ge:n10}
What are the weakest class-theoretic assumptions sufficient for the supported-prefix extension, small-net rigidity, and inverse-reconstruction schemes? Can their uses of Class Replacement and uniform set choice be separated sharply?
\end{question}
These proofs have different logical mechanisms: image bounding, choosing residual set bijections, and elementary eventual-value comprehension. A reverse-mathematical analysis should examine those mechanisms individually rather than assign the same strength to every global completion assertion.

\merge\ (3 October 2026, batch~89.) Answered in part by source~31 (Part~XV),
which names this question. It separates three mechanisms, selection, collapse
and coding, and image bounding (\cref{swo:gcz:sec:formal}). Over Zermelo set
theory with Choice, selection restricted to countable inputs, with Separation
for the selector, is already nonconservative (\cref{swo:gcz:thm:main}, through
an unreviewed interface to Glazer's countermodels); in the full-class rank
models global choice holds at every height, while ordinal coding and image
bounding have different exact thresholds, and Class Replacement on a set holds
exactly when its size is below the cofinality of the height
(\cref{swo:gcz:lem:domain,swo:gcz:thm:replacement,swo:gcz:cor:decompose}). The
weakest assumptions for each of the three named schemes are not determined;
source~31 restates that remainder as its \cref{swo:gcz:n10}
(\cref{swo:gcz:sec:qstatus}).

\begin{question}[Non-set-like tails and class completion]\label{swo:ge:n11}
Construct a completion theory for arbitrary class well-orders that uses the direct common-prefix relation and continues through proper-class initial segments. Which kinds of index orders, or external universe levels, are necessary to retain the tails?
\end{question}
An $\Ord$-word completion cannot see a tail following a full $\Ord$ prefix. The finite-tail examples give mandatory tests for any proposed theory, and Theorem~\ref{swo:ge:thm:rawlex} supplies a comparison relation that does not presuppose a class-order-type calculus.

\begin{question}[A verified ideal-to-surreal pipeline]\label{swo:ge:n12}
Formalize the generic ideal-envelope and maximal-subgroup results, the singular self-normalizer, and the character diagonal, then instantiate them at a rigorously sized surreal cutoff. Develop the global class-model statements as a separate semantic layer.
\end{question}
This target directly extends the inspected source without conflating its simplicity theorem with cut existence. A successful implementation should record theorem-to-file mappings, universe levels, and the distinction between compiled proofs, imported assumptions, and model-theoretic hypotheses.

\subsection{Source 29: further research questions after these results}\label{swo:bw:sec:agenda}

The agenda below is revised in light of both the pinned source and
the present proofs. Several questions in older lists have acquired
answers: the centered increasing-word type has a product description;
actual numerical thresholds reduce by translation; all noninitial
strata have the stated residual analysis; and complete condensation
histories have an exact equivalence with strong class comparability.
The following questions concern what is still missing.

\begin{question}[The remaining singular upper code]\label{swo:bw:rq:singular}
Let $\lambda$ be singular and not strong limit. Under what hypotheses
on a $\lambda$-sized ordered residual alphabet $Y$ does
\[
 \WO_\lambda(Y)\emb\B_\lambda
\]
hold? In particular, settle the residual cases $\lambda\le\kappa$
in \Cref{swo:bw:ns:cor:coding} for which the ordinal bounds $\varrho_{\mathrm{lo}}<\varrho_{\mathrm{up}}$ remain
different after absorption.
\end{question}

The exact embedded-cube spectrum does not answer this question.
A proof must construct an upper code, or exhibit an obstruction
stronger than the absence of a larger binary cube. The countable
and finite-aleph birthday bands avoid the unresolved residual case
and supply useful fully classified test instances.

\begin{question}[Isomorphism on a constant-cardinality birthday band]\label{swo:bw:n13.2}
For fixed $\alpha$ of cardinality $\mathfrak c$, determine when
\[
 \WO_\alpha(\No_{<\theta})\cong\WO_\alpha(\No_{<\eta}),
 \qquad\omega<\theta,\eta<\omega_1.
\]
Do some of these orders distinguish $\theta$ and $\eta$ even though
all have the same equimorphism type given by
\Cref{swo:bw:ns:cor:countable}?
\end{question}

The native alphabets themselves form a strict embeddability chain.
The problem is to identify which of that information survives in
the pure permutation order. Gap arrangement, local completeness,
and the distribution of residual order types are possible invariants;
the finite-tail topology illustrates why cardinal spectra alone
can miss a distinction.

\begin{question}[Infinite tails at the countable alphabet]\label{swo:bw:n13.3}
Classify the native topology and Borel structure of
$\WO_\alpha(\mathbb{Q})$ for countable $\alpha\ge\omega\cdot2$.
Determine their exact relation to the coordinate Borel structure,
and identify natural standard Borel subspaces or quotients.
\end{question}

The article compares the coordinate and native topologies at every
countable length, but gives the complete measurable classification
only for finite tails after $\omega$. For longer types, the tail
is an infinite order varying with the omitted alphabet. It cannot
be replaced by a constant finite split. The cellularity argument in
\Cref{swo:bw:tp:prop:borel-relation} already implies that all these full
native Borel structures are non-countably-generated and hence
nonstandard: they contain $2^{\mathfrak c}$ distinct open sets,
whereas a countably generated sigma-algebra has at most
$\mathfrak c$ members.

\begin{question}[Intrinsic geometry of the centered product]\label{swo:bw:n13.4}
What are the order automorphisms of
${\mathbf{T}_{\min}}^{\mathrm{op}}\mathbin{\times_\lex}{\mathbf{T}_{\min}}$? Are its displayed lower-prefix
fibers recognizable from the pure order, perhaps after naming a
small amount of structure? Is there a simpler canonical presentation
that explains its full cut arrangement?
\end{question}

The factorization is an explicit isomorphism theorem. It does not
assert that its fibers are definable from the resulting bare order.
The earlier failures of prefix recovery make this a real additional
problem rather than a notational reformulation.

\begin{question}[Nonprincipal termination cuts]\label{swo:bw:n13.5}
Classify increasing-word orders whose distinct terminator lies at
a nonprincipal class cut with a set cofinal family on the lower
side or a set coinitial family on the upper side.
\end{question}

The factorization in \Cref{swo:bw:wp:factorization} reduces the question
to increasing words over the two cut sides. Actual surreal
thresholds and nonprincipal cuts whose two sides both retain the
full set-cut property are already covered by
\Cref{swo:bw:wp:thresholds}. The remaining cases should be parameterized
by genuine cofinality and endpoint data, not by the numerical value
of a threshold that translation removes.

\begin{question}[The dense quotient of numerical class carriers]\label{swo:bw:n13.6}
Classify the shorter-first numerical class-carrier order after
contracting the adjacent pairs of \Cref{swo:bw:nc:adjacency}. Which
properties of the upper cones $U(A)$ survive in this quotient?
Can the range of available final-segment orders be encoded as a
canonical family of decorations on it?
\end{question}

\Cref{swo:bw:nc:cofinal} supplies every possible numerical final class
segment as an available-letter order after an increasing prefix.
A classification must therefore address arbitrary class cuts,
rather than only bounded-support or set-prefix data.

\begin{question}[The exhaustive-branch stabilizer]\label{swo:bw:n13.7}
Characterize the uniform systems of local increasing residual
bijections that preserve every exhaustive class branch of the
injection tree. Are there useful generators or closure operations
for the resulting subgroup?
\end{question}

\Cref{swo:bw:ta:fixed-stage} gives a substantial explicit family of such
automorphisms. \Cref{swo:bw:ta:branch-transitivity,swo:bw:ta:bounded-stage-agreement}
show that prefix coherence and every single fixed set-height
restriction are insufficient tests. The condition must express
global coverage of labels, not just local successor-order behavior.

\begin{question}[Comparability versus stronger recursion]\label{swo:bw:n13.8}
Investigate the relation of $\CWO$, and therefore $\CTH$, to
$\ETR$, continuous rankings, and weak comparability by arbitrary
suborder embeddings.
\end{question}

Hamkins--Woodin formulate these comparisons in their Question~7
\cite{HamkinsWoodin}. The present article supplies a new equivalent
presentation of the strong comparability principle; it does not
settle the converses involving stronger recursion. Finite normal
forms from a history may make that boundary easier to study,
because they identify what a condensation-specific construction
can provide without a universal truth recursion.

\merge\ (4 October 2026, batch~96.) Not settled by Part~XVI. Over $\GB$,
sources~34 and~35 add equivalent forms of $\CWO$: canonical histories and
initial embeddings into $P(W)$ (\cref{swo:bo:hist:equivalence,swo:fc:gb-comparability}),
and source~35's fixed-point extension principle $\FPE$
(\cref{swo:fc:cor:FPE-CWO}, over $\GB$ by \cref{swo:xvi:thm:choicefree}).

\begin{question}[Alternative condensation limits]\label{swo:bw:n13.9}
How do different limit conventions compare with the nested
least-representative rule used here? Which retain finite normal
forms or the equivalence with strong comparability?
\end{question}

For the present rule, \Cref{swo:bw:ch:quotient-limits} proves that the
induced equivalence relation at a limit is the union of the
earlier equivalences. This removes one ambiguity. Conventions
that choose new representatives or form an external quotient
without retained anchors can have different existence requirements.

\begin{question}[Recovering a class realization from an expanded order]\label{swo:bw:n13.10}
Which additional predicates on the global enumeration order, its
core, or its ordered prefix tree determine the available class
collection up to an appropriate isomorphism?
\end{question}

The bare external set-like enumeration order of a countable
two-sorted class model can be $\mathbb{Q}$. Naming heights and successor orders still permits the
branch changes of \Cref{swo:bw:ta:branch-transitivity}. Literal label
evaluation is sufficient to rule out those particular changes,
but whether a substantially smaller invariant family of predicates
recovers the intended realization remains open in this analysis.

\begin{question}[Scan equivalence for relation encodings]\label{swo:bw:n13.11}
Classify the order types obtained from different well-ordered scans
of relation tables on a fixed surreal carrier or birthday set.
Identify natural hypotheses under which two scans induce
isomorphic, equimorphic, or provably different orders of well-orders.
\end{question}

The existing endpoint examples already rule out scan-independence
in general. A useful next theorem should specify a structural
class of scans and compare their effects without silently replacing
relation-bit comparison by enumeration comparison.

\begin{question}[A certified mathematical core]\label{swo:bw:n13.12}
Implement the set-sized first-difference, binary fusion, birthday
spectrum, and canonical word-factorization results in Lean on top
of the inspected sign-sequence foundation. Then formalize the
normal-form theorem from a supplied history in an explicitly
chosen class or universe-relative framework.
\end{question}

The native spectrum is a particularly focused first target: its
statement is exact at every ordinal cutoff, its proof is independent
of Global Choice, and its delicate limit invariant is explicit.
Success there would provide a reusable library for the later
permutation and class-level constructions.

\subsection{Source 30: research questions after the new results}\label{swo:rt:sec:research}

The following are proposed research tasks for this program.
Where a problem is inherited, its remaining scope is narrowed
by the theorems above. The list is not a claim that every item
is an independently established open problem throughout the
literature.

\subsubsection{Residual coding beyond the classified cases}

\begin{question}[Singular residual cardinals that are not strong limit]\label{swo:rt:n12.1}
Suppose $\nu\leq\kappa$, $\nu<2^{<\kappa}$, is singular and not strong limit.
Determine the exact equimorphism type of
$\WO_{\mu\gamma+\nu\delta+n}(\No_{<\kappa})$ in ZFC.
\end{question}

The present proof gives a concrete interval of possibilities:
pair orientations give a lower binary factor of length
$\nu\delta$, while padding the entry codes gives an upper
factor of length $\nu^2\delta$, appended after
$\rho_\kappa\gamma$. The strong-limit lower construction
cannot simply be reused because $\No_{<\nu}$ may contain
more than $\nu$ labels. A productive approach is to identify
which $\nu$-sized residual alphabets can replace its disjoint
sign cones. The aim is a coding-capacity theorem for arbitrary
residual alphabets, not just a cardinality estimate.

\begin{question}[Dependence on cardinal arithmetic]\label{swo:rt:n12.2}
Which additional cardinal-arithmetic hypotheses, weaker than
GCH, guarantee the full fixed-type classification? Can two
models with the same relevant cardinalities have different
residual binary coding lengths?
\end{question}

The mixed-block theorem already gives one sufficient condition:
every singular cardinal at most $\kappa$ actually encountered
in the finite cardinal descent is strong limit; larger residual
cardinals are covered by the native padded code. No hypothesis about unrelated
cardinals is needed. The next step is to decide whether this
condition is necessary or merely sufficient.

\subsubsection{Topological classification beyond invariants}

\begin{question}[The positive finite-prefix spaces]\label{swo:rt:n12.3}
Are $E_n$ and $E_m$ homeomorphic for all positive finite
$n,m$? What about their doubled orders and the spaces
$P_n$ for $n\geq3$?
\end{question}

All $E_n$ for $n>0$ share the proper $\Delta^0_3$
description and meagreness proved here. These invariants do
not classify their homeomorphism types. (\merge\ Source~30's $P_n$ is
$P_{\omega+n}$ here.) The doubled-space
Borel formula adds a precise constraint: any candidate
homeomorphism has to respect the countable-exception
structure of measurable separation of fibers.

\begin{question}[Later countable ordinal types]\label{swo:rt:n12.4}
For arbitrary countable $\alpha>\omega+2$, determine the
Cantor--Bendixson derivative sequence and Baire-category
behavior of $\WO_\alpha(\mathbb Q)$.
\end{question}

The non-Borel ranking obstruction is already known from
\cref{swo:rt:cor:later-countable-nonmeasurable}; that should not be
left as the main unresolved question. What remains is a
structural analysis of the order topology itself, especially
at limit remainders, where finite fibers no longer describe
the whole local geometry.


\begin{question}[Reverse coding at later countable types]\label{swo:rt:n12.5}
For which countable $\alpha\geq\omega+\omega$ is the map from
lexicographic enumerations to relation tables Borel measurable?
What structural feature of the terminal order determines its
failure or success?
\end{question}

The opposite-direction ranking map already fails to be Borel
at every $\alpha\geq\omega+3$. The reverse direction requires
a separate analysis. At $\omega+2$, one binary endpoint-orientation
predicate repairs the measurable presentation exactly
(\cref{swo:rt:prop:single-orientation-enrichment}); that case is settled.
For $n\geq3$, the lexicographic Borel structure contains too many
sets to be contained in any standard Borel structure on the same
carrier. An appropriate standard presentation must therefore
change which sets are measurable, rather than simply add
predicates to all existing order-open sets.

\subsubsection{Global scans and reconstruction}

\begin{question}[Arbitrary scans and non-set-like jumps]\label{swo:rt:n12.6}
Is relation-table lexicography on all class well-orders
dense for every set-like scan? If not, characterize a scan
and a pair of non-set-like orders producing a jump.
\end{question}

Theorem~\ref{swo:rt:reltable:arbitrary-density} settles the set-like
suborder, and Theorem~\ref{swo:rt:reltable:canonical} settles the
explicit max-index scan even on all class orders. Neither
proof alone settles every scan on all orders. A counterexample
would have to exploit proper-class predecessor structure
that cannot be closed into the common initial set used in
the set-like proof.

\begin{question}[Topologies determined by scans]\label{swo:rt:n12.7}
Classify when a scan's support topology and its order
topology agree. Determine which changes of scan preserve
the intrinsic local-character description of bounded
inversion support.
\end{question}

Our canonical scan already separates these topologies and
identifies one-sided set coinitiality with bounded inversion
support. A general classification should explain how much
of this asymmetry is a scan artifact and how much is forced
by well-foundedness.

\begin{question}[How much named core suffices?]\label{swo:rt:n12.8}
Find intermediate named structures between a unary predicate
for the support core and its pointwise embedding that recover
the class realization.
\end{question}

The endpoints are now precise:
\cref{swo:rt:fnd:prop:coloredcore} shows that even a baseline point
and the whole core named setwise can lose ETR, while fixing
the core pointwise recovers all labels through its represented
cuts. Candidates include prefix cylinders, the evaluation
map on a structured subfamily, or the pair-swap Boolean
operations. The distinction between a countable external
language and an internal uniform family must be preserved.

\begin{question}[Uncountable realizations and common baselines]\label{swo:rt:n12.9}
Which analogues of the universal-baseline theorem hold for
uncountable set models? Which external order invariants of
their admitted enumeration spaces detect more than the
cardinality of the class collection?
\end{question}

The countable argument uses both Cantor back-and-forth and
Williams's countable minimum-realization theorem.
Removing countability is not a routine restatement. The
labelled inclusion theorem itself does not need it and
provides a useful comparison standard.

\subsubsection{Foundational and formal priorities}

The most concrete next formalization target is the
prefix-free code together with the regular block-length
lemma. It is self-contained, uses already available
small-cut foundations, and supports every regular residual
case. The next difficult target is the singular scheduler.
The most compact class-theoretic target is pair coding
and its decoder; the most informative local-to-global
target is partial-table extension.

A broader foundational question asks how much choice
follows from universality of the surreal \emph{numerical}
order for all class linear orders, without assuming a
global well-order of its labels. That is a different
question from \cref{swo:rt:thm:choice-baseline}; it was posed
explicitly by Hamkins \cite{HamkinsUnivChoice}.
Nothing in the present proof settles that question, and
the global baselines used here cannot be assumed in an
argument attempting to derive global choice.

For every type $\alpha=\mu\gamma+\sum_{i<k}\lambda_i\eta_i+n$ of

Open: singular non-strong-limit residual cardinals at most $\kappa$

Dedekind completion with a dense meagre $F_\sigma$ of omitted points, every open
interval is isomorphic to the whole order, finite partial maps extend, and
prefix cylinders are not intrinsic (sources~21 and~24,

of every stratum are known (\cref{swo:rg:thm:topology,swo:rg:thm:finite-chars}).
The isomorphism type at uncountable cutoffs is open.

% ---- hand chunk q31 (batch 89)
\subsection{Source 31's research questions (batch 89)}\label{swo:gcz:sec:questions}

\merge\ (3 October 2026.) Source~31's Section~13, ``Further research
questions'', printed whole; its questions~1--12 are numbered here in this
section's sequence and labelled \code{swo:gcz:n1}--\code{swo:gcz:n12}.

% ---- source 31 (batch-89 manuscript 01), lines 1265-1381

The following questions are proposed directions. Except where explicitly
identified as repository questions, they are formulated here and are not being
advertised as a catalog of established open problems. Each distinguishes a
specific missing step from results proved above.

\begin{question}[Global selection from finite sets]\label{swo:gcz:n1}
Is \(\ZC\) with a selector on all nonempty finite sets and expanded Separation
nonconservative over \(\ZC\)? What changes with Foundation?
\end{question}
The present proof uses selection on every nonempty subset of a countable carrier.
Finite-input selection does not supply that operation. Enayat's global finite
choice principles provide relevant background, but do not by themselves settle
this Zermelo conservativity question.

\begin{question}[Pairs and bounded finite cardinalities]\label{swo:gcz:n2}
For a fixed integer \(m\ge2\), what pure set-theoretic consequences follow from
a class selector on \(m\)-element sets, with expanded Separation? Can these
consequences distinguish different \(m\)?
\end{question}
A proof would require either a different obstruction model or a new reduction
from finite-input choices to a useful uniform presentation. Arbitrary
countable-set enumeration cannot simply be assumed.

\begin{question}[The Separation complexity needed by the refinement]\label{swo:gcz:n3}
Which finite collection, or syntactic fragment, of Separation instances involving
the selector suffices for \cref{swo:gcz:thm:main}?
\end{question}
The proof gives explicit containing sets, but its defining formulas include
well-order tests and unbounded quantification over class labels. Boundedness of
the output is not a claim that every defining formula is \(\Delta_0\).
Tracking the actual formulas is a feasible formalization project.

\begin{question}[Reducing ordinary Choice]\label{swo:gcz:n4}
How much of ordinary \(\AC\) can be removed from the localized
nonconservativity theorem?
\end{question}
The positive uniformization proof only asks for well-orders of \(D\) and
\(\mathcal C_D\); for \(D=\omega\), the latter can be coded by a fixed
set of reals. A complete weakening must also recheck the base countermodel and
the final cardinal obstruction, rather than dropping Choice from the proof
statement alone.

\begin{question}[Fragments that restore conservativity]\label{swo:gcz:n5}
Which Replacement or Collection fragments suffice to restore conservativity for
countable-input global selection with expanded Separation?
\end{question}
Collecting every definable \(\omega\)-family destroys the particular
class-family obstruction used here. That observation does not establish a
general conservativity theorem, which would require an expansion or forcing
argument for arbitrary models of the chosen base.

\begin{question}[Selectors beyond the countable threshold]\label{swo:gcz:n6}
For well-ordered sets \(D\) and \(E\), when do restricted global selection
on \(D\)-small and on \(E\)-small sets have the same original-language
consequences over a fixed weak base?
\end{question}
Every bound containing \(\omega\) already gives our nonconservativity witness.
The uniform presentation theorem supplies a common method of comparison but
does not collapse the full hierarchy of consequences.

\begin{question}[Definable-class versions of the spectra]\label{swo:gcz:n7}
What replaces the rank-model classification when the admitted classes are
\(\operatorname{Def}(V_\lambda,p)\), rather than all external subclasses?
\end{question}
External cardinal equality then need not produce an admitted bijection, and a
cofinal witness to Replacement failure need not be definable from the permitted
parameter. The full-class answers provide bounds and test cases, not an answer
to this definability problem.

\merge\ (4 October 2026, batch~96.) Answered in part, for the external order
types at a strongly inaccessible height: for the classes definable over
$V_\kappa$ in a fixed finite language with set parameters the realized types
form an interval $[0,\Theta_L)$ with $\kappa<\Theta_L<\kappa^+$, of countable
cofinality under a named global well-order, closed under ordinal arithmetic,
and raised by a truth predicate, which represents the old ceiling exactly
(sources~32--35; \cref{swo:xvi:sec:status}~(e)). The analogues of the
thresholds of Part~XV for definable classes remain open.

\begin{question}[Abstract weak-theory equivalences]\label{swo:gcz:n8}
Find a natural two-sorted extension of \(\ZC\) over which particular
surreal coding principles characterize ordinal abstraction, an image-bounding
scheme, or a restricted class-choice principle.
\end{question}
Our exact equivalences are semantic statements about \(\RM_\lambda\).
Turning one into an abstract equivalence requires a proof for arbitrary models,
including models without the full external rank hierarchy or all subclasses.

\begin{question}[All set-like order types at a cutoff]\label{swo:gcz:n9}
Classify the external order types of every internally set-like well-order of
\(S_\lambda\), especially at singular and non-strong-limit heights.
\end{question}
We classify whether some such order has type \(\lambda\), and whether it
can respect birthdays. A classification of all possible types requires control
of the birthday bounds on every proper initial segment and may contain more
information than cardinality alone.

\begin{question}[The repository's global control schemes]\label{swo:gcz:n10}
For each precise supported-prefix extension, small-net rigidity, and
inverse-reconstruction scheme in ProveIt, identify the minimum selection,
collapse, and image-bounding assumptions.
\end{question}
This is the remaining program behind \code{swo:ge:n10} (\cref{swo:ge:n10}). The domain-size
criterion can test candidate image-bounding claims, while bounded trace
compression may test claims that a uniform presentation is available. No
equivalence for all three schemes has been proved here.

\begin{question}[A verified bounded uniformization theorem]\label{swo:gcz:n11}
Can a proof assistant verify \cref{swo:gcz:thm:uniform,swo:gcz:thm:compression} over an explicit
Zermelo axiom interface, with no imported theorem using Replacement?
\end{question}
This is a concrete near-term target. Every newly formed set can carry its
containing-set witness as part of the formal construction. A separate module
can then instantiate the theorem with the Glazer obstruction interface.

\begin{question}[Surreal transfer and parameter-sensitive choice]\label{swo:gcz:n12}
Can the distinctions between uniform choice, ordinal coding, and admitted
definability be used to sharpen the obstruction to definable transfer expansions
of \(\No\)?
\end{question}
Hamkins's surreal transfer question and Glazer's contribution to its discussion
are a direct further intersection \cite{gczSurrealTransfer}. Our results concern
weak foundations and full-class rank models. They do not settle transfer in
\(\ZFC\) with arbitrary set parameters; a solution would require a separate
definability or forcing argument.

\merge\ Status of source~31's questions, 3 October 2026. All twelve are
proposed continuations. \Cref{swo:gcz:n9} is answered at strongly inaccessible
heights by source~12's \cref{swo:st:thm:model}~(ii): there every internally
set-like global well-order of $\No_{<\kappa}=S_\kappa$ has external type $\kappa$;
elsewhere it is open. \Cref{swo:gcz:n10} restates the open remainder of
source~28's \cref{swo:ge:n10}, item~(a) below. \Cref{swo:gcz:n11} is a
formalization proposal. \Cref{swo:gcz:n12} concerns Hamkins's surreal transfer
question \cite{gczSurrealTransfer}, not the universality question of
\cref{swo:sec:answers}~(f). The others are open; this write found no answer to
them elsewhere in this report.

and the capped normal-form reconstruction; source~34's R12 and source~33's
question~12.12 ask for proof-carrying notation. All open: no statement of
Part~XVI is formalized (\cref{swo:sec:formal}). This report's earlier
formalization plans for the class orders are in \cref{swo:ix:sec:lean} and
\cref{swo:b83:sec:foundations}.

\begin{question}[Source~34, R1: kernel-check the $\GB$ refinement]\label{swo:bo:R1}

% ---- source 34 (batch-96 manuscript 10), lines 2097-2102
Formalize \Cref{swo:bo:power:GB} and the canonical-history
equivalence in a two-sorted encoding that records comprehension
instances. The key deliverable is an axiom audit showing that no
Choice or $\ETR$ axiom entered either proof. A full-model ordinal
calculation alone would not meet this objective.

\end{question}

% ---- source 35 (batch-96 manuscript 11), lines 2739-2768
\paragraph{Verify the choice-free core first}

\begin{question}[Source~35, Question~10.1: Formalize the finite-support minimization theorem]\label{swo:fc:n10.1}
Can the greedy proof of \cref{swo:fc:thm:finite-support} be formalized in a
two-sorted theory whose set axioms are precisely ZF, with all uses of
class comprehension and Replacement recorded?
\end{question}

This is the most immediate verification target.  A successful
formalization should use the original subclass of candidate polynomials
and a finite prefix as parameters, rather than postulating a sequence
of newly formed tail classes.  Its termination argument should explicitly
construct the uniquely specified sequence of exponent labels in the
nonterminating case.  Checking this point also provides a reusable
pattern for other finite-support functors.

\begin{question}[Source~35, Question~10.2: Verify the complete normal-form argument]\label{swo:fc:n10.2}
Can one give a machine-checked proof of the $\GB$ fixed-schedule
criterion, including the capped reconstruction establishing that
the polynomial image is an \emph{initial} subclass?
\end{question}

An ordinary order embedding would not suffice for the equivalence
with strong comparability.  The finite reconstruction with a retained
upper cap is the most important part to preserve.  A formal library
should then separate the choice-free result for arbitrary carriers
from the Global-Choice-dependent reduction to the whole surreal
carrier.  The inspected repository has not already supplied a
machine verification of this later manuscript development.

% ---- source 32 (batch-96 manuscript 08), lines 853-857
\begin{question}[Source~32, Question~12.11: A verified presentation library]\label{swo:dc:n12.11}
Can the weak presentation theorems, the ETR-dependent existence theorem, and the external spectrum theorems be formalized in one library without identifying their notions of well-foundedness or smallness?
\end{question}
A successful implementation should expose a theorem's class-admissibility assumptions in its type, and should make it impossible to import an external well-foundedness proof into an arbitrary internal model without an explicit absoluteness bridge. This is a substantive design constraint, not merely a namespace convention.

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1755-1762
\begin{question}[Source~33, Research question~12.13: Formal reverse mathematics]\label{swo:dh:n12.13}
Implement the two-sorted class-model interface and verify the distinction
between the $\GBC$ theorems and the ETR-dependent existence theorems.
A particularly focused first milestone is a complete formal proof of the
uniform-family diagonal, followed by a bounded-satisfaction compiler for
one fixed complexity level.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Source~34, R12: a proof-carrying notation interface]\label{swo:bo:R12}

% ---- source 34 (batch-96 manuscript 10), lines 2184-2188
Design a syntax whose constructors carry certificates of class
well-ordering and whose conversions carry explicit initial
embeddings. The goal is an extensible and checkable family,
not a final catalog. The uniform diagonal theorem proves that
the latter goal is too strong.

\end{question}

% ---- source 33 (batch-96 manuscript 09), lines 1747-1754
